title: Getting Started: Accounts, Navigation and Support
content:
# Getting Started: Accounts, Navigation and Support
This section explains how to create an account, log in, recover a forgotten password, find your way around the application, use the Dashboard and Global Search, contact the support team, and read the legal and data-deletion pages. Everything here applies to every workspace member regardless of plan, unless a role restriction is stated.

## Key Concepts

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Workspace (also called "tenant") | Your company's private space in Omni Platform. All your channels, contacts, conversations, flows and campaigns live inside it. Data is completely separated from other companies. |
| Owner | The person who created the workspace. Each workspace has at least one owner. |
| Admin, Agent, Viewer | The other three roles a workspace member can have (see "Roles and What They Can Do" below). |
| Tenant ID | A long unique code that identifies your workspace. The application shows only the first 8 characters; you can copy the full value from the profile menu (see "Profile Menu"). |
| Toast | A small coloured message that appears briefly at the bottom-right corner of the screen to confirm an action or report an error. |

## Roles and What They Can Do

Your role is shown as a coloured badge in the sidebar and in the top bar. Roles are assigned by an Owner or Admin in **Settings & Scale > Team**.

| Role | Badge colour | Summary of what the role is meant for |
|---|---|---|
| Owner | Purple | Full control of the workspace, including promoting other members to Owner. |
| Admin | Blue | Manages channels, flows, campaigns, team members, API keys, billing and audit information. |
| Agent | Green | Works customer conversations in the Team Inbox (reply, assign, change status). Cannot change workspace configuration. |
| Viewer | Grey | Read-only. Can look at information but cannot work conversations or change configuration. |

What is confirmed in the product:

- Only **Owner** and **Admin** can invite members, change roles, deactivate members, remove members, create or revoke API keys, manage channels, flows, campaigns, billing and audit information.
- Only **Owner** can promote another member to the Owner role.
- Conversation actions in the Team Inbox (reply, assign, close and similar) require **Owner**, **Admin** or **Agent**. A Viewer can only look.
- Every role can use the Dashboard, Global Search, the Documentation page and the Support & Helpdesk page, and can open and reply to support tickets.
- The left sidebar shows the same menu items to every role. If a menu item opens a page where you cannot perform an action, the system will show an error message when you try (for example, a message saying you do not have permission). This is expected for Agents and Viewers.

> **Good to know:** the in-app guide lists a role matrix (Owner / Admin / Agent / Viewer against Inbox, Flow Builder, Campaigns, Billing & Settings). Treat the list above as the authoritative summary of what is enforced; the detailed permissions of each feature are described in the section for that feature.

title: Creating an Account (Sign Up)
content:
# Creating an Account (Sign Up)
## What it is for

Signing up creates a brand-new **workspace** and your personal login at the same time. You automatically become the **Owner** of that workspace. Other people join later when an Owner or Admin adds them from the Team settings; they do not use the Sign Up page.

## How to get there

- Open the application address in your browser; if you are not logged in you are taken to the login page.
- Click **Sign up for free** under the Log In button, or open the `/signup` address directly.
- If you are already logged in, the Sign Up page is not available: you are sent straight to the Dashboard.

## Screen layout

On a computer, the left half is a blue marketing panel listing platform benefits; the right half is the form. On a phone or narrow window only the form is shown.

## Fields and controls

| Field / control | Required | What to enter | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| Company Name | Yes | The name of your business, for example "Acme Inc." Helper text: "This will be your unique tenant identifier". | Cannot be empty or only spaces. Error: "Company name is required". |
| Email Address | Yes | Your work email. This becomes your login name. | Must look like an email (text, an @ sign, a domain with a dot). Errors: "Email is required" or "Invalid email format". The email must not already be registered (see Common problems). |
| Password | Yes | A password of your choice. Helper text: "Minimum 8 characters". | At least 8 characters. Errors: "Password is required" or "Password must be at least 8 characters". |
| Confirm Password | Yes | Type the same password again. | Must match exactly. Error: "Passwords do not match". |
| Terms checkbox | Yes | "By signing up, you agree to our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy." The two names are links that open the legal pages. | The **Create Account** button stays disabled (greyed out) until this box is ticked. |
| Create Account button | - | Submits the form. | Shows a spinner while working. |
| Log in link | - | "Already have an account? Log in". | Takes you to the login page. |
| Footer links | - | Documentation, Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, Data Deletion. | These pages can be opened without logging in. |

## Step by step

1. Open the Sign Up page.
2. Type your **Company Name**.
3. Type your **Email Address**.
4. Type a **Password** of at least 8 characters, then type it again in **Confirm Password**.
5. Tick the checkbox to accept the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. You may click the links first to read them (they open in the same window; use the browser Back button to return, your typed values will be lost, so read them before filling in the form if you prefer).
6. Click **Create Account**.
7. On success a green message "Account created successfully! Welcome to Omni Platform" appears and you land on the Dashboard, already logged in as the Owner.

## Validation rules and limits

- All checks on the page run when you click **Create Account**; error messages appear in red under the relevant field. Fix every highlighted field and click again.
- The server also requires company name, email and password to be present.
- Passwords are stored in a protected (hashed) form; nobody, including support staff, can read your password.

## Common problems

| Message | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| "An account with this email already exists" | The email (not case sensitive) is already registered, either as a workspace Owner or as a team member in any workspace. | Log in instead, or use **Forgot password?** if you cannot remember the password. Use a different email if you want a separate workspace. |
| "Signup failed" | An unexpected server problem. | Wait a minute and try again; if it persists open a ticket from another account or contact your administrator. |
| Create Account button is grey | The terms checkbox is not ticked, or a request is in progress. | Tick the checkbox / wait for the spinner to finish. |

> **Good to know:** an email address can belong to only one account on the platform, so the same person cannot be a member of two workspaces using the same email.

title: Logging In and Out
content:
# Logging In and Out
## What it is for

Logging in identifies you and opens your workspace. Your session is remembered by your browser so you do not need to log in again every time you open the application.

## How to get there

Open the application address. If you are not logged in, every page redirects to the login page (`/login`).

## Fields and controls

| Field / control | What it does |
|---|---|
| Email Address | Your account email. Must look like an email address. |
| Password | Your password. It is shown as dots. |
| Remember me (checkbox) | Displayed on the form. Notes: in the current version this checkbox has no visible effect; you stay logged in for the lifetime of the session either way. |
| Forgot password? | Opens the password recovery page (see "Resetting a Forgotten Password"). |
| Log In button | Submits the form. |
| Sign up for free | Opens the Sign Up page. |
| Footer links | Documentation, Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, Data Deletion. They work without logging in. |

The right half of the screen (computers only) summarises the platform: unified team inbox, no-code flow builder, tenant isolation and role-based access.

## Step by step: log in

1. Open the login page.
2. Enter your email and password.
3. Click **Log In**.
4. A green message "Welcome back! Logged in successfully" appears and the Dashboard opens.

## Validation and messages

| Message | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| "Email is required" / "Invalid email format" / "Password is required" | The form was submitted with missing or badly formatted data. | Correct the field shown in red. |
| "Invalid email or password" | No account matches that combination. The same message is used whether the email or the password is wrong. | Check typing and Caps Lock; use **Forgot password?** if needed. |
| "Account has been deactivated. Please contact your workspace administrator." | An Owner or Admin switched your account to deactivated. | Ask an Owner or Admin of your workspace to reactivate you. You cannot do this yourself. |
| "Login failed" | Unexpected server problem. | Try again shortly. |

## How long you stay logged in

- A login session lasts 7 days by default (this can be configured by the platform operator).
- Reloading the page or closing and reopening the browser tab keeps you logged in, as long as the session has not expired and you did not log out.
- If at any time the system tells your browser that your session is no longer valid (expired session, your password was reset, or your account was removed), you are logged out automatically and sent to the login page.
- If an Owner or Admin deactivates your account while you are working, your next action will fail with a deactivation message.
- Resetting your password logs you out on all other devices (see below).

## Logging out

Use either of these:

1. The **Log out** icon (arrow leaving a door) at the bottom of the left sidebar, next to your name.
2. Open the profile menu in the top bar and click **Sign Out** (it carries the hint "End session").

When you log out the live connection is closed and you return to the login page. Notification history and your sound/desktop preferences remain stored in this browser (see "Notifications").

> **Good to know:** the platform has no two-factor authentication screen and no account lock-out screen in the tenant application.

title: Resetting a Forgotten Password
content:
# Resetting a Forgotten Password
## What it is for

If you cannot log in because you forgot your password, you can request a one-time link by email and choose a new password.

## Part 1: Requesting the link (page "Forgot Password?")

How to get there: click **Forgot password?** on the login page, or open `/forgot-password`.

| Field / control | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Email Address | The email you log in with. The cursor is placed here automatically. |
| Send Reset Link | Sends the email. |
| Back to login | Returns to the login page. |

Steps:

1. Enter your account email.
2. Click **Send Reset Link**.
3. The page changes to "Check your inbox". It says: "If an account exists for this email, we've sent a password reset link." It shows the address it was sent to and the reminder that **the link expires in 30 minutes** and that you should check your spam folder.
4. Open the email and click the link (see Part 2).

After sending:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| Resend link / "Resend link in 60s" | You must wait 60 seconds after each send before the button becomes active. Clicking it sends a fresh link and shows "Reset link sent again". |
| Use a different email | Takes you back to the form so you can enter another address. |

Important behaviours:

- For privacy the system gives the same "If an account exists..." reply whether or not the email is registered. If you receive no email, the address may be mistyped or not registered.
- Limits: from one network address you can request at most **5** links per 15 minutes, and for one email address at most **3** links per 15 minutes. Beyond that you see "Too many requests. Please try again later." Wait 15 minutes and try again.
- A deactivated account cannot reset its password: you will see "Your account is deactivated. Please contact your workspace administrator." under the email field.
- Only the newest link should be used; older links may no longer work.

## Part 2: Choosing a new password (page "Reset Password")

How to get there: click the button/link in the email. The address contains a long code (token) after `?token=`. Do not edit it.

The page first shows "Checking your reset link..." with a spinner, then one of the following states.

| State | Heading | What you see |
|---|---|---|
| Valid link | "Set a New Password" | The password form. |
| Invalid link | "Link Expired" | "This reset link is invalid, expired or has already been used." plus a note that links expire after 30 minutes and work only once, and a **Request new link** button. A page opened without a token shows the same state. |
| Success | "Password Updated" | A green notice and a **Go to login** button. After about 2.5 seconds you are redirected to login automatically. |

Form fields:

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| New Password | Required, at least 8 characters (helper text "Minimum 8 characters"). Errors: "Password is required", "Password must be at least 8 characters". |
| Confirm New Password | Must equal the new password: "Passwords do not match". |
| Reset Password button | Saves the new password. |

Steps:

1. Click the link in the email.
2. Wait for the form to appear.
3. Enter the new password twice.
4. Click **Reset Password**. You see "Password reset successfully. Please log in with your new password."
5. Log in with the new password.

What changes when you reset a password:

- The old password stops working immediately.
- You are logged out of every other device and browser where you were logged in ("you've been logged out on other devices").
- The link can be used only once.

Troubleshooting:

| Problem | What to do |
|---|---|
| "This reset link is invalid or has expired" (also appears if the link expires while the form is open) | Click **Request new link** and use the newest email within 30 minutes. |
| Email does not arrive | Check spam/junk, check the address spelling, wait a minute and use **Resend link**. Check you have not hit the request limit. |
| Message "Password must be at least 8 characters" | Use a longer password. |

## Changing your password while logged in

You can change your name and password from **Settings & Scale > Profile** (profile menu > **Profile & Account Details**). You must enter your current password. Note: the server accepts a new password of at least 6 characters here, but we recommend using 8 or more characters for consistency with Sign Up and Reset. The Settings screens are documented in their own section.

title: The Application Layout
content:
# The Application Layout
After logging in, every screen has the same three areas:

1. **Left sidebar**: the main menu, your workspace and account information.
2. **Top bar**: search box, connection status, notifications bell and your profile menu.
3. **Content area**: the page you selected.

On a phone or narrow window the sidebar is hidden to save space. Tap the **menu (three lines)** button at the left of the top bar to open it; tap outside the sidebar or choose a page to close it. On a computer the sidebar is always visible.

The Team Inbox page uses the full width of the screen for more room; all other pages use a centred layout with a maximum width.

## Sidebar

From top to bottom:

| Part | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Brand header | The Omni Platform logo and the words "Multi-Tenant SaaS". |
| Workspace card | "Tenant:" followed by the first 8 characters of your Tenant ID, a green pulsing dot with the word "Active", and your role badge. |
| Menu | The navigation items listed below. The page you are on is highlighted in blue. A small arrow appears on hover. |
| User card | Your initials, your name (or your email if no name is set), and your role. The **Log out** icon is on the right. |
| Legal links | Privacy, Terms and Data Deletion links. |

Menu items, in the order shown:

| Menu item | Opens | Purpose (short) |
|---|---|---|
| Dashboard | `/` | Overview of your workspace (this section). |
| Team Inbox | `/inbox` | Work customer conversations from all channels. |
| Channels | `/channels` | Connect WhatsApp, Telegram, web chat and other channels. |
| Flow Builder | `/flows` | Build automated conversation flows. |
| Contacts | `/contacts` | Your customer directory. |
| Campaigns | `/campaigns` | Broadcast and drip messaging. |
| Deals & CRM | `/deals` | Sales pipeline. |
| Products | `/products` | Product catalogue. |
| Orders | `/orders` | Customer orders. |
| Analytics & Infra | `/analytics` | Reports and system health. |
| AI Knowledge Base | `/knowledge-bases` | Documents used by the AI assistant. |
| Documentation & Guide | `/docs` | The in-app guide. |
| Support & Helpdesk | `/support` | Contact the platform support team (this section). |
| Settings & Scale | `/settings` | Profile, team, API keys, plans and billing. |
| Global Search | `/search` | Search messages and contacts (this section). |

> **Good to know:** these pages are explained in their own sections of this manual. Your Agent or Viewer role may limit what you can do on some of them.

## Top bar

| Control | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Menu button | Phones / narrow windows only | Opens the sidebar. |
| Search box | Hidden on very small screens | Type words and press Enter to open Global Search with your query. |
| Connection badge | Wide screens only | Shows the live connection status (see below). |
| "Tech Provider Active" badge | Medium and wider screens | An information badge showing that the platform is operating as a Meta Technology Provider. It is not clickable and requires no action. |
| Bell | Always | Opens the notifications panel. |
| Profile button | Always | Opens the profile menu. |

### Connection badge (live gateway)

The platform delivers new messages and updates to your screen in real time through a live connection.

| Badge | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Green "Live Gateway" with a pulsing dot | Connected. New messages and ticket replies appear instantly. | Nothing. |
| Amber "Connecting..." | The connection is starting or re-establishing. | Wait a few seconds. |
| Red "Offline" | No live connection. Real-time updates, notifications and sounds will not arrive until it recovers. | Check your internet connection and reload the page. If it persists, contact support. |

Hover over the badge to see the raw status word.

### Using the top-bar search

1. Click the search box (placeholder: "Search messages, contacts, conversations...").
2. Type your words.
3. Press **Enter**. Nothing happens if the box is empty or only spaces. The Global Search page opens with results.

## Profile menu

Click your initials/name at the right of the top bar. The panel has these parts:

| Part | Details |
|---|---|
| Header | Your initials, name (or "Workspace User" if not set), email, a "Role: ..." chip and a status chip (normally "active"). |
| Workspace | Your company name. |
| Plan Tier | Your current subscription plan name. If it cannot be loaded it shows "Starter Tier". |
| Tenant ID | Shows the first 8 characters. Click it to copy the **full** Tenant ID to the clipboard; the button shows "Copied" and a blue message "Tenant ID copied to clipboard" appears. Support staff may ask you for this value. |
| Profile & Account Details | Opens Settings on the Profile tab. |
| Workspace Settings & RBAC | Opens Settings on the Team tab (members and roles). |
| Developer API Keys | Opens Settings on the API Keys tab. |
| User Manual & Docs | Opens the in-app documentation. |
| Sign Out | Logs you out. |

Close the profile menu by clicking anywhere else or pressing **Esc**. The same applies to the notifications panel.

> **Good to know:** your name appears only after you set it in the Profile settings; until then your email (the part before @) is displayed.

title: Notifications
content:
# Notifications
## What it is for

The bell icon alerts you to things that need attention while you are using the application, so you do not miss customer messages.

## What creates a notification

| Event | Notification title | Text | Where clicking takes you |
|---|---|---|---|
| A customer sends you a message | New Customer Message | A preview of the text, or "Sent an attachment (type)" for media, or "New incoming message" | That conversation in the Team Inbox |
| A conversation is assigned to **you** | Conversation Assigned | "You have been assigned a new customer conversation." | That conversation |
| A conversation is reopened | Conversation Reopened | "A customer conversation has been reopened." | That conversation |

Messages you or your colleagues send are not notified. Assignments to other people are not shown to you.

## Where notifications are stored (important)

- Notifications are created in your browser while the application is open and connected. If the app is closed or you are offline, you will not receive them, and they will not appear later.
- They are kept in this browser only, separately for each workspace. They are **not** shared with colleagues and do **not** follow you to another computer or browser.
- At most the latest **50** are kept; older ones are discarded automatically.

## The notification panel

Click the **bell**. A red number badge on the bell shows how many are unread (it shows "9+" above nine). A header chip shows "N new".

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| Speaker icon | Switches the alert sound on or off. Tooltip shows "Alert sounds: ON/OFF". When on, a short two-tone chime plays for each new notification. Default is on. |
| Bell-with-waves icon | Desktop (pop-up) notifications. If the browser has not yet allowed notifications it asks for permission; once allowed it toggles desktop alerts on or off. Tooltip shows the current state. |
| Double-tick icon | "Mark all as read". Only visible while there are unread items. |
| Blue banner "Enable desktop alerts for incoming messages" with **Enable** button | Shown only until you answer the browser's permission question. Click **Enable**, then choose Allow in the browser prompt. |
| Tabs **All (n)** and **Unread (n)** | Filter the list. |
| A notification row | Unread items have a blue dot, bold title and tinted background. Click a row to mark it as read, close the panel and open the linked conversation. Shows how long ago it arrived (for example "5m ago", "2h ago"). |
| Trash icon on a row | Appears when you hover over a row; deletes that single notification. |
| Clear all | In the footer; removes every notification at once (no confirmation). |
| Footer status | Shows "Live WebSocket Active" when connected, otherwise the connection state. |

Empty states: "No notifications yet" (nothing received) or "No unread notifications - You're all caught up".

## Turning on desktop notifications

1. Open the bell panel.
2. Click **Enable** in the blue banner (or the bell-with-waves icon).
3. Your browser shows a permission question. Choose **Allow**.
4. A green message "Desktop notifications enabled!" appears. From now on a pop-up appears on your desktop for each new notification, even when the browser tab is in the background. Clicking the pop-up brings the tab forward and opens the related conversation.

If you chose Block, a message says "Desktop notifications blocked in browser settings". The application cannot override that: open your browser's site settings for this address and change notifications to Allow, then reload.

> **Good to know:** the sound and desktop preferences are remembered in this browser only. Browsers may refuse to play sound until you have clicked somewhere on the page at least once after loading it.

title: System Messages: Toasts and Confirmation Dialogs
content:
# System Messages: Toasts and Confirmation Dialogs
## Toasts (colour messages)

Short messages appear at the **bottom-right** corner and disappear by themselves after about 4 seconds. Click the **X** to dismiss one sooner.

| Colour / icon | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Green with tick | The action succeeded (for example "Reply sent to support team"). |
| Red with exclamation | The action failed. The text usually explains why. Read it and correct the problem, then try again. |
| Blue with "i" | Information (for example "Tenant ID copied to clipboard"). |

Several toasts can stack up. If an error flashes by too quickly, repeat the action and read it carefully, or take a screenshot to give to support.

## Confirmation and notice dialogs

Before risky actions (such as deleting something) the application shows a centred window over a dimmed background.

- A **confirm dialog** has two buttons: the action button (the coloured one, which is focused so pressing Enter confirms it) and **Cancel**. Red dialogs warn about destructive actions, amber ones are warnings, blue ones are information, green ones success.
- A **notice dialog** has one button (usually **OK**) and just informs you.
- Click the **X** in the corner or click outside the window to cancel (for a confirm dialog this counts as "No").

Always read the message before confirming; some actions cannot be undone.

title: The Dashboard
content:
# The Dashboard
## What it is for

The Dashboard ("Overview Dashboard") is the first page after login. It gives a quick, at-a-glance summary of your channels, conversations, contacts, sales pipeline and campaigns, with shortcuts to the most common tasks.

## How to get there

Click **Dashboard** in the sidebar, or open the root address `/`. It is shown automatically after logging in. While data loads a spinner is shown.

## Header buttons

| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| Connect Channel | Opens the Channels page, where you connect WhatsApp, Telegram, web chat and others. |
| New Campaign | Opens the "new campaign" page to create a broadcast or drip campaign. |

## Summary cards

| Card | Large number | Small text under it |
|---|---|---|
| Channels | Total number of connected channels. | "N Active": how many have the status *active*. Channels that are not active (for example disconnected or with a problem) are counted in the total but not in the active number. |
| Open Chats | Number of conversations whose status is *open*. | "N Total Conversations": the total number of conversations loaded. |
| Contacts | Number of contacts loaded. | "Audience Directory". Notes: this card counts only the first batch of contacts the dashboard loads (up to 10), so it is a quick indicator, not your total. Use the Contacts page for the real total. |
| Deals Pipeline | Combined value of all deals across all stages, shown with a "$" sign. | "Across all CRM stages". |

## WhatsApp Embedded Signup capacity banner

A dark banner appears only when the platform can report your onboarding capacity. It reads "WhatsApp Embedded Signup Capacity: N remaining" and explains how many of your client-onboarding slots you have used within the rolling window (for example "You have used 3 of 10 client onboarding slots in the rolling 30-day window"). A progress bar shows the used share. The **Manage WhatsApp WABAs** button opens the Channels page. If the banner is missing, it simply means the information could not be loaded; it is not an error you need to fix.

## Recent Conversations

Shows the **latest five** conversations. Each row shows:

- Contact initials in a grey square, the contact's name (or their external ID, or "Unknown Contact").
- A channel badge (green for WhatsApp, blue for others).
- A one-line preview of the last message ("No message preview" if none).
- How long ago it happened ("Just now", "12m ago", "3h ago", "2d ago", or a date after a week).
- A status badge: green for *open*, grey for other statuses (for example closed).

Click a row to open that conversation in the Team Inbox. **View Inbox** opens the full inbox. With no conversations you see "No conversations yet. Inbound webhooks will appear here."

## Deals Pipeline Breakdown

One bar per pipeline stage showing "stage name (N deals)", the stage value and a bar proportional to its share of the total (stages with a very small share still show a minimum bar so they remain visible). The **Kanban Board** link opens the Deals page. Empty message: "No deals in the pipeline yet."

> **Good to know:** deal values are stored in the smallest currency unit and the dashboard divides by 100 and displays them with a dollar sign; the Dashboard does not convert between currencies.

## Recent Campaigns

Shows up to **three** campaigns as cards:

- A type badge: purple for **broadcast**, blue for other types (for example drip).
- A status badge: green when *completed*, amber (yellow) for any other status (draft, scheduled, running and so on).
- The campaign name.
- For a broadcast, the first 50 characters of the message text; for a drip sequence, the number of steps.

**All Campaigns** opens the campaigns list. With none you see a hint to click **New Campaign**.

## Things to know

- The Dashboard loads each block independently. If one block cannot be loaded (for example a temporary error), that block is shown as empty or zero while the others still work. If numbers look wrong, reload the page.
- It does not refresh by itself on a timer; reload the page or navigate away and back to update the figures.
- Every role can open the Dashboard.

title: Global Search
content:
# Global Search
## What it is for

Global Search finds **message text** and **contacts** across all your channels in one place, so you can quickly locate an old conversation or a customer.

## How to get there

- Click **Global Search** in the sidebar, or
- Type in the search box of the top bar and press **Enter** (the search opens already filled in).

The address looks like `/search?q=your words`; you can bookmark or share it with colleagues in your workspace.

## Screen elements

| Element | What it does |
|---|---|
| Search input | Placeholder "Search by keywords, messages, phone number, or contact name...". The cursor is placed here automatically. |
| Search button | Runs the search. It shows a spinner while working. |
| Tabs: All Results (n) / Messages (n) / Contacts (n) | Appear after a search. They filter what is displayed and show the counts. |
| "Showing results for ..." | Reminds you which words are being displayed. |
| Matching Messages | Result cards for messages. |
| Matching Contacts | Result cards for contacts. |

## Message result cards

Each card shows:

- A direction badge: **inbound** (message from the customer, blue) or **outbound** (message sent from your side, purple).
- The conversation reference ("ID: ..."), which is an internal conversation code.
- The date and time of the message.
- The message text.
- **Open in Inbox**: opens that conversation in the Team Inbox.

## Contact result cards

Each card shows:

- The contact's initials, name ("Unnamed" if there is none) and phone number or external ID.
- A channel badge: green for WhatsApp; for web chat the badge also shows the name of the web chat channel ("webchat · name"); other channels are shown by name.
- **View Contact**: opens the Contacts page (it does not jump to that single contact; use the Contacts page search there to find them).

## Step by step

1. Open Global Search.
2. Type one or more words, a phone number or a contact name.
3. Press **Enter** or click **Search**.
4. Read the results. Click a tab to see only messages or only contacts.
5. Click **Open in Inbox** to continue a conversation, or **View Contact** to see the contact.

## Rules and limits

- The search text is required; an empty search shows the prompt "Enter a query above to start searching messages and customer contacts." (Pressing Enter with an empty box does nothing.)
- The search text can be at most **200 characters**.
- By default up to **20 messages** and up to **20 contacts** are returned, so very broad searches will not list everything. Use more specific words to narrow down.
- Only messages that contain **text** are searchable. Pictures, documents and audio without text cannot be found by their content.
- You only ever see results from your own workspace.
- New messages are added to the search index in the background and may take a moment to become searchable.
- Every role can use Global Search.

## Messages you may see

| What you see | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| "No matching results found" | Nothing in messages or contacts matches. | Try different or fewer words; check spelling or the phone number format. |
| "No matching messages" / "No matching contacts" | The currently selected tab is empty but the other tab may have results. | Click the other tab or All Results. |
| "Search is unavailable right now. We couldn't reach the search service." plus a red message "Search failed or Elasticsearch unavailable" | The search service is temporarily unreachable (or the text was too long). | Click **Try again** after a moment. If it keeps failing, open a support ticket. |

---

title: Support & Helpdesk (Support Tickets)
content:
# Support & Helpdesk (Support Tickets)
## What it is for

This page lets you contact the Omni Platform support team directly from the application. You open a **ticket** (a case) describing a problem or question, the support team replies, and the whole conversation is kept in one place. It is the right place for bugs, outages, billing questions, channel connection problems, AI/knowledge-base issues and compliance requests. It is not for talking to your own customers (that is the Team Inbox).

## How to get there

- Click **Support & Helpdesk** in the sidebar (`/support`), or
- Click **Get Support** or **Open Support Ticket** buttons on the Documentation page.

Every workspace member can open this page, create tickets and reply. Tickets belong to the **workspace**: everyone in your workspace sees the same list of tickets, including those opened by colleagues.

## Page layout

1. Header with **Refresh** and **Open New Ticket** buttons.
2. Four summary cards.
3. The ticket list with status filters and a search box.
4. When you click a ticket, its conversation opens in a panel on the right (below the list on small screens).

## Header buttons

| Button | What it does |
|---|---|
| Refresh | Reloads the list (and the open ticket). The icon spins while loading. |
| Open New Ticket | Opens the "Open Support Ticket" form. |

## Summary cards

The cards count the tickets **currently shown in the list** (so they change when you filter).

| Card | What is counted |
|---|---|
| Total Cases | All tickets in the list. |
| Active / In Progress | Tickets with status Open or In Progress. |
| Pending Your Action | Tickets with status "Pending You" (waiting for your reply). |
| Resolved / Closed | Tickets with status Resolved or Closed. |

## Ticket statuses

| Status shown | Colour | Meaning | What you should do |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open | Blue | New ticket, not yet picked up. | Wait for a reply; you can add more information. |
| In Progress | Amber | The support team is working on it (a staff reply moves an Open ticket to In Progress). | Wait, and answer any questions. |
| Pending You | Purple | The support team is waiting for information from you. | Reply with the requested details. |
| Resolved | Green | Support believes the problem is solved. | If it is solved, no action. If not, reply: **your reply automatically reopens the ticket** (status becomes Open). |
| Closed | Grey | The ticket is finished. | You can no longer reply. Open a new ticket if you need more help. |

The status is changed by the support staff (and by your own replies as described); you cannot change a ticket's status yourself.

## Priority levels

| Priority | How it appears | Intended use |
|---|---|---|
| Low | Plain grey label "Low" | General query. |
| Medium | Blue label "Medium" | Standard issue (default). |
| High | Amber label "High" | Issue impacting your operations. |
| Urgent | Red label "URGENT" | Critical outage. |

Please choose honestly; urgent tickets are sorted first by the support team.

## Categories

| Category in the form | Use it for |
|---|---|
| General Inquiry | Anything that does not fit elsewhere (default). |
| Billing & Subscription | Invoices, plan changes, payments. |
| Channel Integration | Connecting WhatsApp, Telegram, web chat; webhook and message delivery problems. |
| AI & Knowledge Base | AI assistant answers, document uploads. |
| Technical Bug / Outage | Something is broken or unavailable. |
| GDPR & Compliance | Data protection and compliance requests. |

## Finding tickets (filters and search)

| Control | How it works |
|---|---|
| Status buttons: **All**, **Open**, **In Progress**, **Pending Customer**, **Resolved** | Click one to show only tickets in that status. The list reloads immediately. Notes: there is no button for "Closed" tickets; closed tickets appear only under **All**. Pending Customer is the same as the purple "Pending You" status. |
| Search box ("Search ticket # or subject...") | Type part of the ticket number (for example "1042") or a word from the subject, then press **Enter**. It is not case sensitive and matches any part of the text. It combines with the selected status button. Clear the box and press Enter to show everything again. |

If nothing matches you see "No tickets found" with the hint "No tickets matched your current search and filter criteria." If you have never created a ticket the text says "You don't have any support tickets yet", with a **Create Ticket** button.

## The ticket list

Each ticket card shows:

- The **ticket number** (for example `TICK-1042`) in a highlighted tag, and the category.
- Priority and status labels on the right.
- The subject (one line).
- "Opened ..." with how long ago it was created.
- The number of messages in the conversation ("3 msgs").

Click a card to open it; the selected card is outlined in blue. The list shows newest tickets first.

## Opening a new ticket

1. Click **Open New Ticket** (or **Create Ticket** when the list is empty).
2. In the "Open Support Ticket" window fill in the form:

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Ticket Subject | Yes | A short title, for example "WhatsApp channel webhook synchronization failing". |
| Category | No (default General Inquiry) | See the category table. |
| Urgency / Priority | No (default Medium) | Low - General query; Medium - Standard issue; High - Impacting operations; Urgent - Critical outage. |
| Detailed Description & Steps to Reproduce | Yes | Describe the problem in detail. Include error messages, IDs, times and what you expected. |

3. Click **Submit Ticket** (or **Cancel** to close without saving; the typed text is kept until you reload the page).
4. A green message "Support ticket TICK-xxxx created successfully!" appears, the window closes, the new ticket is selected and opens on the right.
5. A confirmation email is sent to your account email address.

Validation: Subject and description cannot be empty or only spaces. If you try, the message "Subject and message are required" appears. Leading/trailing spaces are removed.

Tips for a good ticket:

- State what you were doing, what happened and what you expected.
- Copy the exact error message that appeared (red toast or dialog).
- Include the channel name or phone number, the contact or conversation involved, and the time it happened.
- Give your Tenant ID if asked (copy it from the profile menu).
- Do not include passwords, full card numbers or secret keys in a ticket.

## Reading and replying to a ticket

When you open a ticket, the right panel shows:

- Header: ticket number, status, priority, category and the subject.
- The conversation, oldest message first. Your side (and your colleagues') is shown on the right in grey with the sender's name. Replies from the support team are shown on the left in blue with a shield icon, the staff member's name (or "Support Engineer") and the label "Official Staff".
- A reply box at the bottom.

To reply:

1. Type your message in "Write a reply to the support team...".
2. Click **Send Reply**. The button is disabled while the box is empty.
3. Your message appears in the conversation and the message "Reply sent to support team" is shown. The support team is notified immediately.

Replies from support appear on their own, in real time, while the page is open, and you also receive an email for each support reply and when a ticket is marked resolved. Statuses, priority, category and assignment changes made by support are also updated live.

If the ticket is **Closed**, the reply box is replaced by "This ticket is closed. Open a new case if you need further assistance."

> **Good to know:**
>
> - You cannot attach files from this screen; describe the problem in text (paste error text rather than screenshots).
> - Internal notes written by support staff are never shown to you.
> - Tickets cannot be deleted by customers.

## Common problems

| Problem | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Failed to load support tickets" or "Failed to load ticket details" | Click **Refresh**; check the connection badge in the top bar; try again later. |
| "Failed to create support ticket" | Check the subject and description are filled in, then retry. Keep your text safe (copy it) before retrying. |
| "Failed to post reply" | Retry. If the ticket has just been closed, open a new ticket. |
| You do not see a colleague's ticket | Use **All** status and clear the search box; tickets of your whole workspace are shown. |
| No reply for a long time | The page says "We typically respond within 15 minutes", and the page states the support team is available 24/7. These are targets, not guarantees. If it is urgent, add a reply explaining the urgency (you cannot change the priority of an existing ticket yourself) or open a new ticket with priority Urgent. |

---

title: The In-App Documentation (User Manual)
content:
# The In-App Documentation (User Manual)
## What it is for

The Documentation page is a searchable guide built into the application. It is available both inside the application (**Documentation & Guide** in the sidebar, or **User Manual & Docs** in the profile menu) and **without logging in** at `/docs` (also `/documentation`, `/guide`, `/manual`). When you are not logged in, a top bar with **Log In** and **Start Free Trial** buttons is shown.

## Page elements

| Element | What it does |
|---|---|
| Search box | Type words (for example "WhatsApp setup", "Flow builder", "webhooks", "RAG"). The chapters list filters as you type. A **Clear** button resets it. |
| Print / PDF button | Opens the browser's print window; choose "Save as PDF" as the printer to make a PDF copy. |
| Get Support (logged-in only) | Opens Support & Helpdesk. |
| Category pills | All Guides, Quickstart & Architecture, Channels & WhatsApp, Team Inbox & Routing, AI Copilot & RAG, Visual Flow Builder, Campaigns & Broadcasts, CRM Deals & Catalog, Billing & Quotas, Privacy & Security, APIs & Webhooks, FAQ & Troubleshooting. Click one to show only that chapter. |
| Table of Contents (computers) | Left side list of chapters with a count. Click to scroll to the chapter; the current chapter is highlighted as you scroll. |
| "Need Live Assistance?" card | Button **Open Support Ticket**. |

## Chapters

1. Getting Started & Architecture, including a 5-step launch checklist and the roles table.
2. Channels & Messaging Gateways (WhatsApp Embedded Signup and manual setup, Telegram, web chat widget with website embed instructions).
3. Omnichannel Team Inbox & Routing (conversation lifecycle).
4. AI Copilot, RAG & Knowledge Bases.
5. Visual Flow Builder & Automations.
6. Campaigns & WhatsApp Templates.
7. Deals CRM, Catalog & Orders.
8. Billing, Plans & Resource Quotas.
9. Data Privacy & Zero-PII Shield.
10. Developer REST APIs & Webhooks.
11. FAQ & Troubleshooting (eight common questions that expand when clicked).

## The 5-minute launch checklist

Chapter 1 contains an interactive checklist for new workspaces. Click a step to tick it (it turns green and gets a progress percentage). When logged in, **Go** takes you directly to the relevant page.

| Step | What to do | Page |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Configure workspace profile and timezone | Settings > Profile |
| 2 | Connect your WhatsApp channel (1-click Embedded Signup or manual) | Channels |
| 3 | Upload company FAQs to the AI Knowledge Base | AI Knowledge Base |
| 4 | Build or activate a welcome flow | Flow Builder |
| 5 | Invite support agents and assign roles | Settings > Team |

> **Good to know:** ticked steps are only a visual aid kept on the page while it is open; they are not saved and do not change any setting.

## Frequently asked questions (from the in-app guide)

| Question | Short answer |
|---|---|
| Messages show "Failed" or are not delivered | WhatsApp requires an approved template for business-initiated messages outside the 24-hour customer window; also check that the access token is valid, the phone number ID matches, and the Meta payment method is active. |
| Raising the WhatsApp daily limit | Meta upgrades tiers automatically when you send at least half of your current limit to unique people within 7 days while keeping a high quality rating. |
| Can platform staff see my customer conversations? | The guide states no: platform operators see only workspace metadata (name, plan, usage and error rates), not message contents. |
| Testing billing without a card | Settings > Usage & Plans > choose a plan > "Instant Sandbox". |
| Question not covered by the AI Knowledge Base | If the answer's confidence is below the configured threshold (default 0.70) the AI says it does not know and hands the conversation to a human (status "Unassigned"). |
| Are internal notes visible to customers? | No. |
| Downloading invoices | Settings & Scale > Invoices & Billing History > View Receipt > Print / Download PDF. |
| Restricting where the web chat widget can appear | Enter allowed domains in the web chat channel settings. |

> **Good to know:** those answers are quoted from the in-app guide; the corresponding screens are covered in their own sections of this manual.

title: Legal Pages: Privacy Policy, Terms of Service and Data Deletion
content:
# Legal Pages: Privacy Policy, Terms of Service and Data Deletion
These three pages are public (no login needed), share the same layout (a "Legal & Trust Center" header with links between the pages plus **Log In** and sign-up buttons), and are linked from the login page, sign-up page and the bottom of the sidebar. Each page shows a "last updated" date (currently September 3, 2026).

| Page | Address(es) | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| Privacy Policy | `/privacy` or `/privacy-policy` | 10 numbered sections: introduction; information collected; how WhatsApp Cloud API data is handled; how information is used; sub-processors; security and tenant isolation; retention and deletion schedules; your privacy rights (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, opt-out under GDPR/CCPA); data deletion requests; and contact details. |
| Terms of Service | `/terms` or `/terms-of-service` | 12 sections: agreement; description of the service; account registration and security; WhatsApp compliance; acceptable use; Meta Cloud API terms; data ownership; fees and billing; service-level disclaimer; limitation of liability; termination; governing law. |
| Data Deletion | `/data-deletion` or `/data-deletion-instructions` | How to remove the app from your Facebook/Meta account and a deletion request form with a status check (see below). |

Points worth knowing from the Privacy Policy:

- Active account data is kept while your subscription is active.
- Message transcripts and logs are kept up to 90 days after delivery, or as configured in the client's data retention settings.
- After an account is closed, all workspace data, contacts and tokens are permanently removed within 30 days.
- Privacy contacts: Data Protection Officer `dpo@omni-platform.com`, general privacy `privacy@omni-platform.com`. Formal privacy and deletion requests are answered within 48 business hours.

> **Good to know:** this manual only summarises these documents; they are legal texts and the pages themselves are authoritative.

## Requesting data deletion

The Data Deletion page offers three parts.

**Part 1: Remove the app from Facebook / Meta.** If you connected a WhatsApp Business Account or Facebook login, you can revoke access yourself:

1. Log in to Facebook, click your profile picture and choose **Settings & Privacy > Settings**.
2. In the left menu click **Apps and Websites**.
3. Find **Omni Platform** (or the connected WhatsApp Tech Provider app).
4. Click **Remove**, tick the option to delete the related data, and confirm. Meta then notifies Omni Platform automatically so that it can remove the associated data.

**Part 2: Submit a deletion request.**

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Account Email Address | One of the first two | The primary email used on Omni Platform. |
| Phone Number or Meta User ID | One of the first two | The WhatsApp phone number or Facebook user ID. |
| Tenant / Organization Name | No | Your company name, optional. |
| Scope of Deletion | Yes (default: all) | Complete Account & All Associated Data; WhatsApp Message Transcripts & Media Only; Contact Directory & Segment Tags Only. |
| Reason for Erasure | No | Pre-filled with "Revoked App Authorization / Requested Erasure"; you can edit it. |

Steps:

1. Fill in at least the email **or** the phone number / Meta ID. If both are empty a warning dialog "Identifier Required" asks you to provide one.
2. Choose the scope and optionally edit the reason.
3. Click **Submit Deletion Request & Generate Code**.
4. A green panel "Data Deletion Request Received" shows your **tracking code** in the form `DEL-OMNI-XXXXXX-1234`. Click **Copy Code** and keep it. **Submit Another Request** returns to the blank form.

**Part 3: Check status.** Enter the tracking code (for example `DEL-OMNI-ABC123-4567`) and click **Check Status**. The result shows the code, a status label (completed, processing or pending), the scope, the request time and, when finished, the completion time with an explanation. A code that is not recognised shows "No active or historical data deletion request found for this tracking code."

IMPORTANT NOTES (accuracy):

- In the current version the on-page request form and the status check work **inside your browser only**: the tracking code is generated on the page and remembered in that browser, and the status shown for codes not created in your browser is a generic sample result. The form does not send your request to the platform's servers. For a request that must be acted upon and be provable (for example for a legal or compliance requirement), **also** email `privacy@omni-platform.com` (manual requests are stated to be processed within 48 hours) or open a **GDPR & Compliance** category ticket under Support & Helpdesk, and keep a copy of the confirmation you receive.
- Removing the app from Facebook (Part 1) triggers a separate automatic process on the platform side and is the recommended method for Meta-connected data.
- To delete your whole workspace or individual contacts from inside the application, use the relevant settings and contact management screens documented elsewhere in this manual; ask your Owner if you are unsure who can perform deletions in your workspace.

title: Quick Troubleshooting Reference for this Section
content:
# Quick Troubleshooting Reference for this Section
| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Redirected to the login page unexpectedly | Session expired (7 days by default), password was reset, or account removed. | Log in again. |
| Cannot sign up: "An account with this email already exists" | Email already registered. | Log in or reset the password. |
| No password-reset email | Wrong address, spam folder, or request limit reached (3 per email / 5 per network per 15 minutes). | Check spam, wait and retry. |

| Red "Offline" badge | No live connection. | Check internet, reload. |

| Dashboard Contacts card shows a small number | The card counts only the first batch of contacts loaded. | Open the Contacts page for the full count. |
| Search says "unavailable" | Search service temporarily unreachable. | Use **Try again**; open a ticket if it continues. |
| Cannot reply to a ticket | Ticket is Closed. | Open a new ticket. |
| Menu item opens but actions fail with a permission message | Your role (Agent or Viewer) does not allow that action. | Ask an Owner or Admin to change your role if you need access. |

title: Team Inbox (Conversations)
content:
# Team Inbox (Conversations)
The Team Inbox is where your team reads and answers customer conversations from every connected channel (WhatsApp, Telegram and website Live Webchat) in one place. This section covers the inbox screen, replying, sending files and WhatsApp templates, assigning and closing cases, bot/AI handoff, message delivery ticks, delivery-failure messages, the WhatsApp 24-hour rule, real-time updates, and the Live Webchat widget that your website visitors use.

## What you can and cannot do in the Inbox (summary)

| You can | Notes |
|---|---|
| Read all conversations of your workspace | Filter by status, channel, owner (Everyone / Mine / Unassigned) and team |
| Reply with text | Plain text, one message at a time |
| Send a file | Image, video, audio, PDF, Office document, text file, ZIP (max 50 MB) |
| Send a WhatsApp template | WhatsApp channels only; needed after the 24-hour window closes |
| Assign a case to an agent or route it to a team | Owner, Admin and Agent roles only |
| Claim an unassigned case | Owner, Admin and Agent roles only |
| Close and reopen a case | Owner, Admin and Agent roles only |
| Hand a conversation back to the bot ("Resume AI Bot") | Owner, Admin and Agent roles only |
| Use AI Copilot (smart replies, summary, rephrase, classify) | Needs AI to be enabled for your workspace (see Notes) |
| See the customer's contact card, deals and orders; add a deal | Right-hand panel |

What the Inbox does **not** have (so you do not look for it): there are no internal notes on conversations, no conversation labels/tags that you can set from the Inbox (tags shown on the contact card come from the Contacts area), no emoji picker, no message editing or deleting, no canned-response library, no typing indicator for visitors in the Inbox, and no server-side message search across old messages (the search box filters the list you already see).

---

title: Opening the Inbox
content:
# Opening the Inbox
1. Sign in to the Omni Platform web app.
2. Choose **Inbox** (Team Inbox) from the left navigation menu.
3. The Inbox opens with your most recent conversations. On a computer, the newest conversation opens automatically. On a phone (screen narrower than about 768 pixels), you see only the list until you tap a conversation.

Opening a specific conversation: each conversation has its own address in the browser (`/inbox?id=...`), so you can bookmark or share a link with a colleague in the same workspace.

---

title: Screen layout
content:
# Screen layout
The Inbox is a three-column screen on a large monitor.

| Area | What it holds |
|---|---|
| **Left column: conversation list** | Title "Inbox (n)", connection badge, refresh button, search box, status buttons, channel menu, owner buttons, team menu, and the list of conversations |
| **Middle column: the open chat** | Chat header, case-action bar (agent, team, claim, close), the message feed, the Smart Reply bar, and the message box |
| **Right column: contact and AI panel** | Two tabs: **CRM & Deals** and **AI Copilot**. Hidden or shown with the person icon in the chat header |

Responsive behaviour:

- **Phone/tablet narrower than 768 px:** list and chat are shown one at a time. Use the left arrow in the chat header ("Back to conversations") or swipe from the very left edge of the screen to the right to go back to the list.
- **Narrower than 1024 px:** the right-hand panel opens as a slide-over drawer from the right when you tap the person icon. Tap the dark background or the X to close it.
- **Wider than 1024 px:** the right-hand panel is a fixed column. It starts hidden on screens narrower than 1440 px and visible on wider screens. Your choice (open or hidden) is remembered in your browser.

---

title: The conversation list (left column)
content:
# The conversation list (left column)
## Header

| Item | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Inbox (n)** | n is the number of conversations returned by the current filters (before the search box is applied) |
| **Live / Reconnecting / Offline badge** | Real-time connection state. **Live** (green) means new messages and changes appear instantly. **Reconnecting** (amber) means the app is trying to reconnect. **Offline** (grey) means the real-time link is down; the list still refreshes by itself every 15 seconds |
| **Refresh icon** | Reloads the conversation list immediately and shows a loading spinner |

## Search box

- Placeholder: "Search chat or phone...".
- It matches, as you type, the contact name, the contact's phone number/ID, and the preview text of the last message.
- Search only looks at conversations already loaded in the list under your current filters. To find an older conversation, set the status filter to **all**, the owner to **everyone** and the team to **All Teams** first.

## Filters

Filters can be combined. Status, owner and team are applied on the server (they change what is loaded); search and channel are applied on your screen.

| Filter | Options | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **Status buttons** | all, open, pending, closed | Show only conversations with that status (see "Conversation statuses" below) |
| **Channel menu** | All Channels, WhatsApp, Telegram, Live Webchat | Show only that channel |
| **Owner buttons** | everyone, mine, unassigned | **mine** = assigned to you; **unassigned** = no agent assigned; **everyone** = no owner filter |
| **Team menu** | All Teams, plus each support team | Shown only if your workspace has created at least one support team. Shows conversations routed to that team |

If nothing matches, the list shows "No conversations found".

## A conversation row

Each row shows:

- A two-letter avatar from the contact's name ("CT" if the name is unknown) with a small channel badge: green **W** for WhatsApp, blue **T** for Telegram, purple speech bubble for Live Webchat.
- The contact name (or phone/ID if there is no name; "Unknown" if neither).
- Time of the last message (for example "5m ago").
- A one-line preview of the last message. Files and templates show placeholders such as `[Image]`, `[Document: file.pdf]` or `[Template: name]`.
- A status badge (see below).
- The channel's display name (for Live Webchat it is highlighted in a purple chip so you can tell apart several website widgets).
- Ownership line: "Agent: <name>" or "Unassigned", followed by " · Team: <name>" if routed to a team.

The conversation you are viewing has a coloured bar on its left edge. The list is sorted by most recent message first, and a conversation jumps to the top when a new message arrives.

## Conversation statuses

| Status shown | Internal status | Meaning | How it gets there |
|---|---|---|---|
| **open** (green) | open | Active case | New conversation; reopened case; a case you claimed or replied to |
| **needs agent** (amber) | pending | A bot flow handed the chat to a human and nobody has picked it up yet | Bot/flow "hand off to agent" step. Filter button is labelled **pending** |
| **closed** (grey) | closed | Resolved | An agent pressed **Close case** |

Status rules the system applies automatically:

- When a human agent replies to a **pending** case, it becomes **open**.
- When an agent claims a **pending** case, it becomes **open**.
- If a customer writes again on a **closed** case, that same case is reopened automatically (the system does not start a second case for the same contact). The previous agent and team stay on it unless that agent is no longer active, in which case the case becomes unassigned.
- Bulk campaign (broadcast) sends do **not** reopen a closed case.

---

title: The open chat (middle column)
content:
# The open chat (middle column)
## Chat header

| Item | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Back arrow** (small screens only) | Return to the list |
| **Avatar and name** | Contact name; if unknown, the phone/ID |
| **Channel badge** | `whatsapp`, `telegram`, or **Live Webchat · <widget name>** |
| **Phone/ID line** | The contact's external ID (phone number for WhatsApp, chat ID for Telegram, visitor session ID for webchat). Shows "No external phone" if empty |
| **Green clock countdown** (WhatsApp only) | Time left in the 24-hour reply window, as HH:MM:SS. See "The WhatsApp 24-hour window" |
| **Green robot icon** | **Resume AI Bot**: hand the conversation back to the bot/flow (see "Bot and AI handoff") |
| **Person icon** | Show or hide the right-hand contact/AI panel. Highlighted blue when the panel is open |

## Case-action bar

A grey bar under the header with the controls for ownership and status.

For **Owner, Admin and Agent** roles:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Agent** drop-down | Assign the case to any active Owner, Admin or Agent of your workspace. Choose **Unassigned** to remove the assignee. The change is saved immediately when you pick a name (no confirm button). Toast: "Conversation assigned" / "Conversation unassigned" |
| **Team** drop-down | Route the case to a support team. Choose **No team** to clear it. Toast: "Routed to team" / "Team cleared" |
| **Claim** button | Appears only when the case has no agent and is not closed. Assigns the case to you, and moves a pending case to open. Toast: "You took this case" |
| **Close case** (green) | Marks the case closed. Toast: "Case closed" |
| **Reopen** | Replaces **Close case** when the case is closed. Sets it back to open. Toast: "Case reopened" |

While one action is running, all the controls in the bar are disabled for a moment.

For **Viewer** role: the bar is read-only and just says "Assigned to <name or nobody> · Team <name>".

> **Good to know:**
>
> - Viewers and deactivated users do not appear in the Agent list and cannot be assigned.
> - Two agents pressing **Claim** at the same moment: one wins, the other sees "This case is already assigned to another agent".
> - You cannot claim a closed case: "This case is closed — reopen it first".
> - Every assignment, team change, claim, close/reopen and bot resume is recorded in the workspace audit log with who did it.

## The message feed

Messages are shown oldest to newest. Messages from the customer are white bubbles on the left; messages your team or the bot sent are blue bubbles on the right. Each bubble shows the date/time and, for outgoing messages, delivery ticks.

The feed scrolls to the newest message when you open a conversation and when new messages arrive, unless you have scrolled up to read history (then it stays where you are).

What each kind of message looks like:

| Message type | How it appears | What you can do |
|---|---|---|
| **Text** | Plain bubble; line breaks kept | Read |
| **Image / Sticker** | Thumbnail picture in the bubble | Click to open the full-size viewer; there is a **Download full size** link in the viewer; click outside or the X to close |
| **Document / PDF** | File card with file name, size (KB) and a download button | Click the download arrow |
| **Audio / voice note** | Built-in audio player | Play/pause/seek |
| **Video** | Built-in video player | Play |
| **WhatsApp cart order** | Green card "WhatsApp Cart Order" with items, quantity, estimated total, and the customer's note | **Manage in Orders** link opens the Orders page. An order record is created automatically from the cart |
| **Template message** | Template card (see below) | Click a quick-reply button to put its text into your message box |

If a file or image cannot be loaded, you will see a placeholder text such as `[Image]`, `[Audio]` or `[Document]`.

### Template cards

A template message (see "Sending a WhatsApp template") is drawn like WhatsApp shows it:

- Top strip: template name, category chip (for example MARKETING, UTILITY), and a green **Meta Approved** mark if the template is approved.
- Header: text, image, video or document (an image can be clicked to enlarge; a missing media file shows a dashed placeholder such as "Image Header (Upload image)").
- Body text with the variables filled in.
- Footer text in italics (if the template has one).
- Buttons: **link** buttons open the web address in a new tab; **call** buttons dial the phone number; **quick reply** buttons copy their text into your message box (they do not send automatically).

## Message status ticks (outgoing messages)

Ticks appear next to the time on every message you or the bot sent. Hover over a tick to see its name.

| Icon | Name shown on hover | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Single grey/pale tick | **Sent** | Accepted by the platform and handed to the channel (WhatsApp/Telegram). Also the default when no later update has arrived yet |
| Double tick (pale) | **Delivered to device** | The channel confirmed it reached the customer's phone/device |
| Double tick (sky blue) | **Read by customer** | The customer opened the message (WhatsApp may not report this if the customer has read receipts turned off) |
| Amber circled "i" | **Not delivered** | The message failed. A message box with the reason appears right under the bubble |

Ticks update by themselves as the channel reports back; you do not need to refresh. Incoming (customer) messages show no ticks.

## Delivery-failure message ("Not delivered")

When an outgoing message fails, a small note appears under it with a one-line reason and a grey number chip (the WhatsApp error code). Click **Details** to expand: it shows what it means and what to do, and, when available, WhatsApp's own wording ("WhatsApp said: ...").

| Code | Title you see | What it means and what to do |
|---|---|---|
| 131049 | WhatsApp limited this marketing message | Meta chose not to deliver a marketing message to protect the person from too many promotions. Try again later or send a utility/service message instead |
| 131026 | This number can't receive the message | The number is not on WhatsApp, has blocked your business, or uses an outdated WhatsApp version. Check the number; nothing you can resend will fix a block |
| 131047 | 24-hour reply window is closed | The customer has not written in the last 24 hours. Send an approved template instead |
| 131048 | Sending limit reached for this number | WhatsApp paused sending because many recent messages were reported or ignored. Slow down and improve message/template quality |
| 131056 | Too many messages to this contact | Too many messages to this person in a short time. Wait a while |
| 130429 | Sending rate limit reached | Your phone number hit its speed limit. Send more slowly and retry |
| 130472 | Delivery paused by Meta for this number | Meta is running a test including this recipient. No action needed; it may work later |
| 132000 | Template parameters don't match | The number of variable values does not match the approved template. Check every variable |
| 132001 | Template not found or not approved | The template does not exist in that language or is not approved yet |
| 132012 | A template value has the wrong format | A variable is not in the format the template expects |
| 131000 | WhatsApp had a temporary problem | Problem on the WhatsApp side. Send again later |
| any other | Message not delivered | WhatsApp did not deliver it. Meta's own sentence (if any) is shown; otherwise "Check the WhatsApp channel connection and try again." |

Failure notes use calm colours: amber for things you can usually fix or retry, grey for things outside your control.

Important: a failed message is **not** resent automatically. Fix the cause and send a new message.

title: Replying to a customer
content:
# Replying to a customer
## Send a text reply

1. Open the conversation from the list.
2. Click the box at the bottom ("Type a reply...").
3. Type your message.
4. Click **Send** (the paper-plane button), or press Enter in the box.
5. The message appears in the feed with a single tick, and a "Message sent" notice is shown.

Rules and behaviour:

- **Send** is disabled while the box is empty or contains only spaces. Leading and trailing spaces are removed.
- While sending, the box is locked and says "Sending message...". If sending fails, you see the error and your text is put back in the box so you do not lose it.
- The message box is one line of plain text.
- The first time your team replies in a case, the system records the first-response time for the case's response-time reports.
- When you reply, any running bot flow for this conversation is paused so the bot does not talk over you (see "Bot and AI handoff").
- If the case has no assigned agent, you automatically become the assigned agent when you reply (as long as you are an active Owner/Admin/Agent). A pending case becomes open.

## When the message box is replaced by a notice

| Situation | What you see | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| The case is **closed** | "This case is closed. Use **Reopen** above to reply. If the customer writes again, this same case reopens automatically." | Click **Reopen** in the case-action bar |
| WhatsApp conversation where the 24-hour window has run out | Red box "24-Hour Customer Care Window Expired" with a **Send Template Message** button | Send an approved template (see below) |

## Smart Reply suggestions

Above the message box is a purple **Smart Reply** bar.

- When you open a conversation, the system asks the AI for suggested replies. While it works it shows "Generating AI suggestions...".
- Each suggestion is a button, sometimes with a confidence percentage. Click one to place the text in your message box. It is **not** sent: edit it and press Send yourself.
- **Refresh** (circular arrows) asks for new suggestions. **X** hides the bar until you reload the page. If there are none, a **Get suggestions** link appears.
- If the AI service is unavailable, the bar simply stays empty; no error is shown.

## Attach and send a file

1. In an open, non-closed conversation, click the **paperclip** icon left of the message box.
2. Choose a file from your computer. Accepted types in the picker: images, video, audio, PDF, plain text, Word (.doc/.docx), Excel (.xls/.xlsx) and ZIP.
3. The **Send Media Attachment** window opens. Images show a preview; other files show their name, size (MB) and type.
4. Optionally type a **Caption** (one line).
5. Click **Send Attachment** (or **Cancel** to discard).
6. When done you see "Media sent successfully" and the file appears in the feed.

Rules:

- **Maximum 50 MB** per file. A larger file shows "File size exceeds 50MB limit" and is not selected.
- One file at a time.
- The system chooses the message type from the file: pictures are sent as images (WebP pictures are sent as stickers), videos as video, audio files as audio, everything else as a document. The original file name is kept for documents.
- The caption is sent as the text with the file.
- The paperclip is disabled while a text message is being sent.
- The channel itself (for example WhatsApp) may impose its own size/format limits that are stricter than 50 MB; if the channel refuses a file, you will see its error message. The exact WhatsApp limits per type are not enforced or shown by the platform (Notes).

## Sending a WhatsApp template

Templates are pre-approved messages created in Meta Business Suite and synced to your WhatsApp channel. They are the only way to start or restart a conversation when the 24-hour window is closed.

How to open the template window:

- If the window has expired, click **Send Template Message** in the red notice, or
- In a WhatsApp conversation with an open window, click the **green document-with-check icon** left of the message box ("Send WhatsApp Business Template").

Steps:

1. The **Send WhatsApp Template Message** window opens and loads your channel's templates ("Loading approved WhatsApp templates...").
2. In **Choose Template**, pick a template. The list shows `name (language) • category`. The first template is pre-selected.
3. If the template has a header:
   - **Text header:** type the header text.
   - **Image / Video / Document header:** upload a file (or give a media link). This is required: without it you see "Please upload a image file or provide a media URL for this template."
4. Under **Fill Template Variables**, type a value for each variable `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`, ... in the body. Variable `{{1}}` is pre-filled with the contact's name when known.
5. Check the **Live WhatsApp Chat Preview** at the bottom: it shows exactly how the customer will see the message.
6. Click **Send Template**. You see `Template "<name>" sent successfully`, and the card appears in the feed.

Rules and tips:

- Only approved templates are listed. If your channel has no approved templates but has others, those others are listed instead (they may then fail at send time with code 132001).
- If no templates are found at all you see "No Approved Templates Found: Sync templates in Channel Settings or create new templates in Meta Business Suite." Go to the Channels page, open the WhatsApp channel, and sync templates.
- The variable boxes are not marked as required by the screen, but WhatsApp rejects a template with a missing or wrongly formatted value (codes 132000 and 132012). Fill in every variable.
- The template button is shown only on WhatsApp conversations.
- Template language defaults to English if the template does not state one.
- Marketing templates may be refused by WhatsApp for some recipients (code 131049).

---

title: The WhatsApp 24-hour window
content:
# The WhatsApp 24-hour window
WhatsApp only allows free-form messages (text and files) for **24 hours after the customer's last message**. After that, only approved templates can be sent.

How the Inbox shows it:

- In the chat header of a WhatsApp conversation, a green clock chip counts down the time left (HH:MM:SS). It ticks every second and resets to 24 hours each time the customer writes.
- When it reaches zero, the chip disappears and the message box is replaced by the red "24-Hour Customer Care Window Expired" notice with **Send Template Message**.
- A WhatsApp conversation where the customer has never written (for example one started from a campaign) counts as expired, so you must use a template.
- Telegram and Live Webchat have no 24-hour limit; no clock is shown.
- When the customer replies to your template, the window opens again for 24 hours and the normal message box returns.

> **Good to know:**
>
> - Only the customer's messages restart the window; your own messages do not.
