title: Bot and AI handoff
content:
# Bot and AI handoff
Your channel can be connected to an automated **flow** (visual bot) in the Flows area. The Inbox shows and controls the handoff between that bot and your human team.

| Event | What happens |
|---|---|
| A customer writes and a published flow is set as the channel's default flow | The flow starts and replies automatically |
| The flow reaches its "hand off to agent" step | The conversation status becomes **needs agent** (pending). The bot stops replying. Anyone on the team can **Claim** it or reply |
| A human sends a message from the Inbox while the bot is running | The bot is paused for this conversation (marked "handed off") so it will not answer the customer's next message |
| You press **Resume AI Bot** (green robot icon) | The conversation is released to the bot: any paused or running flow is marked finished, and the bot/flow can answer the customer's next message from the start. Toast: "AI Bot / Flow reply mode resumed for this conversation" |
| You press **Close case** | Same release as above, so the next customer message starts fresh |
| The flow is not published, or the channel has no default flow | Nothing replies automatically; it is "Human inbox only" |

> **Good to know:**
>
> - **Resume AI Bot** does not change the status (a pending case stays pending) and does not send anything by itself; the bot answers when the customer next writes.
> - The button is shown for every conversation; it has no effect if no flow is configured for the channel.
> - While a conversation is in the handed-off state, bulk campaign messages that need the bot flow skip this contact.
> - To create flows or choose which flow a channel/widget uses, see the Flows and Channels sections.

---

title: Right-hand panel
content:
# Right-hand panel
Toggle with the person icon in the chat header, or collapse with the small panel icon at the top right of the panel. It has two tabs.

## Tab 1: CRM & Deals

**Contact Details**

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Name | Contact's name ("No Name Set" if missing) |
| Channel line | Channel type and the channel's display name |
| Phone/ID | The contact's external ID |
| Email | Shown if the contact has an email (webchat visitors who gave one) |
| Tag chips | Tags stored on the contact (managed in Contacts, not here) |

**Deals (n)**: all CRM deals of this contact, each with title, stage badge and value. Values are stored in cents and displayed with a dollar sign ($10,000 cents = $100).

To add a deal:

1. Click **+ Add** next to "Deals".
2. In **Create New Deal**, fill in **Deal Title** (required, for example "Enterprise License").
3. **Deal Value (in Cents)**: number, for example 10000 = $100.00. If left blank or not a number the value is saved as 0.
4. Choose **Stage**: Lead, Qualified, Proposal, Negotiation, Won, Lost.
5. Click **Save Deal**. "Deal created successfully" is shown.

**Orders (n)**: the contact's latest 5 orders with order number, status (completed, cancelled/refunded, paid/processing, others), item count, total with currency, payment status and date. **View All** opens the Orders page.

> **Good to know:** the contact card, deals and orders load only for contacts among the first 100 contacts of the workspace. For other contacts, the card falls back to the name/ID shown in the conversation and deals/orders may appear empty (see Notes at the end).

## Tab 2: AI Copilot

Three tools. They use your workspace's AI service and may show an error toast if AI is not available.

**Summary**

1. Click **Generate** (or **Regenerate**).
2. You get: sentiment badge (positive, negative, mixed, neutral), main intent, a short summary, **Key Details** bullets and **Next Action Items**.
3. Click **Use** beside an action item to put it in the message box.

**Rephrase**

1. Type or paste a draft in **Draft Message**, or click **Copy from Composer** to take what you typed in the message box.
2. Choose a tone: Professional, Friendly, Concise, Bullet Points or Sales Pitch.
3. Click **Rephrase with AI**. Error "Please enter text to rephrase" appears if both boxes are empty.
4. Use the copy icon to copy the result, or **Insert into Composer** to place it in the message box for sending.

**Classifier**

1. Paste a customer message, or leave empty to use the latest incoming message of the conversation.
2. Click **Classify Intent & Urgency**.
3. Result: urgency (critical, high, medium...), detected intent, sentiment, confidence bar and extracted entities.
4. Error "No customer message found to classify" appears if there is nothing to classify.

Summaries, suggestions and classifications are reset when you switch conversations.

---

title: Real-time behaviour
content:
# Real-time behaviour
- The Inbox keeps a live connection to the platform. The badge in the list header shows its state.
- When live, you get instantly: new incoming and outgoing messages (also those sent by colleagues or the bot), delivery tick changes (sent, delivered, read, failed), and conversation changes made by colleagues (assignment, team, status).
- A new conversation from a customer appears at the top of the list; if a colleague changes a case so that it no longer matches your filters (for example it is assigned to someone else while you are on **mine**), it disappears from your list.
- If the live connection is down, the list and the open chat re-check the server every 15 seconds, so nothing is lost; there is just a delay.
- There are no sound or browser notifications in the Inbox.
- If you send a message while a refresh happens, the page avoids showing it twice.

---

title: Role restrictions
content:
# Role restrictions
| Role | Inbox access |
|---|---|
| Owner, Admin, Agent | Full: reply, attach, templates, assign, claim, team routing, close/reopen, resume bot, AI Copilot, add deals |
| Viewer | Can read conversations; the case-action bar is read-only text. Assignment, claim, status change and Resume AI Bot are refused by the server. (Sending messages is not blocked by the server for viewers according to the code; do not rely on it, ask your Owner to give the right role.) |

Only active Owners, Admins and Agents can be assigned a case.

title: Common errors and fixes (Inbox)
content:
# Common errors and fixes (Inbox)
| Message or situation | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "Failed to load conversations" | Network or server problem | Click Refresh; check your connection; sign in again if your session expired |
| "Failed to load messages" | Same | Click the conversation again |
| "Could not load team members for assignment" / "Could not load support teams" | The member/team lists could not load | Reload the page; the Agent and Team menus will be incomplete until then |
| "Failed to send message" (text returns to the box) | Channel problem, disconnected channel, or WhatsApp refused it | Check the channel on the Channels page; resend. If it is a WhatsApp conversation, check the 24-hour clock |
| Failed message with code 131047 | 24-hour window closed | Send an approved template |
| "File size exceeds 50MB limit" | File too large | Compress or send a link instead |
| "Failed to send media" | Channel refused the file type/size or the storage was unavailable | Try another format (JPEG/PNG images, MP4 video, PDF documents) |
| "No Approved Templates Found" | No templates synced | Sync templates in Channel Settings or create templates in Meta Business Suite and wait for approval |
| "Template parameters don't match" (132000) | A variable value is missing | Open the template again and fill all variables |
| "This case is closed — reopen it first" | You tried to claim a closed case | Click Reopen first |
| "This case is already assigned to another agent" | Someone else claimed first | Use the Agent drop-down to reassign |
| "Assignee must be an active owner, admin or agent of this workspace" | You tried to assign to a viewer or inactive user | Pick another person |
| "Action failed" | Generic failure of an assign/close action | Try again; if it persists contact your administrator |
| Colleagues' changes do not appear instantly | Badge says Offline/Reconnecting | Wait, or click Refresh; the list auto-refreshes every 15 s |

# Live Webchat widget

Live Webchat lets website visitors chat with your team from a chat bubble on your website or from a shareable link. Webchat conversations arrive in the Team Inbox with the **Live Webchat** badge and are answered like any other conversation.

title: Where it is managed
content:
# Where it is managed
Widgets are created and customised on the **Channels** page, on the **Live Webchat** tab (next to the Messaging tab). The tab shows a card for every widget. This section explains what the widget does and how to publish it; see the Channels section for the full channel setup.

title: Creating a widget
content:
# Creating a widget
1. Open **Channels** and select the **Live Webchat** tab.
2. Click **Create New Widget**.
3. Fill in the form (all optional except the internal name has a default):

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Channel / Widget Name (Internal)** | Name your team sees in the Inbox for this widget (default "Website Live Chat 1") |
| **Default Flow** | A published bot flow that answers visitors first. **None (Human inbox only)** means visitors wait for your team |
| **Chat Window Header Title** | Title at the top of the chat window (default "Chat with us") |
| **Subheader Text** | Line under the title; shown while you are online (default "Typically replies in minutes") |
| **Colour** | Main colour of the header, launcher and your visitor's bubbles |
| **Position** | Bottom Right or Bottom Left |
| **Launcher Button Text** | Text on the floating button. Leave empty for a round icon-only button |
| **Greeting Message** | First bubble the visitor sees (default "Hello! How can we help you today?") |
| **Input Box Placeholder** | Hint text in the message box |
| **Offline Fallback Message** | Banner shown when you are outside business hours |
| **Require name / Require email** | Ask the visitor to enter them before chatting |
| **Allowed origins** | Website addresses that may show the widget, separated by commas or new lines. Empty = every website allowed |
| **Active** | Switch the widget on or off |
| **Business hours** | Enable and choose a time zone (for example America/New_York or UTC) |

4. Click **Create Webchat Widget**. The embed-code window opens automatically.

To change settings later, use the customise (edit) button on the widget card and click **Save Widget Changes**. The card also has an **Active/Inactive** switch, a **Default Flow** selector, a copyable **Widget Key**, and a delete button. Deleting a widget deletes its channel; the embed script stops working on all websites immediately.

title: Installing the widget on your website
content:
# Installing the widget on your website
The embed window offers three options.

**Option 1: Script tag (recommended)**

1. Click **Copy Script**. It looks like:
   `<script src="https://YOUR-OMNI-ADDRESS/api/webchat/embed.js?key=wc_xxxxxxxx" async defer></script>`
2. Paste it in your website's page HTML, just before the closing `</body>` tag (or inside `<head>`), on every page where the chat bubble should appear.
3. Save/publish your website and reload a page: a chat bubble appears in the chosen corner.

**Option 2: Direct shareable link**

Click **Copy Link** or **Open**. The link is `https://YOUR-OMNI-ADDRESS/chat/<widget key>`. Send it by e-mail, SMS or social media bio. It opens a full chat page with no website needed.

**Option 3: Iframe**

Click **Copy Iframe** and paste into your page where you want a chat panel inside the page:
`<iframe src="https://YOUR-OMNI-ADDRESS/chat/<widget key>?embed=true" width="100%" height="600px" frameborder="0"></iframe>`

Tips:

- The widget key (starts with `wc_`) identifies your widget; treat the script as public (it is visible on your website).
- The script works in an isolated layer so your site's styles do not break the widget.
- To advanced users: you may define `window.OmniChatConfig = { widgetKey: '...' }` before the script as an alternative to the key in the address. If the key is missing, the widget does not appear (a message is logged in the browser console).
- Allowed origins: if you list addresses, visitors on other websites get an "Origin not allowed" error. Listing `example.com` also allows its sub-domains (such as `app.example.com`). `localhost`, 127.0.0.1 and common test tunnels are always allowed.

title: The visitor's experience
content:
# The visitor's experience
1. **Launcher:** a floating bubble in the corner (or the full page when using the direct link). It shows an unread count if your team replies while the window is closed.
2. **Header:** your title and subtitle, a green dot when online or "Currently Offline" with a grey dot when outside business hours, a sound on/off toggle, and a minimise (X/minimise) button. The agent avatar is shown if enabled.
3. **Offline banner:** outside business hours the visitor sees your offline message but can still send messages.
4. **Details form (if required):** "Welcome to Live Chat - Please introduce yourself". Name and/or email fields (email must be a valid address) and **Start Conversation**. If the visitor leaves a required field empty, nothing happens/an alert asks for it. Without these requirements the visitor can type straight away; the contact is then called "Website Visitor".
5. **Greeting:** your greeting message appears as the first bubble.
6. **Writing:** the visitor types and presses **Enter** (Shift+Enter for a new line) or clicks the send button. Their messages appear on the right in your chosen colour with ticks (sent, delivered, read; a red mark if it failed).
7. **Attachments:** the paperclip uploads a photo or document (images, PDF, Word documents, plain text; the embedded script also accepts audio). Maximum **25 MB**. If the upload fails the visitor sees "Failed to upload file. Please try again."
8. **Your replies:** appear on the left, with a sound beep if sound is on, and typing dots if the sender reports typing. Bot messages with choice buttons show as buttons; clicking one sends its label as the visitor's message.
9. **Coming back:** the visitor is recognised by their browser, so their previous conversation and name/email are restored for up to 30 days. If they clear browser data or use another browser/device, they start as a new contact.
10. **Footer:** a "Powered by Omni-Platform" note in the embedded script.

Real-time and refresh: the on-page script checks for new messages every few seconds (about 3.5 seconds while open, about 12 seconds while minimised). The direct-link page uses a live connection.

title: What happens in the Inbox
content:
# What happens in the Inbox
- Each visitor becomes a contact (name "Website Visitor" or the name they entered; email stored on the contact; page address, browser and referrer are saved with the contact).
- The first message creates (or reopens) a conversation with channel **Live Webchat · <widget name>**; its status is **open**.
- If a default flow is set, the bot answers first; when it hands off, the case becomes **needs agent**.
- You answer from the Inbox as normal. Replies to webchat have no 24-hour limit. Ticks on webchat replies show as **Sent**.
- Visitors only ever see their own conversation. The Inbox does not show whether a visitor is currently typing.
- If a visitor writes after you closed the case, the same case reopens.

title: Common problems (Live Webchat)
content:
# Common problems (Live Webchat)
| Problem | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Bubble does not appear | Wrong or missing key in the script; script not pasted on that page; widget deleted | Copy the script again from the widget card; check the browser console |
| "Failed to load live chat widget" / "Widget not found" | Wrong key or deleted widget | Re-copy the code |
| "Origin not allowed for this webchat widget" | The website is not in **Allowed origins** | Add the website address in the widget settings, or leave the list empty |
| Widget shows but messages do not send | The widget is **Inactive** ("Webchat widget is currently disabled") | Turn the switch to **Active** |
| Always shows "Offline" | Business hours enabled but outside hours; also see Notes | Check the time zone; or disable business hours |
| Visitor lost the conversation | Browser data cleared or a different device | A new conversation starts; nothing to fix |
| Upload failed | File over 25 MB or unsupported type | Use a smaller file; images, PDF, DOC/DOCX, TXT |

title: Channels
content:
# Channels
## What the Channels page is for

The **Channels** page is where you connect the places your customers talk to you, and manage how each one behaves. Everything that arrives from a customer (a WhatsApp message, a Telegram message, a website live-chat message) comes in through a "channel". Each channel can also be given an automation (a "Default Flow") that answers customers automatically.

The page has two tabs:

| Tab | What it contains |
|---|---|
| **Messaging Channels** | WhatsApp and Telegram connections. You can connect, check, share a link or QR code for, manage templates for, and disconnect each one. |
| **Live Webchat Widgets** | Live-chat bubbles you place on your own website (or share as a link). You can design the look, set business hours and get the embed code. |

Channel types supported in this version of the product:

| Channel | How you connect it | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|
| WhatsApp (official Meta WhatsApp Business) | One-click "Meta Embedded Signup" (recommended), or manual entry of Meta credentials | Messaging Channels tab |
| Telegram bot | Manual entry of a bot token and a secret token | Messaging Channels tab |
| Website live chat (Webchat) | Create a widget; no outside account needed | Live Webchat Widgets tab |

> **Good to know:**
>
> - Instagram, Facebook Messenger and Email channels are **not** available on this page. You will not find a button to connect them. (The system has internal placeholders for some of these names, but there is no screen or working connection for them.)
> - Email used by the platform (for example notification emails) is configured by the platform operator, not from the Channels page.

## How to get there

1. Sign in to Omni Platform.
2. In the left-hand menu, click **Channels** (the radio-tower icon).
3. The page opens on the **Messaging Channels** tab. Click **Live Webchat Widgets** to switch.

You can also reach the page from links on the Dashboard and from the "Getting started" steps in the in-app Documentation page.

## Who can do what (roles)

Anyone who is signed in can **see** the Channels page, the list of channels, a channel's settings, its QR/link and its WhatsApp templates. Changes are limited by role:

| Action | Who is allowed |
|---|---|
| View channels, open Settings, view QR & Link, view Templates | Any signed-in team member |
| Connect WhatsApp (Meta signup, or manual) | Owner, Admin |
| Connect a Telegram bot (manual) | Owner, Admin |
| Change a channel's Default Flow | Owner, Admin |
| "Sync" a channel's details from Meta/Telegram | Owner, Admin |
| Disconnect (delete) a channel | Owner, Admin |
| Create (submit) a WhatsApp template | Owner, Admin |
| Create, edit, activate/deactivate, delete a webchat widget | Notes: the system does not apply an Owner/Admin restriction to webchat widgets, so any signed-in team member can do these. Check with your account owner if you want to restrict who touches them. |

If you are not an Owner or Admin and try a restricted action, you will see an error such as "Insufficient permissions". Ask an Owner or Admin to do it for you.

title: Messaging Channels tab
content:
# Messaging Channels tab
## Page layout

From top to bottom:

1. **Tab bar** - "Messaging Channels" (with a count of connected non-webchat channels) and "Live Webchat Widgets" (with a count of widgets).
2. **Title and buttons** - the title reads **Channel Integrations**. On the right are two buttons:
   - **Connect Telegram Bot** - opens the manual connection form (it also lets you choose WhatsApp Cloud API direct entry).
   - **Connect WhatsApp (Meta Signup)** - opens the one-click Meta signup window.
3. **Tech Provider Capacity Status banner** (dark banner, only shown if the system could load it). It shows how many WhatsApp onboardings the platform has used out of its allowance. See "Onboarding capacity" below.
4. **Channel cards** - one card for each connected WhatsApp or Telegram channel. If you have none, an empty state says "No channels connected yet" with a **Connect WhatsApp** button.

## Onboarding capacity banner

The dark banner shows:
- A green label **Tech Provider Capacity Status** and a purple badge such as **"7 Available"**.
- A line such as: "Meta rolling limit: 3 used / 10 maximum in 7 days."
- A small refresh icon (**Refresh capacity**) that reloads the page data.

What this means: Meta limits how many new business customers the Omni Platform can onboard through one-click signup. The limit is **10 new WhatsApp signups in any rolling 7-day period, counted across the whole platform (all customers together)**. If the remaining number is 0, new one-click WhatsApp connections are refused until older ones fall outside the 7-day window (see "Common errors").

## Reading a channel card

Each card shows:

| Part of card | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Round logo | **W** (green) for WhatsApp, **T** (blue) for Telegram |
| Name | The channel's display name |
| Type | "whatsapp" or "telegram" |
| Status badge (top right) | Green when the status is **active**; red for anything else (for example "disabled") |
| Phone line (WhatsApp) | The WhatsApp phone number, and the **verified business name** on the right |
| **Name:** badge (WhatsApp) | Meta's approval state for your business display name (see "Display-name statuses") |
| **Quality:** badge (WhatsApp) | Green/Yellow/Red message-quality rating (see "Quality rating") |
| **Tier:** badge (WhatsApp) | Your 24-hour messaging limit (see "Messaging limit tiers") |
| Bot line (Telegram) | The bot's @username and first name (shown once known) |
| **Default Flow** drop-down | Choose which automation answers customers on this channel |
| Buttons | **Settings**, **QR & Link**, **Templates** (WhatsApp only), **Disconnect** |

For Telegram cards, the Disconnect button stretches across the full width because there is no Templates button.

## Default Flow (automation) on a channel

The **Default Flow** drop-down on each card controls what happens when a customer writes in:

- **None (Human inbox only)** - no automation. Messages go to your team inbox only.
- **A flow name with its version, for example "Welcome Bot (v3)"** - that automation runs for incoming text messages.

Rules:
- Only **published** flows are listed. If you cannot see your flow, open the Flows area and publish it first.
- The change is saved the moment you pick a value. You will see the message **"Default automation flow updated"**.
- Only Owners and Admins can change it. Others get an error message.
- If you try to save a flow that has since been deleted you will see "Flow not found or deleted". If the flow is not published you will see "Only published flows can be assigned to a channel. Please publish the flow first."

## Channel status values

| Where | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Card badge | **active** (green) | Channel is connected and working |
| Card badge | any other value (red) | Channel is not active (for example it was disabled) |
| Settings window header | the same status word | Same as above |

> **Good to know:** This page does not have an on/off switch for messaging channels. To stop using one, disconnect it. (The Live Webchat tab does have an Active/Inactive switch for widgets.)

## Display-name statuses (WhatsApp)

The **Name:** badge and the "Meta Name Approval Status" field show Meta's state for your WhatsApp display name:

| Value | Colour / icon | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| APPROVED | Green, tick | Meta approved your business display name |
| AVAILABLE_WITHOUT_REVIEW | Green, tick | The name can be used without review |
| PENDING_REVIEW | Amber, clock | Meta is still reviewing the name |
| Anything else (for example DECLINED, EXPIRED, NONE) | Red, cross | The name was not accepted or has expired; fix it in Meta Business Suite |
| (empty) | "Unknown / Pending" in Settings | Not fetched yet - click Sync |

## Quality rating (WhatsApp)

Meta rates how well customers respond to your messages. It is shown on the card and in Settings.

| Rating | Shown as | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| GREEN | HIGH (Green) | Healthy. Customers are not blocking or reporting you much |
| YELLOW | MEDIUM (Yellow) | Warning. Quality is slipping |
| RED (anything not green/yellow) | LOW (Red) | Poor. Your sending limit can be reduced or the number restricted by Meta |

How to improve: send messages only to people who agreed to receive them, make templates relevant, and avoid sending too often.

## Messaging limit tiers (WhatsApp)

The **Tier** badge tells you how many different customers you may start a conversation with (business-initiated) in a rolling 24 hours. It is read from Meta.

| Tier | Limit per 24 hours | What it generally means | How to move up (as shown in the app) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 50 | 50 contacts | Trial or unverified phone number | Verify your phone number and finish basic Meta setup to reach Tier 250 |
| Tier 250 | 250 contacts | Standard, unverified Meta Business Account. This is also what the app shows if Meta has not reported a tier yet | Complete Meta Business Verification in Meta Business Suite to unlock Tier 1K |
| Tier 1K | 1,000 contacts | Verified business | Send at least 500 high-quality messages within 7 days to scale to Tier 10K |
| Tier 10K | 10,000 contacts | High volume | Keep a GREEN quality rating and send high volume to reach Tier 100K |
| Tier 100K | 100,000 contacts | Enterprise volume | Keep message quality high; Meta promotes you to Unlimited automatically |
| Tier Unlimited | No cap | Maximum tier | Keep a GREEN quality rating to avoid being downgraded |

In **Settings** the six tiers are shown as a row of boxes. The box for your current tier is highlighted purple and labelled **Active**; lower tiers say **Completed**; higher tiers say **Locked**. Below the row, a note explains your tier and "Scaling Next Tier" tips.

> **Good to know:** The limits and upgrade tips are guidance written into the app. Meta decides the real tier and can change it at any time.

---

title: Connecting WhatsApp with Meta Embedded Signup (recommended)
content:
# Connecting WhatsApp with Meta Embedded Signup (recommended)
## What you need before you start

- A Facebook (Meta) personal login that can manage your business.
- A Meta Business account (the popup can help you create one).
- A phone number you can receive a verification code on (a call or SMS). The number must not already be in use with the regular WhatsApp or WhatsApp Business app unless you follow Meta's migration prompts.
- An Owner or Admin role in Omni Platform.
- Your Omni Platform operator must have set up the Meta app on the server. If it is not set up, the button will tell you (see "Common errors").

## Steps

1. Go to **Channels** > **Messaging Channels**.
2. Click **Connect WhatsApp (Meta Signup)** (or **Connect WhatsApp** in the empty state).
3. A window titled **Connect WhatsApp via Meta Embedded Signup** opens, with the sub-title "One-click official Meta Tech Provider onboarding".
4. Look at the small badge on the right of the blue banner:
   - **Loading SDK...** (amber) - Meta's sign-in tools are still loading. Wait a few seconds.
   - **Meta SDK Ready** (green) - you can proceed.
5. Click the blue **Launch Meta Embedded Signup** button. It briefly shows "Opening Meta Popup...".
6. A Meta (Facebook) popup opens. In the popup:
   1. Log in to Facebook if asked.
   2. Choose or create your **Meta Business Account**.
   3. Choose or create your **WhatsApp Business Account**.
   4. Enter the **phone number** you want to use and the display name, then verify it with the code Meta sends.
   5. Grant the permissions requested and finish.
7. When the popup closes, Omni Platform automatically completes the connection. You will see a progress screen "Connecting your WhatsApp Business Channel..." with the text "Exchanging credentials, fetching verified business profile from Meta, and subscribing webhooks automatically."
8. When finished the window closes and a message says **Connected "<name>" successfully!** Your new card appears on the page.

What Omni Platform does for you automatically:
- Exchanges Meta's one-time code for a long-lived access token.
- Finds your WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) ID and Phone Number ID if Meta did not pass them (it reads them from the token).
- Registers your phone number for use with the WhatsApp Cloud API (if Meta says it is already registered, this is fine and is skipped).
- Subscribes the platform to receive your incoming message events (webhooks). You do **not** need to configure a webhook URL or verify token yourself for this method.
- Reads your verified business name, display phone number, quality rating and messaging-limit tier from Meta.
- Names the channel for you in the form **"Verified Business Name (+phone)"**. If no verified name exists it uses the WABA name and phone, or "WhatsApp Business".
- If a channel for the same phone number or WABA already exists in your account, it is **updated** with fresh credentials and set to active instead of creating a duplicate.

Progress messages you may see: "Connecting your WhatsApp Business Account to Omni Platform...", "WhatsApp Account & Phone Number received from Meta!".

## Advanced / Manual Configuration (optional) inside the signup window

Below the blue button there is a collapsible row **Advanced / Manual Configuration (Optional)**. Click it to show a form. You normally do not need it. It is useful if Meta returned a code but the connection did not finish.

| Field | What to enter | Required? |
|---|---|---|
| **Channel Display Name (Optional override)** | A name of your choice. Leave empty to use Meta's verified name. (If Meta supplies a verified name, that name is used regardless.) | No |
| **Authorization Code** | Filled in automatically by the Meta popup ("Code received from Meta SDK" appears in green). You can paste a code if you have one. | Yes, to save |
| **WhatsApp Business Account (WABA ID)** | Filled automatically ("WABA ID captured"). Leave empty to let the platform discover it. | No |
| **Phone Number ID** | Filled automatically ("Phone ID captured"). Leave empty to let the platform discover it. | No |

Click **Save Channel Manually**. The button stays disabled until an Authorization Code is present.

Important: A Meta authorization code can be used **once** and expires quickly. If it was already used or expired you will see: "This Meta authorization code was already used or expired. Please click 'Launch Meta Embedded Signup' to generate a fresh one-time code." Launch the popup again.

## If you close the popup without finishing

Nothing is saved. The window stays open and you can click **Launch Meta Embedded Signup** again.

---

title: Connecting a channel manually
content:
# Connecting a channel manually
Use **Connect Telegram Bot** (top right of the Messaging Channels tab). The window is titled **Connect Channel Manually** with the sub-title "Add a Telegram Bot or direct WhatsApp Cloud API channel".

Fields common to both types:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Channel Type** | Drop-down: **Telegram Bot** (default) or **WhatsApp Cloud API (Direct)** |
| **Channel Display Name** | Required. A name your team will recognise, for example "Support Telegram Bot" |

Buttons: **Cancel** and **Connect Channel**. After a successful save you will see "<name> connected successfully!" and the new card appears.

## Connecting a Telegram bot

Before you start, create a bot in Telegram:

1. In Telegram, search for **@BotFather** and open it.
2. Send the command `/newbot` and follow the prompts to choose a name and username. (The username must end in "bot".)
3. BotFather replies with the **bot token** - a long string like `123456789:ABCdefGHIjklMNOpqrsTUVwxyz`. Keep it private.

Then in Omni Platform:

1. Click **Connect Telegram Bot**.
2. Leave **Channel Type** as **Telegram Bot**.
3. Type a **Channel Display Name**.
4. Paste the token into **Telegram Bot Token** (the hint reads "Get this from @BotFather on Telegram").
5. In **Secret Token (Webhook Verification)** type any random, hard-to-guess string of your own (the example shown is "random-secret-string-here"). Use letters, numbers, underscore or dash. Both fields are required.
6. Click **Connect Channel**.
7. Open **Settings** on the new card and click **Sync from Telegram**. If the token is valid, the bot's @username and first name fill in.

What the system needs from Telegram: it sends your customers' messages to this address, using the secret token as proof it is really Telegram:
- Webhook address for the channel: `<your Omni Platform address>/webhooks/telegram/<channel-id>`
- Telegram must send the secret in the header `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token`.

> **Good to know:**
>
> - The **QR & Link** for Telegram requires the bot's @username to be known. Click **Sync from Telegram** in Settings first.
> - Telegram supports text, photos and documents from customers in this version.

## Connecting WhatsApp Cloud API directly (manual)

Choose this only if you already manage your own Meta app and cannot use Embedded Signup.

1. Click **Connect Telegram Bot** (same button), then change **Channel Type** to **WhatsApp Cloud API (Direct)**.
2. Fill in the fields:

| Field | Where to find it | Required |
|---|---|---|
| **Channel Display Name** | Your choice | Yes |
| **WABA ID** | In Meta Business Suite > WhatsApp Manager > the account's details ("WhatsApp Business Account ID"). Also in your Meta developer app under WhatsApp > API Setup | Yes |
| **Phone Number ID** | In your Meta developer app under WhatsApp > API Setup, next to the phone number (the numeric ID, not the phone number itself) | Yes |
| **Permanent System User Access Token** | In Meta Business Settings > Users > System Users: create a system user, assign it your WhatsApp account, generate a token with the WhatsApp messaging and management permissions, and set it not to expire. Starts with "EAAG..." | Yes (entered as hidden text) |

3. Click **Connect Channel**.
4. In Meta's developer app (WhatsApp > Configuration), set the webhook to point to Omni Platform and subscribe to the "messages" field:
   - Callback URL: `<your Omni Platform address>/webhooks/whatsapp` (a channel-specific form, `/webhooks/whatsapp/<channel-id>`, also works).
   - Verify token: the value your platform administrator set for the WhatsApp webhook verify token. Ask your administrator; it is not shown in this screen.
5. Open **Settings** and click **Sync from Meta** to load the name, quality rating and tier.

> **Good to know:**
>
> - This manual method does not register the phone number or subscribe your app to the account's events for you. Do those in Meta if messages do not arrive.
> - Because the manual form does not save a phone number, the **QR & Link** feature may need a Sync first, or may fail with "WhatsApp channel is missing phone number".
> - The manual form does not save the API address field, so the standard Meta address is used.

---

title: QR & Link (share a chat link with customers)
content:
# QR & Link (share a chat link with customers)
Click **QR & Link** on any card. The window is titled "<channel name> - QR Code & Deep Link" with the text "Share this link or QR code with your customers to start conversations".

It shows:
- A **QR code** picture. Customers scan it with their phone camera to open a chat with you.
- **Deep Link URL** (read-only) with a **Copy** button. Copying shows "Link copied to clipboard".
- **Done** to close.

What the link looks like:
- WhatsApp: `https://wa.me/<phone number digits>`
- Telegram: `https://t.me/<bot username>`

Fixes if it fails (an error toast appears):
- "WhatsApp channel is missing phone number. Please reconnect via Embedded Signup or verify channel credentials." - open Settings and click Sync, or reconnect.
- "Telegram channel is missing bot username in credentials" - open Settings and click Sync from Telegram.
- "Invalid WhatsApp phone number in channel credentials." - the stored number has no digits; reconnect.

title: Channel Settings, health check and sync
content:
# Channel Settings, health check and sync
Click **Settings** on a card. The window is titled "<channel name> - Channel Settings & Status", sub-title "Upstream provider verification status, identifiers, and configuration".

## Top bar

- Logo, channel name, and "<type> Channel - Status: <status>".
- **Sync from Meta** (WhatsApp) or **Sync from Telegram** (Telegram). This is the page's **health check**. Click it to fetch the latest details from the provider. While running it reads "Syncing with Provider...". Success message: "Channel live status synced with Meta WhatsApp Cloud API!" or "...with Telegram Bot API!". Only Owners and Admins can use it.

What Sync does:
- **WhatsApp:** asks Meta for your phone number's verified name, display number, quality rating, name status, code-verification status and messaging tier, and for the account name, time zone and currency. The card on the page updates too.
- **Telegram:** asks Telegram "who am I?" using your bot token and updates the bot's username, first name and ID.
- If the provider does not answer (wrong or expired token, no internet), the old values simply remain and you may not see an error. Compare the "last values" with what you expect. If the values never change after a Sync, your token may be wrong or expired - reconnect the channel.

## WhatsApp section: "Meta WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) Details"

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Verified Business Name** | The name Meta shows to customers. "Not configured" if unknown |
| **Display Phone Number** | The customer-facing number |
| **Meta Name Approval Status** | See "Display-name statuses" |
| **Phone Number Quality Rating** | See "Quality rating" |
| **Phone Number ID** | Meta's ID for the phone number, with a copy button ("Phone Number ID copied to clipboard") |
| **WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) ID** | Meta's ID for the account, with a copy button ("WABA ID copied to clipboard") |
| **WABA Account Name** | Shown only if known |
| **Currency & Timezone** | Shown only if known, for example "USD - America/New_York" |
| **24-Hour Messaging Limit Tier** | Purple panel with the six-step tier ladder and tips (see tier table) |
| **System User Access Token** | Shows **Securely Encrypted (AES-256)** when a token is stored, or **Missing**. A masked sample of the token is displayed. The full token is never shown |

## Telegram section: "Telegram Bot Configuration"

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Bot Username** | Shown as @name, or "Not detected" |
| **Bot First Name** | Display name of the bot, or "Not set" |
| **Telegram Bot ID** | Shown when known |
| **Bot API Token** | **Encrypted (AES-256)** or **Missing**; masked sample shown |

## Danger zone

**Disconnect Channel** button - see the next section.

## Editing a channel

This version has no screen to rename a channel or change its credentials. To change a token or number, disconnect and connect again (for WhatsApp Embedded Signup, connecting again for the same number simply refreshes the existing channel).

title: Disconnecting a channel
content:
# Disconnecting a channel
1. On the channel card click **Disconnect** (or open **Settings** and click **Disconnect Channel** at the bottom).
2. A confirmation window titled **Disconnect Channel** opens with a yellow warning for "<channel name>":
   - Omni Platform will immediately stop receiving incoming messages on this channel.
   - The default automation flow will be unlinked automatically.
   - Historical message logs and past conversations will remain safely archived.
3. Click **Cancel** to keep it, or the red **Disconnect Channel** button to confirm.
4. You see **Disconnected "<name>" successfully** and the card disappears.

> **Good to know:**
>
> - You can reconnect the same type of channel later.
> - Disconnecting here removes the channel from Omni Platform. It does **not** delete your WhatsApp account or Telegram bot. If you want to stop Meta sending events, also remove the connection inside Meta Business settings.
> - Only Owners and Admins can disconnect.
> - Before disconnecting, consider whether any scheduled campaigns use that channel.

title: WhatsApp Message Templates
content:
# WhatsApp Message Templates
Templates are pre-approved messages. WhatsApp requires them for any message you send **outside the 24-hour customer service window** (for example broadcast campaigns, or follow-ups after the customer has been silent for more than 24 hours). Inside the 24-hour window after a customer writes to you, you can reply with free-form messages.

Templates are submitted to Meta for approval. They live in your Meta WhatsApp Business Account, so templates are per WhatsApp account, not shared between channels with different accounts.

## Opening the template list

1. On a **WhatsApp** card, click **Templates**. (Telegram cards do not have this button.)
2. A large window titled "<channel name> - Message Templates" opens, sub-title "View approved message templates synchronized with Meta WABA". The list is loaded live from Meta each time you open it ("Loading templates from Meta Graph API...").

Requirements: the channel must have a stored WABA ID and access token. If not, you will see "WhatsApp channel is missing WABA ID. Please reconnect via Embedded Signup." or "WhatsApp channel is missing access token. Please reconnect via Embedded Signup."

## Template list features

- Hint text: "Templates are required for outbound broadcast campaigns outside the 24-hour service window."
- **New Template** button (top right) - opens the creation form.
- **Search box** - "Search by name, category or body text...". Filters as you type (short delay).
- **Status filter chips** - **All**, **Approved**, **Pending**, **Rejected**, **Paused**, **Disabled**. Each shows a count in brackets. A chip for a status is only shown if at least one template has it. Click a chip to filter.
- **Clear filters** link appears when nothing matches.
- **Close** button.

Each template row shows: name (monospace), category tag, language code, and **Header: <format>** tag if it has a header, plus a status badge on the right. Click the row to expand or collapse it. When expanded you see:
- The header text (if a text header), or "Media Attachment (IMAGE/VIDEO/DOCUMENT)" for media headers.
- The body text.
- The footer text.
- Each button as a small tag, for example "[QUICK REPLY] Yes", "[URL] Visit Website", "[PHONE NUMBER] Call Support", "[COPY CODE] SUMMER2026".

## Template statuses

| Status | Badge colour | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **APPROVED** | Green | Meta approved it. You can use it to message customers |
| **PENDING** | Amber | Submitted and waiting for Meta review. Usually minutes, sometimes up to 24 hours or more |
| **REJECTED** | Red | Meta refused it. Create a corrected template under a new name |
| **PAUSED** | Red (any non-approved, non-pending status shows red) | Meta paused it, usually because of low quality or poor customer feedback |
| **DISABLED** | Red | Meta disabled it after repeated problems |

> **Good to know:** The red-badge statuses other than REJECTED are not explained inside the app; the meaning above comes from Meta's usual behaviour. This page does not show Meta's rejection reason; check it in Meta Business Suite > WhatsApp Manager > Message Templates.

## Refreshing ("syncing") templates

The list is fetched from Meta every time you open the Templates window and after you submit a new template. To see a status change (for example Pending to Approved), close the window and click **Templates** again. There is no separate "Sync templates" button.

## Deleting or editing templates

This version of the Channels page **cannot edit or delete** templates. To change or remove an approved template, use **Meta Business Suite > WhatsApp Manager > Message Templates**. To "change" a template here, create a new one with a new name.

## Creating a template (full guide)

1. In the Templates window click **New Template**.
2. A window titled **Create WhatsApp Message Template** opens. The left side is the form (five numbered sections). The right side is a **Live WhatsApp Preview** phone mock-up that updates as you type.
3. Complete the sections below, then click **Submit Template to Meta** at the bottom right (or **Cancel** at the bottom left).
4. On success you see "Template submitted to Meta for approval!", the window closes, and the template list reloads. The new template normally appears as **PENDING**.

Only Owners and Admins can submit.

### Section 1 - General Information

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| **Template Name** | Required. Lowercase letters, numbers and underscores only. As you type, capital letters become lowercase and any other character (spaces, dashes, dots) becomes an underscore automatically. Up to 512 characters. Example: `order_shipped_v1` |
| **Category** | **MARKETING** (offers and promotions), **UTILITY** (orders, alerts, updates) or **AUTHENTICATION** (OTP and security). Default is MARKETING |
| **Language** | Drop-down. Default English (US). Options: English (US) en_US, English (UK) en_GB, Spanish (Spain) es_ES, Spanish (Latin America) es_LA, Portuguese (Brazil) pt_BR, French fr, German de, Italian it, Indonesian id, Hindi hi, Arabic ar, Turkish tr, Russian ru, Japanese ja, Korean ko, Chinese (Simplified) zh_CN, Chinese (Traditional) zh_TW, Vietnamese vi, Thai th, Malay ms, Dutch nl, Polish pl |

Category guidance:
- Choose **MARKETING** for promotions, offers, announcements, re-engagement.
- Choose **UTILITY** for messages about something the customer already did (order confirmation, delivery update, appointment reminder). It must not contain promotional text.
- Choose **AUTHENTICATION** for one-time passcodes and login/verification messages.
- Meta may change a category after review. If your category is wrong, Meta can re-categorise or reject it.

> **Good to know:** The AUTHENTICATION category on Meta normally has its own special format (a built-in one-time-password button). This form sends authentication templates using the same free-form layout as others; Meta may reject them. If you need OTP templates, check Meta's rules.

### Section 2 - Header (optional)

Pick one of five tabs: **None**, **Text**, **Image**, **Video**, **Document**. Default is None. Switching tabs clears any previous error message.

**Text header**
- Field **Header Text**, maximum 60 characters (a counter shows "0 / 60").
- Can contain at most one variable: `{{1}}` (for example "Order Confirmation #{{1}}").
- If the header contains `{{1}}`, a box **Header Sample Value for Meta Review** (required, marked with a red asterisk) appears. Enter a realistic example (such as 12345).

**Image / Video / Document header** - a file uploader called "Sample Image File" (or Video, Document). Meta needs an example to review. It has two modes (switch with the small toggle at the top right of the box):

| Mode | How it works |
|---|---|
| **Upload File** | Click the dashed box or drag a file onto it. The file is uploaded to the platform's storage. A green box then shows a thumbnail (images), the file name, a **Replace** button and an **X** (remove) button |
| **URL / Variable** | Type a public HTTPS link to the media, for example `https://example.com/file.jpg`. (The box also accepts a placeholder such as `{{variable_name}}` for dynamic use, but for template submission use a real public link.) |

File limits by header type:

| Header type | Accepted files | Max size |
|---|---|---|
| Image | JPG, PNG, WEBP | 5 MB. The description recommends a 1.91:1 or 16:9 shape |
| Video | MP4, 3GP (also QuickTime/MOV is accepted by the picker) | 16 MB. H.264 video with AAC audio recommended |
| Document | PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, PPT, PPTX, TXT, CSV | 100 MB. PDF is recommended |

Errors you may see in the uploader:
- "File is too large (X MB). Max allowed size for images is 5MB." (similar for videos and documents).
- "Failed to upload media file." or the specific message from the server.

A media header requires either an uploaded file or a URL before you can submit: "Please upload a sample image file or enter a sample media URL."

### Section 3 - Body Text & Variables (required)

- Big text box with a **character counter "0 / 1024 chars"**. Maximum 1,024 characters.
- Placeholder example: "Hello *{{1}}*! Thank you for ordering from us. Your order #{{2}} has been confirmed."

**Formatting toolbar** (above the box). Select text first, then click:

| Button | Writes | Looks like in WhatsApp |
|---|---|---|
| **Bold** | `*text*` | **bold** |
| **Italic** | `_text_` | *italic* |
| **Strike** | `~text~` | strikethrough |
| **Code** | three backticks around text | monospace |

If nothing is selected, the word "text" is inserted for you to replace.

**Variables (placeholders for personal details)**
- Syntax: double curly brackets with a number: `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`, `{{3}}`.
- Click the purple **Add Variable {{n}}** button to insert the next number where your cursor is.
- Numbers must start at 1 and have **no gaps** and be in a complete sequence. If you use `{{1}}` and `{{3}}` the form warns "Missing variable {{2}} in sequence." If the first is not 1 you see "Variables must start with {{1}}."
- Names like `{{name}}` are not supported here; use numbers only.
- When variables are detected, a section **Variable Samples for Meta Review** appears with one input box per variable ("2 variables detected"). Every sample is **required** (red asterisk). Use realistic data, such as "John" for a name or "12345" for an order number. Meta uses these samples to judge your template.
- The same variable number used twice is counted once.

Tips for approval (from the hint box beside the preview):
- Variables must represent realistic data for approval.
- Marketing templates require clear opt-out language in the footer.
- Utility templates cannot contain promotional copy.

Additional Meta habits to be aware of (general WhatsApp rules, not checked by this screen): do not start or end the body with a variable, avoid too many variables for a short message, and keep a reasonable amount of fixed text around each variable.

### Section 4 - Footer (optional)

- Single line, maximum 60 characters ("0 / 60 chars").
- No variables and no formatting characters.
- Good for opt-out text, for example "Reply STOP to unsubscribe".

### Section 5 - Action Buttons (optional)

A counter shows "0 / 10 buttons". You can add up to 10 buttons in total. Click an "Add" tile to add a button, then fill in its fields. Use the trash icon on a button to remove it.

| Button type (tile label) | Limit | Fields | Defaults added |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Quick Reply** | Counts toward the 10 total | Button Label | "Quick Reply" |
| **Website Link** (URL) | Maximum **2** per template | Button Label; **Website URL** (must start with http:// or https://; may include `{{1}}` at the end for a dynamic link); **Sample URL for Meta Review** (required when the URL contains `{{1}}`) | "Visit Website", https://example.com |
| **Call Number** (Phone) | Maximum **1** per template | Button Label; **Phone Number (E.164)** such as +18005550199 | "Call Support", "+1" |
| **Copy Code** | Maximum **1** per template | **Coupon / Offer Code** (for example SUMMER2026). The button shows as "Copy Code" in WhatsApp. | "Copy Code", "OFFER20" |

- **Button Label** maximum **25 characters** (all types except Copy Code, where the label is fixed by WhatsApp).
- Once you reach a type's limit, its tile is greyed out. Trying beyond limits shows messages such as "Meta limits templates to a maximum of 10 buttons total.", "Meta permits only 1 Phone Number button per template.", "Meta permits a maximum of 2 URL buttons per template.", "Meta permits only 1 Copy Offer Code button per template."
- Dynamic URL: only the placeholder `{{1}}` is supported in the URL.

> **Good to know:** Meta also has its own rules about mixing button types (for example quick replies must be grouped together, and total sizes). The form does not check these. If Meta refuses, the exact Meta message is shown at the bottom of the form.

### Live WhatsApp Preview

The right-hand phone mock-up shows how your template will look. It uses your sample values in place of variables, renders bold/italic/strike/code, shows the header (image/video/document placeholder or text), footer, and each button. It updates instantly. It is only a preview; actual WhatsApp appearance can differ slightly.

### Validation checklist (what happens when you click Submit)

The form checks, in this order, and shows the first problem in a red "Submission Error" box (you can close the box with the X):

1. Template Name is required.
2. Template name uses only lowercase letters, numbers and underscores.
3. Body text is required.
4. Variables start at {{1}} with no gaps.
5. If the header text has `{{1}}`, the header sample is filled in.
6. Every body variable has a sample value.
7. A media header has an uploaded file or URL.
8. All buttons have text; phone buttons have a number; URL buttons start with "http" and, if dynamic, have a sample URL; copy-code buttons have a code.

If everything passes, the template is sent to Meta. If Meta objects, the message from Meta is shown (for example "Meta: Invalid parameter"). Fix the issue and click Submit again.

## Common template errors and fixes

| Message | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Template Name can only contain lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores | Invalid characters | Use `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` |
| Variables must start with {{1}} / Missing variable {{n}} in sequence | Gaps in numbering | Renumber so they go 1, 2, 3... |
| Please provide a sample value for variable {{n}} | A variable has no example | Fill in each sample box |
| Please provide a sample text value for the Header variable {{1}} | Header has a variable but no example | Fill in the header sample |
| Please upload a sample image file or enter a sample media URL | Media header has no file | Upload a file or paste a public link |
| URL buttons must start with http:// or https:// | Link is not complete | Add the full link |
| Please provide a sample URL for the dynamic URL button | URL has `{{1}}` but no example | Enter a full example link |
| Meta: (something) | Meta rejected the submission - for example duplicate name and language, content policy, or invalid sample | Read the message, change the template (use a new name if the same name already exists), submit again |
| WhatsApp channel is missing WABA ID / access token | Channel was not connected via Embedded Signup | Reconnect the channel |
| Templates are only available for WhatsApp channels | You opened templates for a non-WhatsApp channel | Use a WhatsApp channel |
| Meta API error (...) while loading list | Token expired or revoked, or Meta temporarily down | Click Sync in Settings; reconnect if it persists |

title: Live Webchat Widgets tab
content:
# Live Webchat Widgets tab
Webchat lets website visitors chat with you in real time. You can place a chat bubble on any website with one line of code, or share a standalone chat page link.

## Page layout

- Title: **Live Webchat Widgets**. Sub-title: "Configure, preview, and embed real-time live chat widgets on external websites."
- Button **Create Webchat Widget** (top right).
- Information banner "Zero-Setup Embeddable Live Webchat" with a **WebSocket Real-Time** badge, a short description (single script tag or direct link; includes visitor authentication, visual flow automations, media uploads, live agent typing indicators) and a **Create New Widget** button.
- Widget cards (one per widget) or the empty state "No Webchat widgets created yet" with **Create First Webchat Widget**.

## Widget card

| Element | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Coloured icon | Uses your chosen brand colour |
| Name and "Title - Subtitle" | Internal name, then the title and subtitle visitors see |
| **Active / Inactive** badge (click it) | Click to switch the widget on or off immediately. Messages "Widget activated successfully" / "Widget deactivated successfully". Inactive cards are dimmed. An inactive widget shows "disabled" to visitors and does not accept new chats |
| **Widget Key** + copy | A unique code starting with `wc_`. Identifies the widget. Copy shows "Widget key copied to clipboard" |
| **Direct Link** - **Open Chat** and copy icon | A standalone page: `<your Omni Platform address>/chat/<widget key>`. "Direct chat link copied" appears when copied |
| **Position** | Bottom Right or Bottom Left |
| **Business Hours** | Shown only if business hours are on; shows the time zone |
| **Default Flow** drop-down | Same as for messaging channels: None (Human inbox only) or a published flow. "Webchat automation flow updated" on success |
| **Website Embed Script** (dark box) | The ready-to-paste script tag with **Copy Script** button |
| **Get Embed Code & Link** | Opens the embed window (see below) |
| **Customize** | Opens the customise form with current values |
| **Delete** | Deletes the widget (confirmation required) |

## Create a widget (step by step)

1. Open the **Live Webchat Widgets** tab.
2. Click **Create Webchat Widget** (or **Create New Widget**).
3. The window **Create Live Webchat Widget** opens: a form on the left and an interactive **Live Preview** on the right. The preview updates as you type; you can click inside it to try it.
4. Fill in the fields (see tables below).
5. Click **Create Webchat Widget** at the bottom (sticky bar). Use **Cancel** to abandon.
6. On success: "Webchat widget created successfully!" and the **Embed Code** window opens automatically so you can copy the code.

The default values are pre-filled. The internal name starts as "Website Live Chat 1" (the number goes up with each widget).

## Widget form fields

**General & Channel Settings**

| Field | Description | Required |
|---|---|---|
| **Channel / Widget Name (Internal)** | Name for your team (not shown to visitors) | Yes |
| **Default Bot Flow** | None (Human inbox only), or a published flow with its version | No |

**Branding & Styling**

| Field | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Chat Window Header Title** | Heading at the top of the chat window | Customer Support |
| **Subheader Text** | Smaller text under the title | We typically reply within minutes |
| **Primary Brand Color** | Colour picker plus a text box for a hex code such as #4f46e5. Used for the launcher button, header and visitor message bubbles | #4f46e5 |
| **Widget Position** | **Bottom Right** or **Bottom Left** | Bottom Right |
| **Launcher Button Text** | Text on the floating button | Chat with us |

**Greeting & Prompts**

| Field | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Initial Bot Greeting Message** | First message the visitor sees | Hello! How can we help you today? |
| **Input Box Placeholder** | Grey hint text in the message box | Type your message here... |
| **Offline Fallback Message** | Shown when you are outside business hours | We are currently away. Leave us a message and we will get back to you soon! |

**Visitor Lead Capture & Security**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Prompt for Visitor Name** (tick box) | Asks visitors for their name when they start a chat |
| **Prompt for Visitor Email** (tick box) | Asks visitors for their email address |
| **Allowed Domains / Origins (CORS Security)** | Websites that may show the widget. Enter full addresses such as `https://example.com, https://app.example.com`, separated by commas or new lines. **Leave empty to allow all websites.** A bare domain like example.com also covers its subdomains; a wildcard such as `*.example.com` is accepted. Local test addresses (localhost) are always allowed |

**Business Hours Schedule**

- Tick **Enable Schedule** to turn on business hours.
- **Timezone** - type a time zone name such as `America/New_York` or `UTC`. It starts as your browser's time zone.
- When business hours are on, visitors outside the hours see your Offline Fallback Message.
- The preview treats the widget as online when business hours are off.

> **Good to know:** The form only asks for the time zone. It does not offer a day-by-day timetable on this screen. The system stores an empty schedule unless one was set elsewhere. Check with your administrator how the open/closed hours are determined before relying on this setting.

> **Good to know:** The launcher icon style exists in the system (default "chat") but has no control on this form. The "agent avatar" option exists and is on by default, but also has no control on this form.

## Customise (edit) a widget

1. On the widget card click **Customize**.
2. The window **Customize Webchat Widget** shows the same form with current values.
3. Change what you need and click **Save Widget Changes**. Success message: "Webchat widget updated successfully".

## Embedding on your website

Click **Get Embed Code & Link** on a card (or it opens automatically after creating). The window "<title> - Embed Code" offers three options:

| Option | What it is | How to use |
|---|---|---|
| **Option 1: Embed Script Tag (Recommended)** | One line: `<script src="<your address>/api/webchat/embed.js?key=<widget key>" async defer></script>` | Click **Copy Script**. Paste it just before the closing `</body>` tag on every page where the chat bubble should appear (the card also says it can go in `<head>`). Message: "Embed script copied to clipboard" |
| **Option 2: Direct Shareable Link** | `<your address>/chat/<widget key>` | Click **Copy Link** or **Open**. Send by email, SMS or put it in a social-media bio |
| **Option 3: Full-Page Iframe Embed** | `<iframe src="<your address>/chat/<widget key>?embed=true" width="100%" height="600px" frameborder="0"></iframe>` | Click **Copy Iframe** and paste into a page to show the chat inside the page body |

Click **Done** to close.

Common website notes:
- If you set **Allowed Domains**, the website that embeds the widget must be on the list, otherwise the chat is refused ("Origin not allowed for this webchat widget").
- Website builders (WordPress, Shopify, Wix etc.) usually have a "custom code" or "header/footer scripts" area where you paste the script tag.

## Webchat behaviour for visitors

- Visitors are identified without a login (stateless visitor session).
- If **Prompt for Visitor Name/Email** is on, they are asked before chatting.
- The widget supports media uploads from visitors and shows live typing indicators when an agent is typing.
- When a visitor writes in, a conversation appears in your Inbox and the widget's Default Flow (if any) runs.
- A visitor cannot send an empty message ("Message text or media is required").
- If the widget is switched to **Inactive**, visitors see it as disabled ("Webchat widget is currently disabled").

## Delete a widget

1. On the card click **Delete**.
2. The confirmation window **Delete Webchat Widget** says:
   - The embed script will immediately stop loading on all external websites.
   - Direct standalone chat links will return a 404 Not Found error.
   - The associated channel integration and automated bot flows will be unlinked.
3. Click **Delete Widget** to confirm or **Cancel**. Message: "Webchat widget deleted successfully".

> **Good to know:** Deleting a widget also deletes its underlying channel. This cannot be undone. If you only want to pause it, click the **Active** badge to make it **Inactive** instead.

title: Incoming messages and webhooks (what happens behind the scenes)
content:
# Incoming messages and webhooks (what happens behind the scenes)
You do not need to set this up for Embedded Signup or webchat. For reference:

| Channel | Incoming address | How it is verified |
|---|---|---|
| WhatsApp | `<address>/webhooks/whatsapp` (or `/webhooks/whatsapp/<channel id>`) | Meta signs each message. The platform checks the signature |
| Telegram | `<address>/webhooks/telegram` (or `/webhooks/telegram/<channel id>`) | The secret token header from Telegram is compared with the one stored |
| Webchat | Built in | Widget key and allowed-domain check |

When a customer message arrives, the platform:
1. Finds the matching channel (by channel ID in the address, or by WhatsApp phone number/account in the message).
2. Finds or creates the contact and an open conversation (a message from a customer reopens their closed conversation).
3. Saves any photo, document, audio, video or sticker they sent.
4. For text, button replies and catalogue orders with text, runs the channel's Default Flow if one is set.
5. Skips messages it has already seen (duplicates are ignored).

Delivery receipts (sent, delivered, read, failed) from WhatsApp are recorded on the message and on any campaign that sent it. A failed receipt includes a code and message from the provider.

If no matching channel is found, the platform silently accepts the message and ignores it (this is so the provider does not keep retrying). If the signature is wrong, the message is rejected.

## WhatsApp catalogue orders

If a customer places an order from your WhatsApp catalogue, the platform automatically creates an order (with payment method "whatsapp_catalog") and matches items by SKU to your products. Currency defaults to INR if Meta does not say otherwise. Items whose SKU is not found are still added as "Product (<sku>)". Orders appear in the Commerce area, not on the Channels page.

> **Good to know:** There are no catalogue or payment-gateway settings on the Channels page itself. Product, order and payment settings are managed in the Commerce area. (The payment webhook uses a Razorpay secret set by the platform operator.)

content:
# Common errors and fixes (Channels page)
| What you see | Likely cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| "Failed to load channels" | Network or sign-in problem | Refresh; sign in again |
| "Meta Configuration ID is not configured in backend/.env" | The platform operator has not set up the Meta signup | Contact your platform administrator. Use manual WhatsApp entry only if you have your own credentials |
| Badge stays at "Loading SDK..." | Facebook script blocked (ad blocker, firewall) or the Meta App ID is not configured | Disable blockers for this site; allow facebook.com; refresh; contact admin |
| "Meta Facebook SDK is still loading. Please try again in a few seconds." | You clicked too early | Wait for "Meta SDK Ready" |
| Nothing happens after the Meta popup closes | You cancelled or the browser blocked the popup | Allow popups for the site and launch again |
| "This Meta authorization code was already used or expired..." | One-time code was already used | Click Launch Meta Embedded Signup again |
| "Meta authorization code is required..." | You clicked Save Channel Manually without a code | Launch the popup, or paste a code |
| "META_APP_ID / META_APP_SECRET are not configured..." | Platform operator did not finish Meta setup | Contact your platform administrator |
| "Token exchange failed (...)" | Meta rejected the code | Launch signup again |
| "Could not determine WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) ID from Meta." / "...Phone Number ID from Meta." | The popup did not finish selecting an account or number | Launch again, complete every step, make sure a phone number is added to the account. Or expand Advanced and enter the IDs |
| "Onboarding capacity reached: X/10 in the last 7 days" | Platform-wide limit of 10 new signups per 7 days reached | Wait until an earlier signup is more than 7 days old, then try again; contact support to raise the limit |
| "Insufficient permissions" | You are not an Owner or Admin | Ask an Owner or Admin |
| "type and displayName are required" | Missing name when connecting manually | Fill in the Channel Display Name |
| "Failed to create channel" | Missing/invalid input or server issue | Check each field; try again |
| Settings shows no values, Sync does nothing | Token is wrong, expired or revoked | Reconnect the channel |
| "Failed to fetch templates" / "Meta: ..." in templates | Meta rejected the request | Sync the channel; reconnect if the token expired |
| New template stays PENDING | Awaiting Meta review | Wait; reopen Templates later |
| Template REJECTED | Content breaches Meta rules | Fix wording/category; create a new template with a new name |
| QR & Link shows an error | Phone number or bot username not known | Click Sync in Settings; reconnect if needed |
| Telegram messages do not arrive | Webhook not registered or secret mismatch | See the Telegram notes above; contact your platform administrator |
| Webchat bubble does not show on my site | Widget Inactive, Allowed Domains does not include your site, script not on the page, or an ad blocker | Check Active badge, domain list, and paste the script again |
| "Origin not allowed for this webchat widget" | Your site is not in Allowed Domains | Add the site (or clear the list to allow all) |
| "Webchat widget not found" | The widget was deleted | Create a new one |

title: Flow Builder, AI Knowledge Base and Campaigns
content:
# Flow Builder, AI Knowledge Base and Campaigns
This part of the manual covers the three areas you use to automate conversations and reach your audience at scale:

| Area | Sidebar item | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| Flow Builder | **Flow Builder** | Design automated conversations (menus, questions, AI answers, hand-off to a human) on a visual canvas. |
| AI Knowledge Base | **AI Knowledge Base** | Store your company documents so an AI step in a flow can answer customer questions from them. |
| Campaigns | **Campaigns** | Send a message, a WhatsApp template, a flow, or a timed sequence to many contacts at once and track the results. |

How they connect:

1. You build a **Knowledge Base** (optional) and upload your FAQs, policies and guides.
2. You build a **Flow** that can use the Knowledge Base in an AI step, and you **Publish** it.
3. You attach the published flow to a **channel** (Channels page, "Default Flow") so it answers every incoming conversation, and/or you use it in a **Campaign** to start the flow with many contacts.

## Who can do what

| Action | Owner | Admin | Other roles (for example agents) |
|---|---|---|---|
| View the flow list, open a flow in the editor | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Create, edit/save, publish, delete a flow | Yes | Yes | No (the server rejects the request) |
| Knowledge Bases: create, edit, delete, add or delete documents, test | Yes | Yes | Yes (no role restriction is applied) |
| View the campaign list, campaign details and recipient logs | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Create, send, delete a campaign | Yes | Yes | No |
| Export campaign responses to Excel | Yes | Yes | No (the button is hidden) |

> **Good to know:**
>
> - The Flow Builder and Campaigns pages are visible to every signed-in user in the sidebar. If you are not an Owner or Admin, buttons that change data will show an error message when you click them.

title: Flow Builder: the Flows list
content:
# Flow Builder: the Flows list
## Purpose

The Flows page ("No-Code Flow Builder") lists every automation flow in your workspace. From here you create a new flow (blank or from a template), open a flow in the editor, or delete a flow.

## How to get there

Click **Flow Builder** in the left sidebar. The page is at `/flows`.

## What you see on the page

| Element | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Blank Flow** button (top right) | Opens the "Create Automation Flow" window with the Blank Flow template preselected. |
| **Create from Template** button (top right) | Opens the same window with the first template preselected. |
| **Pre-built Business Flow Templates** banner and **Explore Templates** button | Opens the same window so you can browse templates. The banner says "6 Ready Templates". |
| Flow cards | One card per flow (see below). |
| Empty state ("No flows created yet") | Shown when you have no flows. Offers **Start Blank Flow** and **Pick from Templates**. |

## What a flow card shows

| Item | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Flow name | The name you gave the flow. |
| Status badge | `draft` (yellow) or `published` (green). |
| Version badge (for example `v2`) | Goes up by one every time you publish. |
| "N nodes configured - Entry: node_1" | Number of steps (nodes) and the ID of the starting step. Shows "Entry: None" if no starting step is set. |
| "Updated ..." | Date and time of the last change. |
| **Open Flow Editor** button | Opens the visual editor for this flow. |
| Trash icon ("Delete Flow") | Opens a confirmation window to delete the flow. |

## The six starter templates

| Template | Category | Nodes | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Blank Flow** (badge "Empty Canvas") | General | 1 | One message node saying "Hello! How can we assist you today?". Start from scratch. |
| **Welcome & Onboarding** (badge "Popular") | Marketing | 9 | Greets the contact, asks their full name (saved as `userName`), shows a 1/2/3 menu (products, pricing, support), branches on the answer, hands off to a human for option 3, otherwise ends. |
| **FAQ & Self-Service Menu** (badge "Recommended") | Support | 10 | A 4-option menu (hours and location, shipping, refunds, speak to an agent). Unknown answers apologise and hand off to a human. |
| **Customer Follow-Up & CSAT Survey** (badge "Delayed Queue") | Support | 8 | Thanks the customer, waits 2 hours, asks for a 1 to 5 satisfaction score, thanks 4 and 5, and hands 1 to 3 to a human. |
| **Lead Qualification & Discovery** (badge "B2B Sales") | Sales | 8 | Asks company name and team size. "50+" or "10-50" gets an enterprise message and a hand-off; others get a self-service message and the flow ends. |
| **AI Knowledge Base Support (RAG)** (badge "RAG AI Loop") | AI & Automation | 9 | Asks a question, answers it with the AI Agent step from your Knowledge Base, loops for more questions, and hands off to a human if the AI is not confident or the customer types "agent", "human" or "support". Types "exit", "bye", "done" or "no" end the chat. |

> **Good to know:**
>
> - The AI template comes with no Knowledge Base selected. You must open the AI Agent node and choose one before you can publish.
> - Template text such as prices ("Basic ($29/mo)") and addresses is sample text. Replace it with your own before publishing.

## Create a flow from a template or from scratch

1. Click **Blank Flow** (empty canvas with one message) or **Create from Template**.
2. In the **Create Automation Flow** window, use the category chips **All, General, Support, Sales, Marketing, AI & Automation** to filter. The window shows "N templates available".
3. Click a template card to select it. Each card shows the name, category, description, node count and up to two tags. The selected card is highlighted, and the footer shows "Selected: <template name>".
4. Type a **Flow Name** (required). The name is prefilled from the template (for example "Customer Welcome & Onboarding"). Helper text tells you how many steps the flow starts with.
5. Click **Create Flow**. A message "Flow ... created successfully!" appears and you are taken straight into the editor.
6. Click **Cancel** to close the window without creating anything.

The new flow is created as a **draft** at version 1. It does not answer any customers until you publish it and attach it to a channel.

## Delete a flow

1. Click the trash icon on a flow card (or the trash icon in the editor toolbar).
2. Read the warning: channels using this flow are unlinked, any conversations currently running this flow are marked completed, and historical logs and past analytics remain.
3. Click **Delete Flow** to confirm, or **Cancel**.

> **Good to know:**
>
> - Deleting a flow is done by Owners and Admins only.
> - After deletion, the "Default Flow" on any channel that used it becomes "None (Human inbox only)".
> - If a campaign was created from this flow, the campaign still exists but its flow is no longer available, so sending it will fail with a message that the flow is missing or not published.
