title: Flow Builder: the Flow Editor
content:
# Flow Builder: the Flow Editor
## Purpose

The editor is a visual canvas where you place steps (called **nodes**), connect them with lines (called **connections**), and describe how the conversation moves from step to step.

## How to get there

- From the Flows page, click **Open Flow Editor** on a flow card, or create a new flow.
- From a campaign page, click **View Flow Graph**, **Flow Editor** or **Open**.
- From the new-campaign page, click **Edit in Flow Builder** (opens in a new tab).

## Screen layout

The editor has four areas.

**1. Top toolbar**

| Item | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Flows** (back arrow) | Returns to the flow list. Unsaved changes are not saved automatically. |
| Flow name, status badge, version badge | Shows the name, `draft` or `published`, and `v<number>`. |
| "Entry: <node id>" | The starting step. Shows "None" if none is set. |
| **Node Guide** | Opens the built-in help window (see "The Node Guide" below). |
| Undo / Redo arrows | Step back or forward through changes. See the Notes below. |
| **Save Draft** | Saves the flow as it is on the canvas. Disabled once the flow is `published` (see "Editing a published flow"). |
| **Publish** | Saves and publishes the flow. Disabled if the canvas has no nodes or no entry step. |
| Trash icon | Opens the "Delete Automation Flow" confirmation. |

**2. The canvas (main area)**

- A dotted background. Drag with the mouse to pan, scroll to zoom (zoom range 20% to 200%).
- A **mini-map** in the bottom-right corner for navigation.
- A **Port Color Guide** legend at the top right (blue, green, red, purple; see "Connection colours").
- Each node is a card about 280 pixels wide.

**3. Floating controls (bottom left)**

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Add Node** | Opens a menu of the ten node types (see below). |
| Zoom in (+), Zoom out (-) | Zoom the canvas. |
| Fit to screen | Zooms so the whole flow is visible. |
| Book icon | Opens the Node Guide. |

**4. The node editing window** that opens when you edit a node (described in "Configure each node type").

## Node cards: what you see and click

Each node card has a header and a body.

| Header item | What it does |
|---|---|
| Node ID (for example `message_4821`) | The unique name of the step. Generated automatically from the type plus four digits. It cannot be edited. |
| Type badge | Message, WhatsApp Template, Wait / Retry, Input, Condition, Webhook, AI Agent (RAG), Intent Router, Handoff or End. |
| **ENTRY** tag | Shown on the starting step. |
| Flag icon ("Set as Flow Entry Node") | Makes this node the starting step. Hidden on the node that is already the entry. |
| Pencil icon ("Edit Node") | Opens the node editing window. |
| Trash icon ("Delete Node") | Deletes the node and every connection to and from it. |

The body shows a short summary: message text, template name and header type, wait duration, prompt and variable name, the variable being checked, the webhook address, the Knowledge Base and threshold, and so on.

The bottom of the card has one or more **output ports** (small coloured dots on the right edge). A port represents "what happens next" for one outcome (see below). Every node except the entry node has an **input dot** at the top where lines arrive.

## Create a flow step by step

1. Open the flow (or create one from the Flows page).
2. Click **Add Node** (bottom left) and choose a type. A new node appears near the middle of the canvas with sensible starter settings. Drag it where you want it.
3. Click the pencil icon on the node and fill in its settings (see the per-node sections below). Click **Apply Changes**.
4. Connect the nodes (next section).
5. Decide which node starts the flow (the entry step).
6. Click **Save Draft** (or **Publish** when ready).

If a flow has no nodes yet, the first node you add automatically becomes the entry step.

## Add and connect nodes

There are two ways to connect nodes. Both produce the same result.

**Way 1: drag a line on the canvas**

1. Find the output port (coloured dot, right edge of the card) for the outcome you want.
2. Drag from that dot to the input dot at the top of the next node.
3. A labelled line appears (for example "Continue", "Delivered", "Failed", "== 1", "Default").

**Way 2: choose the target from a list**

1. Open the node's editing window.
2. In the "Next Step" (or "Route To") drop-down, pick the target node. The list shows every other node as `Step: <id> (<type>)`.
3. Click **Apply Changes**. The line appears on the canvas automatically.
4. The first option in each list ("Connect on Canvas ...") means no direct connection from this form; you can still drag a line.

**To remove a connection:**
- Click the line to select it and press **Delete** or **Backspace**; or
- Hover over the line's label and click the small **x** next to it. (If the small x does not respond, use the keyboard method.)

**To delete a node:** click its trash icon, or select it and press **Delete** or **Backspace**.

> **Good to know:**
>
> - Each output port holds one destination. Dragging a second line from the same port to a different node can leave two lines drawn; when you save, only one target per port is kept. Remove the old line first to keep things clear.
> - A flow can loop back to an earlier node (the AI template does this to ask "another question?"). The engine stops a single run after 100 steps in a row without waiting for the customer, so make sure every loop includes a step that waits (Input or Template with buttons).

## Connection colours

| Colour | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Blue | Continue / Next |
| Green | WhatsApp "Delivered" |
| Red, dashed | WhatsApp "Failed" or error |
| Purple | Quick-reply button |
| Orange | Condition branch |
| Grey | Default (nothing matched) |

## Set the entry (starting) step

Exactly one node is the entry. It is where every new conversation begins.

- Click the flag icon on a node, or
- Open the node and click **Set as Entry** in the "Flow Entry Point" panel (it shows "Active Entry" when already set).

If you delete the entry node, the first remaining node becomes the entry automatically. You can change it any time before publishing.

## Variables: the double-curly-brace syntax

Most text fields accept variables written as `{{variable}}`. When the flow runs, each variable is replaced with the real value. Spaces inside the braces are allowed (`{{ contact.name }}`). A variable with no value becomes empty text (nothing is shown, no error).

Variables available in a running flow:

| Variable | What it contains |
|---|---|
| `{{contact.name}}` or `{{name}}` | The contact's name. |
| `{{contact.phone}}` or `{{phone}}` | The contact's phone number / channel ID. |
| `{{contact.email}}` or `{{email}}` | The contact's email, if stored. |
| `{{contact.id}}` | The contact's internal ID. |
| `{{contact.attributes.company}}` or `{{company}}` | Any custom field on the contact (for example from an Excel/CSV import). Use the exact field key. |
| `{{last_message}}` | The text of the customer's most recent message. |
| `{{<name you chose>}}` | Any variable saved by an earlier step: an Input node's "Save Answer As", a Template node's "Save Button Tap As", an AI Agent's "Save Response As", and so on. |
| `{{ai_response}}` | The AI Agent's answer (default name; changeable). |
| `{{ai_response_confidence}}` | The AI Agent's confidence score (0 to 1). If you renamed the response variable, this uses your name plus `_confidence`. |
| `{{detected_intent}}`, `{{detected_sentiment}}` | Set by the Intent Router (defaults; changeable). Sentiment is positive, neutral or negative. |
| `{{detected_intent_confidence}}` | Confidence of the intent detection. |

> **Good to know:**
>
> - Variable names are case-sensitive. `userName` and `username` are different variables.
> - Webhook replies can add more variables (see the Webhook Action node).

## Save, publish and activate

| Concept | How it works |
|---|---|
| **Save Draft** | Stores the canvas (nodes, settings, connections, node positions and the entry step). Shows "Draft flow saved successfully!". |
| **Publish** | Saves first, then publishes. Status becomes `published`, version goes up by 1. Shows "Flow published successfully! It is now active on channels." |
| **Activate** | Publishing alone does not attach the flow to a channel. Go to **Channels**, find the channel card, and pick the flow in the **Default Flow** drop-down. Only published flows are listed. Choose "None (Human inbox only)" to turn automation off for that channel. |
| **Disable** | There is no "unpublish" button. To stop a flow from answering, set the channel's Default Flow to "None (Human inbox only)", or delete the flow. |

What triggers a flow: when a customer sends a message (text, a tapped button, or a WhatsApp catalog order) on a channel that has a Default Flow, and the customer has no flow already in progress, a new run starts at the entry step. If a run is already in progress (for example waiting for an answer), the customer's message continues that run.

After a flow ends (End node, or a step with nothing connected), the next customer message starts it again from the entry step.

After a flow hands the customer to a human (Handoff node), the flow stops answering that conversation. The conversation is marked as needing a human in the Team Inbox. The bot does not restart for that conversation.

If the flow attached to a channel is no longer published (for example deleted), incoming messages simply do not get an automated reply.

## Validation rules (checked when you save and when you publish)

The server checks the flow and refuses to save or publish if any rule fails. A red message appears with the problem.

| Rule | Message you may see |
|---|---|
| The flow must have at least one node. | "Flow definition must contain at least one node" |
| An entry step must be set and must be one of the nodes. | "entryNodeId is required" / "entryNodeId ... is not a node in this flow" |
| Every connection must point to a node that exists. | "Node ... points to unknown node ..." |
| Message node needs text. | "Node ... (message) is missing text" |
| Input node needs a prompt and a variable name. | "(input) is missing prompt" / "(input) is missing saveAs" |
| Condition node needs a variable and at least one branch or a default. | "(condition) is missing variable" / "has no branches or default" |
| Webhook (Action) node needs a URL. | "(action) is missing url" |
| Template node needs a template name; every button needs button text. | "(template) is missing templateName" / "button N is missing buttonText" |
| Wait node needs a duration of zero or more. | "(wait) must have a valid non-negative duration" |
| AI Agent node must have a Knowledge Base selected (checked at publish time only). | "(ai_agent) requires a selected Knowledge Base before publishing" |
| Intent Router needs at least one intent or a default. | "(intent_router) has no branches or default" |
| Node type must be one of the ten supported types. | "has an unknown type" |

> **Good to know:**
>
> - Save Draft does not require an AI Knowledge Base; Publish does.
> - The Publish button is disabled in the toolbar while the canvas is empty or has no entry step.
> - There are no checks for "unreachable" nodes or for nodes with no outgoing connection. A step with nothing after it simply ends the flow.

## Editing a published flow and versions

- Every publish raises the version number (v1, v2, v3...). Only the latest version is kept; there is no version history to browse or roll back.
- Customers are served the **current saved definition** of a flow. Because **Save Draft** is disabled once a flow shows `published`, the way to change a live flow is to edit and click **Publish** again (this saves your edits and publishes them in one step).
- Saving a change to a flow that is already published takes effect for the live flow. The status stays `published`.
- Conversations already in the middle of a flow continue with the updated definition at their current step. If you delete the step a customer is waiting on, that conversation ends on their next message.

## Test and simulate

There is no built-in "run this flow" simulator in the editor. What you can do:

1. **Template preview.** In a WhatsApp Template node, a phone-style preview shows how the message will look. Use the **Sample Data** and **Raw Tags** toggle to see it filled with example values (for example "Alex Johnson") or with the raw `{{...}}` tags.
2. **Knowledge Base test.** In AI Knowledge Base, use the **RAG Playground** to check what the AI will answer (see the Knowledge Base section).
3. **Live test.** Publish the flow, set it as the Default Flow on a test channel (for example a Live Chat or a WhatsApp test number), and send messages from your own phone or the web chat. Watch the conversation in the Team Inbox.

## Undo and redo

The toolbar has Undo and Redo arrows. In the current version these buttons stay greyed out, so they do not undo changes. Use the **x** on lines, the trash icons, or reload the page (before saving) to discard mistakes.

title: Configure each node type
content:
# Configure each node type
Every node opens in the same window: **Configure Node: <node id>**.

Common parts of this window:

| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Node ID** | Read-only. |
| **Step Type** | A drop-down to change the node's type. Changing the type resets the settings that belong to the new type. |
| **Flow Entry Point** panel | Shows "Active Entry" or a **Set as Entry** button. |
| **Delete Node** (red, bottom left) | Deletes this node and its connections. |
| **Cancel** | Closes without changes. |
| **Apply Changes** | Applies the settings to the node on the canvas. Remember to click **Save Draft** or **Publish** afterwards to store them. |

The Step Type drop-down lists: Send Message, WhatsApp Approved Template (Meta), Wait / Delay Queue, User Input, Condition Branch, AI Agent (RAG Knowledge Base), Intent Router (NLU / Classification), Webhook Action, Human Handoff, End Flow.

> **Good to know:**
>
> - Clicking **Apply Changes** only updates the canvas. Nothing is stored until you click **Save Draft** or **Publish**.
> - Applying a node rebuilds its connections from the "Next Step" lists. If you dragged a line on the canvas and then open the node and press **Apply Changes** with the list set to "Connect on Canvas", that line is removed. If you drag lines, prefer to leave the node form alone afterwards, or choose the target in the list too.

## 1. Send Message

**Use it for:** sending a plain text message.

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| **Message Text** | Required. The text to send. Supports variables, for example `Hi {{contact.name}}, here is your update...`. Line breaks are kept. |
| **Next Step (Target Node)** | Which node runs after this message is sent. Optional here; you can connect on the canvas instead. |
| **Max Retry Attempts** | 0 to 10. 0 means no automatic retry. |
| **Retry Delay (Seconds)** | Minimum 5. Wait time between retries. |

Output ports on the canvas:

| Port | When it fires |
|---|---|
| **Continue (Default)** | Right after the message is sent. |
| **On Delivered (WhatsApp)** | When WhatsApp confirms the message reached the customer's phone. |
| **On Failed / Ecosystem Error** | When delivery fails (after the allowed retries). |

How it behaves:
- If you connect **Delivered** or **Failed** (or both), the flow pauses on this message and waits for WhatsApp's delivery report, then follows the matching port. If you only use **Continue**, the flow does not wait and moves on immediately.
- On failure with retries set, the platform waits the retry delay and sends the message again, up to the number of attempts you set; after that it follows the **Failed** port (or ends if nothing is connected).
- A failed message never continues through the **Continue** port.

## 2. WhatsApp Approved Template (Meta)

**Use it for:** official WhatsApp templates (needed to start a conversation or to message a customer after the 24-hour window). The node window is wider and has a live phone preview on the right.

**Left side: configuration**

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| **Meta Approved Template Catalog** | A drop-down of templates with status APPROVED from your connected, active WhatsApp channels. Each entry shows `name (category - language)`. |
| **Sync with Meta** | Reloads the template list from your WhatsApp channels. Use it after creating or approving a template. |
| **Template Name (Manual)** | Shown instead of the drop-down when no approved templates are found. Type the exact template name (for example `order_confirmation_v1`). Required. |
| **Language Code** | For example `en_US`. Filled in when you pick a template. Required. |
| **Save Button Tap As** | Optional variable name. When the customer taps a quick-reply button, the button text is stored in this variable. |
| **Next Step (Default / On Delivered)** | The node that runs when the customer replies with something that is not one of your buttons, or when the template has no buttons. |
| **Template Header Component** | None, Text Header, Image Header, Video Header, or Document / PDF Header. |
| Header file area | For image, video and document headers: **Upload File** (click or drag and drop) or **URL / Variable** (type a link or a `{{variable}}`). Limits: images JPG, PNG or WEBP up to 5 MB; videos MP4 or 3GP up to 16 MB; documents PDF, DOC/DOCX, XLS/XLSX, PPT/PPTX, TXT or CSV up to 100 MB. A text header is just a text box. |
| **Body Parameters Mapping** | Maps each placeholder in the template body (for example `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`) to a value. |
| **Add Param** | Adds another placeholder row. |
| **Select Variable...** drop-down | Inserts a variable: Contact Core (Name, Phone, Email, Contact ID), Custom Attributes (your imported fields), AI and Flow Runtime (Last Message, AI Response, Detected Intent, Detected Sentiment), CRM Deals (Deal Title, Value, Stage; see the note on variables). |
| **Quick Insert Pills** | Click a pill to fill the next empty parameter. |
| **Quick-Reply Button Routing** | **Add Button** adds a row with **Button Text** and **On Tap Route To** (target node). Each button becomes its own port (`btn_0`, `btn_1`, ...). |
| **Max Retry Attempts / Retry Delay (Seconds)** | Same as for Send Message. |

**Right side: live preview**

- A phone-style WhatsApp bubble with your header, body, footer, buttons and the default next step.
- **Sample Data** replaces variables with examples; **Raw Tags** shows the tags as typed.

When you pick an approved template the form fills itself: the language, the header type, the numbered or named placeholders found in the body, and one button row for each button the template has. You then map each placeholder to a value and choose where each button goes.

> **Good to know:**
>
> - Every button needs button text, or the flow cannot be saved.
> - If a template has buttons, the flow pauses after sending and waits for the customer's tap or reply.
> - A template parameter row is only saved if both the placeholder and its value are filled in.
> - If you set Header "Image/Video/Document", provide a file or a link, otherwise WhatsApp may reject the message.

Output ports: **Continue (Default)**, **On Delivered (WhatsApp)**, **On Failed / Ecosystem Error**, plus one purple port per quick-reply button.

Behaviour summary:
- Template with buttons: waits for the customer's reply; a matching button follows that button's port, any other reply follows **Continue**.
- Template with no buttons and no Delivered/Failed connections: moves on immediately via **Continue**.
- Template with **Delivered**/**Failed** connections and no buttons: waits for the delivery report first.

## 3. Wait / Delay Queue

**Use it for:** pausing the flow, for example "wait 2 hours, then ask for feedback".

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| **Duration Value** | Required. A number, minimum 1 in the form. |
| **Unit** | Seconds, Minutes, Hours or Days. |
| **After Delay Route To** | The node to continue with after the delay. |

Output port: **Next Step** (the only one).

How it behaves:
- The platform schedules the rest of the flow for the chosen time. It survives restarts and the conversation stays open for your team.
- **A Wait node must be connected to a next step.** If nothing is connected after the Wait node, the flow simply ends there (it does not wait).
- When the timer ends, the flow resumes at the connected step. A new Wait node starts with 3600 seconds (1 hour) when you add it.
- Customers can still write to you during the wait, and your team can still reply in the Team Inbox.
> **Good to know:** if the customer sends a message while the flow is waiting, the Wait step is reached again, so the delay may be scheduled again. Avoid depending on exact timing when customers are likely to write during a long wait, and test this case.

## 4. User Input

**Use it for:** asking a question and storing the answer.

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| **Prompt Question** | Required. The question sent to the customer. Supports variables. |
| **Save Answer As (Variable)** | Required. A name such as `userEmail`. Later steps use it as `{{userEmail}}`. |
| **After Answer Received Route To** | The next node after the customer answers. |

Output port: **Next Step**.

How it behaves: the flow sends the question and pauses. The customer's next message is saved under the variable name and the flow continues. The reply is stored as typed; it is not checked for format (no email or number validation).

## 5. Condition Branch

**Use it for:** choosing a path based on a saved value.

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| **Variable Name to Evaluate** | Required. The name of a variable (without braces), for example `userChoice`. |
| **Branch Equality Rules** | A list. **Add Branch** adds a rule. Each rule has a **value to match** (for example `1`, `Yes`) and **If Matches Route To**. The ports are named `branch_0`, `branch_1`, ... |
| **Default (Else / No Match)** | The node to use when no rule matches. |

Output ports: one per rule ("If equals ...") plus **Default Fallback**.

How it behaves:
- Rules are checked from top to bottom; the first match wins.
- Matching ignores upper/lower case and extra spaces at the ends. It matches the **whole value** exactly (the reply "yes please" does not match a rule "yes").
- There are no "contains", "greater than" or similar operators; only "equals".
- Rules with an empty value are dropped when you apply the node.
- If no rule matches and no default is connected, the flow ends.

## 6. AI Agent (RAG Knowledge Base)

**Use it for:** answering customer questions from your AI Knowledge Base.

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| **Knowledge Base Source** | Required before publishing. A drop-down of your Knowledge Bases, shown as `name (N docs, model)`. If the list is empty, a link to **AI Knowledge Base** is shown. |
| **Query Variable** | Which variable contains the customer's question. Default `last_message` (the customer's latest message). |
| **Save Response As** | Name for the answer variable. Default `ai_response`. |
| **System Persona & Prompt Override (Optional)** | Extra instructions for this step only (for example "Keep answers under 3 sentences"). If blank, the Knowledge Base's own instruction is used. Supports variables. |
| **On Answer Generated Route To** | The node after a successful answer (port "Answered"). |
| **Confidence Fallback Threshold** | A slider from 0.00 to 1.00 in steps of 0.05. Default 0.20. |
| **Automatically send response message directly...** | Checkbox, on by default. When on, the AI's answer is sent to the customer. When off, the answer is only saved in the variable so another node can send it (for example a Send Message with `{{ai_response}}`). |

Output ports: **Answered (High Conf)** and **On Fallback (< threshold)**.

How it behaves:
- The platform finds the most relevant passages in the chosen Knowledge Base, asks the AI to answer using only those passages, and saves the answer and a confidence score.
- If the confidence is lower than the threshold **and** the **Fallback** port is connected, the flow follows Fallback (usually to a Human Handoff). Otherwise it follows **Answered**.
- Note that when "send automatically" is on, the answer is still sent even if confidence is low, before the flow takes the Fallback path.
- If the Knowledge Base is missing, inactive, the question is empty, or an error occurs, the flow follows Fallback when connected, otherwise Answered.

Lower threshold means the AI answers more often; higher means stricter (more hand-offs). 0.20 to 0.35 is a typical starting range (the AI template uses 0.35).

## 7. Intent Router (NLU / Classification)

**Use it for:** sending the customer down different paths depending on what they want (sales, support, billing and so on).

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| **Input Variable** | The variable holding the customer's message. Default `last_message`. |
| **Intent Branches & Destinations** | **Add Intent** adds a row: an **intent name** (for example `sales`, `support`, `pricing`, `billing`, `speak_to_human`) and **On Match Route To**. Ports are `intent_0`, `intent_1`, ... New routers start with "support" and "sales". |
| **Default (No Intent Matched)** | Node to use when no intent matches. |
| **Save Detected Intent As** | Variable name, default `detected_intent`. |
| **Save Detected Sentiment As** | Variable name, default `detected_sentiment` (positive / neutral / negative). |

Output ports: one per intent plus **Unrecognized / Default**.

How it behaves:
- The message is classified by the platform's AI and the detected intent is compared (ignoring case) with your intent names. The first match is followed.
- If nothing matches, or the AI cannot classify, the **Default** port is followed (or the flow ends if Default is empty).
- Use the same words as the intent names the classifier returns. Test with a few real sentences to confirm your names match.
- Rows with an empty intent name are dropped when you apply the node.

## 8. Webhook Action

**Use it for:** telling another system something happened (CRM, order system, spreadsheet service).

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| **Webhook URL** | Required. Example `https://api.example.com/webhook`. Supports variables in the address. |
| **On Webhook Success Route To** | The node to continue with. |

Output port: **Next Step**.

How it behaves:
- The platform sends a POST request with all current flow variables in JSON form (`{ "variables": { ... } }`) and waits up to 5 seconds.
- If the other system answers with a success code and JSON, each top-level key in that JSON is added to the flow's variables, so later steps can use it, for example `{{orderStatus}}`.
- If the call fails (error code or no reply in time) the flow still continues along the next step (there is no separate failure port in the editor).
- Only POST is used.

## 9. Human Handoff

**Use it for:** passing the conversation to your team.

No fields. Place it where the customer should reach a person (for example when the AI falls back or the customer types "agent").

How it behaves:
- The flow stops and the conversation is marked as pending/needing a human in the Team Inbox.
- The bot does not answer that conversation again.
- It has no output port.
- Any messages queued before the Handoff in the same pass (for example a "Please hold on" message) are sent first.

## 10. End Flow

**Use it for:** finishing the flow cleanly. No fields, no output port. A node that has nothing connected after it also ends the flow, but an explicit End step makes the design clear.

title: Flow Builder: common errors and fixes
content:
# Flow Builder: common errors and fixes
| What you see | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "Failed to load flows" | Network or server problem. | Refresh the page; try again. |
| Publish button is greyed out | No nodes, or no entry step. | Add a node; mark one as entry with the flag icon. |
| "Cannot publish an invalid flow" followed by a list | One or more validation rules failed. | Read each line, open the named node, and complete the missing field or connection. |
| "Node ... points to unknown node ..." | A connection refers to a deleted node. | Re-connect or remove the connection in the node's Next Step list. |
| "(ai_agent) requires a selected Knowledge Base before publishing" | The AI Agent has no Knowledge Base. | Create one in AI Knowledge Base, then pick it in the node. |
| Save Draft is greyed out | The flow is already published. | Click **Publish** to save and publish your changes together. |
| Permission/forbidden error on save, publish or delete | Your role is not Owner or Admin. | Ask an Owner or Admin. |
| Template drop-down is empty | No WhatsApp channel is connected and active, or no templates are approved. | Connect your WhatsApp channel, click **Sync with Meta**, or type the template name manually. |
| Customers get no automatic reply | Flow not published, or not set as the channel's Default Flow, or the conversation was already handed to a human. | Publish; set Default Flow in Channels; check whether the conversation was handed off. |
| A flow seems to stop after the first message | The Message node has nothing connected after it. | Connect Next Step. |
| A Wait node does nothing | No next step is connected. | Connect "After Delay Route To". |
| A Condition never matches | The variable name or value does not match exactly. | Use the exact variable name; check the saved value (whole-value match, case ignored). |
| Variables show as empty text | The variable was never set or is spelled differently. | Check the name; make sure the Input/AI/Intent step runs earlier on that path. |
| Conversation hands off but the customer keeps getting bot messages | Not expected after a Handoff node. | Check whether the Default Flow was changed or a campaign flow restarted for the contact. |

## Best practices (supported by the editor's Node Guide and the behaviour above)

- Always connect the **Default** port of Condition and Intent Router nodes so customers never get stuck.
- Connect the AI Agent **Fallback** port to a Human Handoff.
- Use WhatsApp **Template** nodes, not plain messages, to re-contact customers after the 24-hour WhatsApp window (for example after a long Wait).
- Set the entry step before publishing.
- For menus, put the options in a Send Message, then use an Input node to capture the choice and a Condition node to branch (the Welcome and FAQ templates are built this way).

title: AI Knowledge Base
content:
# AI Knowledge Base
## Purpose

A **Knowledge Base** is a private library of your own documents (FAQs, policies, product guides, price lists). The platform splits each document into small passages and indexes them. When the **AI Agent** node in a flow (or the RAG Playground) receives a question, it finds the best passages and builds an answer from them.

Each Knowledge Base belongs to your workspace only. Other businesses cannot see it.

## How to get there

Click **AI Knowledge Base** in the sidebar (page title "Knowledge Bases & AI Agent RAG", address `/knowledge-bases`).

## Page layout

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Header buttons | **Refresh** reloads the list. **New Knowledge Base** opens the create window. |
| Four summary cards | **Knowledge Bases** (count), **Indexed Documents** (total documents), **Vector Chunks** (total passages), **Embedding Pipeline** (fixed label "text-embedding-3"). |
| **Knowledge Repositories** (left) | A searchable list of your Knowledge Bases. The search box filters by name and description. Each entry shows the name, an "Inactive" badge if switched off, the description, the number of docs and chunks, and the provider (for example "claude"). It has **Edit** (pencil) and **Delete** (trash) icons. |
| Workspace (right) | Shows the selected Knowledge Base with three tabs: **Documents**, **RAG Playground**, **Settings**. The first Knowledge Base is selected automatically. |

If you have none, the list says "No knowledge bases found. Click '+ New Knowledge Base' to create your first repository."

## Create a Knowledge Base

1. Click **New Knowledge Base**.
2. Fill in the window:

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| **Knowledge Base Name \*** | Required. For example "Product FAQs", "Pricing Policy". |
| **Description** | Optional short note about what is inside. |
| **System Instruction Prompt** | The standing instruction given to the AI. Prefilled with: "You are an expert AI customer support assistant. Answer the user query strictly using the provided context. If the answer cannot be found in the context, politely clarify or state that you will connect them with a human specialist." Edit it to match your tone, language and rules. |
| **AI Provider** | Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, or Deterministic Offline Engine. |
| **Model** | Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3 Haiku (Fast), GPT-4o Mini, or Offline Vector Matcher. |
| **Active (Enabled for bot flows and RAG search)** | Checked by default. Untick to switch it off without deleting. |

3. Click **Create Knowledge Base**. The new Knowledge Base is selected, ready for documents.

To change any of these later, click the pencil icon, edit and click **Update Knowledge Base**. The **Settings** tab only displays these values; changes are made through the pencil icon.

> **Good to know:**
>
> - If you leave the System Instruction empty, the platform uses: "You are a helpful customer support AI assistant. Ground your answers strictly on the provided knowledge base context."
> - Temperature is fixed at 0.2 when created in the window (low = consistent, factual answers) and cannot be changed in this screen.
> - An **inactive** Knowledge Base stops answering: AI Agent steps and the playground report that it is inactive, and the flow follows the Fallback path.
> - The provider setting depends on how your platform is configured (API keys). If the real AI service is not available, the platform falls back to a simpler built-in answer builder, so answers may be plainer or just excerpts of your documents. The "Anthropic Claude" option stores the value `claude`; if answers look like simple excerpts, ask your platform administrator to confirm the AI provider is set up.
> - Embeddings (the passage index) use OpenAI when an OpenAI key is configured; otherwise a built-in method that works best when the customer's wording shares words with your documents.

## Add documents

1. Select a Knowledge Base, open the **Documents** tab, and click **Add Document** (or **Ingest First Document** if it is empty).
2. In the **Ingest Knowledge Document** window, fill in:

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| **Document Title \*** | Required. For example "Return & Exchange Policy 2026". Up to 200 characters are kept when uploading a file. |
| **Source Type** | **Plain Text**, **Markdown Documentation**, **PDF Document**, or **Web Page / URL**. |
| **Source URL** | Appears only for Web Page / URL. Stored as a reference only (see the note). |
| **Upload File** | Appears for Markdown (.md, .markdown, .txt) and PDF (.pdf). Click to choose or drag and drop. Maximum 10 MB. The file name (without extension) becomes the title if you did not type one. |
| **Document Content \*** | For text, markdown and URL types: paste the text here. When you upload a markdown/text file, this box shows a read-only preview. For a PDF, no preview is shown because the text is read on the server. A counter shows characters and the approximate number of chunks. |

3. Click **Vectorize & Save Document**. A message shows "Created document with N chunks". The list refreshes and the chunk totals update.

Supported ways to add content:

| Source Type | How to add | Limits and notes |
|---|---|---|
| Plain Text | Paste text, or upload a .txt file under Markdown | Content must not be empty. |
| Markdown | Paste, or upload .md / .markdown / .txt | Max 10 MB; the file must not be empty. |
| PDF | Upload a .pdf (or paste the extracted text) | Max 10 MB. Must be a real text-based PDF. Scanned/image-only PDFs have no readable text and are rejected. Password-protected or damaged PDFs are rejected. |
| Web Page / URL | Paste the page's text and optionally enter the URL | **The platform does not download the web page.** Only the text you paste is indexed; the URL is kept as a label. Copy the page content into the Content box. |

> **Good to know:**
>
> - For file uploads, the file name extension must match the Source Type (for example a .pdf for PDF). A wrong type shows "Unsupported file. Please choose a ... file".
> - Empty files show "That file is empty". Files over 10 MB show "File is too large ... Maximum size is 10 MB".
> - A PDF always counts as type "pdf". For text files, your choice between Markdown and Plain Text is respected.
> - DOCX, Excel, images and other formats are not supported. Convert to PDF, text or Markdown first.

## How documents are processed

1. The document is saved with status **indexing**.
2. The text is split into passages (chunks) of about 600 characters with an 80-character overlap, breaking at paragraphs and sentences where possible. Very short fragments (10 characters or fewer) are dropped.
3. Each passage is turned into a numeric "fingerprint" (1,536 numbers) used for similarity search.
4. When all passages are stored, the status becomes **indexed** and the chunk count is saved.
5. If something goes wrong, the status becomes **failed** and an error message is shown.

Document statuses:

| Status | Meaning | Visible in the list? |
|---|---|---|
| `indexing` | Being split and indexed. Normally lasts moments. | Not shown as a label. |
| `indexed` | Ready; the AI can use it. | The row shows "N vector chunks" with a green check. |
| `failed` | Indexing stopped with an error. | Not labelled in the list. A failed document may appear with "0 vector chunks". Delete it and add it again. |

The list shows for each document: an icon for its type, the title, a type badge (text, markdown, pdf, url), "N vector chunks", and "Added <date>". Most recent documents come first. There is no "edit" for a document: to change content, delete the document and add it again.

## Delete a document or a Knowledge Base

- **Delete a document:** click the trash icon on the row, confirm **Delete Document**. Its passages are removed.
- **Delete a Knowledge Base:** click the trash icon on its card, confirm **Delete Knowledge Base**. All documents and passages are permanently removed.

> **Good to know:**
>
> - If a flow's AI Agent node points to a deleted Knowledge Base, the node can no longer answer and will follow Fallback. Update the node to another Knowledge Base.

## How the AI uses your documents

1. The customer's message (or the variable chosen in the AI Agent's **Query Variable**) is turned into a fingerprint.
2. All passages in the Knowledge Base are compared with it and scored from 0 to 1.
3. Passages scoring at least the **similarity threshold** (default 0.25) are kept, best first, up to **Top-K** (default 4).
4. The AI receives your **System Instruction** (or the AI Agent node's override), the selected passages as "grounding context", and up to the last four earlier messages of the chat, then writes an answer.
5. The **confidence** is the average similarity of the passages used. The AI Agent node compares it with its **Confidence Fallback Threshold**.
6. Each question and answer is recorded in the AI activity log for your workspace.

Tips that follow from this:
- Write documents in the words your customers use; the search favours passages with similar wording.
- Keep one topic per document or per paragraph. Passages break at blank lines.
- Add a document for every common question; unanswered topics lead to the "could not find specific information" reply and a low confidence.

## RAG Playground (test chat)

Use this tab to test a Knowledge Base before connecting it to a flow.

1. Select the Knowledge Base and open **RAG Playground**.
2. Type a question in **User Query** (for example "How do I request a refund?").
3. Adjust the sliders if you want:
   - **Top-K Context Chunks** (1 to 8, default 4): how many passages the AI may use.
   - **Similarity Threshold** (0.10 to 0.80, default 0.25): minimum match score to keep a passage.
4. Click **Ask RAG** (or press Enter) for a full answer, or **Vector Search** to only see the matching passages.

**Ask RAG results ("Grounded AI Synthesis"):** the written answer, a **Confidence** percentage, **Latency** in milliseconds, and "Attributed Grounding Sources", the passages used with their document title and match percentage.

**Vector Search results ("Ranked Vector Matches"):** the best passages, with chunk numbers. The number of results follows the Top-K slider.

> **Good to know:**
>
> - The playground uses the Knowledge Base's own System Instruction.
> - Vector Search uses only the Top-K value; the threshold slider applies to Ask RAG.
> - Playground questions are recorded in the AI activity log, like real ones.
> - Match percentages for Vector Search may not display in some versions. Compare the order of the passages instead.

## Settings tab

Shows (read-only): System Instruction Prompt, LLM Provider, Model Name, Sampling Temperature, and Status ("Active & Serving" or "Inactive"). To change them, click the pencil icon on the Knowledge Base card.

## Connect a Knowledge Base to a flow

1. In the Flow Editor, add an **AI Agent (RAG)** node.
2. Choose the Knowledge Base in **Knowledge Base Source**.
3. Set the threshold, connect **Answered** and **On Fallback**.
4. Publish the flow and set it as a channel's Default Flow.

## Knowledge Base: common errors and fixes

| What you see | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "Name is required" | Name left empty. | Enter a name. |
| "Title is required" | Document title empty. | Enter a title. |
| "Upload a file or paste the content" / "Content is required" | Nothing to index. | Upload a file or paste text. |
| "File is too large ... Maximum size is 10 MB" | File larger than 10 MB. | Split the file or reduce its size. |
| "No text could be extracted from this PDF. It looks like a scanned/image-only document" | The PDF is a picture of text. | Use a text-based PDF, or paste the text. |
| "Could not read this PDF. It may be corrupted or password-protected" | Damaged or locked PDF. | Remove the password or re-export. |
| "The file is not a valid PDF document" | A renamed non-PDF file. | Upload a real PDF. |
| "Unsupported file type. Upload a .md, .markdown, .txt or .pdf file" | Wrong format. | Convert the file. |
| AI says it could not find information | No passage met the similarity threshold. | Add a document covering the topic, rephrase in the customers' words, or lower the threshold. |
| "Knowledge base ... is currently inactive" | The Active box is off. | Edit the Knowledge Base and tick Active. |
| Node says "Not Configured" for the KB | No Knowledge Base chosen. | Open the AI Agent node and choose one. |

---

title: Campaigns
content:
# Campaigns
## Purpose

Campaigns let you reach many contacts at once. There are three campaign types:

| Type (as shown) | What it sends |
|---|---|
| **Flow Builder Automation** (type "flow") | Starts a published flow with every contact in the audience (for example a template message with buttons followed by questions). |
| **Direct Broadcast** (type "broadcast") | One message to everyone: either an approved **WhatsApp template** (with media header, variables and buttons) or a **plain text** message. |
| **Timed Drip Sequence** (type "drip") | A series of text messages spaced out by a number of hours. |

## How to get there

- Click **Campaigns** in the sidebar (list at `/campaigns`).
- Click **Create Campaign** (top right) to start a new one (`/campaigns/new`).
- Quick links to the new-campaign page also appear on the Dashboard and on the Contacts page.

## The Campaigns list

| Element | Details |
|---|---|
| Three summary cards | **Ready / Draft Campaigns**, **Currently Sending**, **Completed Executions**. |
| **Type** filter | All Types, Flow Builder, broadcast, drip. |
| **Status** filter | all, draft, sending, completed. (Campaigns with the statuses partially failed or failed appear under "all".) |
| Campaign card | Name (click to open details), status badge, type badge, "sent / total recipients", "N not delivered" (if any), created date, audience tags, a progress bar ("N% accepted by provider") once the campaign is no longer a draft. |
| Content preview | For flows: the flow ID and **View Flow Graph**. For broadcasts: the message text. For drips: the first two steps with "+Nh". |
| **Analytics** button | Opens the campaign details page. |
| **Send Now** button | Only for campaigns in **draft** status. Asks "Are you sure you want to execute and send this campaign now?" then sends. |
| Trash icon | Deletes the campaign (after confirmation). |

If you have no campaigns, the page offers **Create First Campaign**.

## Campaign statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `draft` | Created, not yet sent ("Ready"). |
| `sending` | The send is in progress. |
| `completed` | The send finished and no recipient failed. |
| `partially failed` | The send finished and some, but not all, recipients failed. |
| `failed` | The send finished and every recipient failed (or the send was interrupted with nothing sent). |

For broadcast and flow campaigns, the status is recalculated from live recipient counts after sending, because delivery receipts keep arriving. A campaign first shown as completed can later change to partially failed or failed if WhatsApp reports messages as undelivered.

There is **no pause, cancel or schedule-for-later option**. Once a broadcast or flow campaign is sent, it runs through its list; to stop it, there is no stop button. Deleting the campaign removes it and its tracking.

> **Good to know:**
>
> - Drip campaigns work differently: see the Drip section for how they start and what their status shows.

## Recipient statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pending` | Waiting to be sent (or, for drips, waiting for the next step time). |
| `sent` | Accepted by the messaging provider; no delivery report yet. |
| `delivered` | The provider confirmed delivery to the phone. |
| `read` | The customer read it. |
| `completed` | (Drips) every step has been sent. Delivery receipts are not tracked for drips. |
| `failed` | Not delivered. Shown to you as "Not delivered" with the reason. |

title: Create a campaign
content:
# Create a campaign
Go to **Campaigns** then **Create Campaign**. The page "Create New Campaign" has three sections and a **Create Campaign** button (top right) plus **Create & Prepare Campaign (N Recipients)** at the bottom, and a **Cancel** button.

## Section 1: Campaign Execution Mode

1. Click one of three cards: **Flow Builder Automation**, **Direct Broadcast**, **Timed Drip Sequence**.
2. Enter a **Campaign Name** (required), for example "Festival Offer Broadcast - WhatsApp".
3. Choose the **Target Channel** from the drop-down. Each entry shows the channel name, its type, and, for WhatsApp, its daily message tier (for example "250 / 24h"). The first channel is selected by default.

## Section 2: Content (depends on the type)

### A. Flow Builder Automation

1. In **Choose Published Flow Automation**, pick a flow. The list shows `name (Published or Draft - version)`. A published flow is preselected if one exists.
2. A green summary card shows the node count, the entry node, the status badge, and counts of template nodes, wait/retry nodes, conditions and handoffs/actions. **Edit in Flow Builder** opens the flow in a new tab.
3. Choose a **published** flow. A campaign using a draft flow can be created but cannot be sent (see the errors table).

If you have no flows, a notice reminds you to design one in Flow Builder first.

What happens at send time: for each contact, the platform opens (or reuses) a conversation on the chosen channel and runs the flow from its entry step. Typically the entry step is a **WhatsApp Template** node. If a customer later answers questions in the flow, their answers are recorded per recipient (see "Export responses").

If a contact is already in the middle of the same flow, the platform does not restart it; it attaches the contact's existing run to this campaign. If the contact has been handed to a human, nothing is sent and the recipient is shown as "Not sent: conversation is handed off to a human agent".

### B. Direct Broadcast

On a **WhatsApp** channel you see two options:

| Option | Details |
|---|---|
| **WhatsApp HSM Template (Recommended)** | Send an approved template. Needed to reach contacts outside the 24-hour customer-service window. |
| **Plain Text Broadcast** | Send ordinary text. |

On other channels (not WhatsApp) only plain text is available.

**Template broadcast**

1. **Select Approved Meta Template.** The drop-down lists the approved templates of the selected channel as `name (category - language)`, with the count "N approved templates available". The first one is selected for you. While loading you see "Loading templates from Meta...". If none exist you see "No Approved Templates Found": sync templates in Channel Settings or create them in Meta Business Suite.
2. **Template Header** (only if the template has an image, video, document or text header): upload a file or enter a link or `{{variable}}`. Same limits as in the flow editor: image 5 MB (JPG/PNG/WEBP), video 16 MB (MP4/3GP), document 100 MB. For a text header, type the text.
3. **Template Body Parameters.** One input per placeholder (`{{1}}`, `{{2}}`...). Type fixed text, or a variable. Parameter `{{1}}` is prefilled with `{{name}}`. The link **Use Contact Name ({{name}})** sets the value to the contact's name.
4. **Live WhatsApp HSM Preview.** A phone-style card shows header, body, footer and buttons. In the preview `{{name}}` appears as "Alex".

Variables you can use in broadcast text, parameters and header values (replaced separately for each contact):

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `{{name}}` or `{{contact.name}}` | Contact name. |
| `{{phone}}` or `{{contact.phone}}` | Contact phone. |
| `{{email}}` or `{{contact.email}}` | Contact email. |
| `{{contact.attributes.<field>}}` or `{{<field>}}` | Any custom contact field, for example `{{company}}`. |

**Plain text broadcast**

1. Type the **Message Text**. Use `{{name}}` to personalise (for example "Hi {{name}}, we are excited to announce..."). A **Sample Preview (Interpolated)** shows the result with "Alex".

### C. Timed Drip Sequence

A drip is a series of text messages.

1. Two steps are prefilled ("Hi {{name}}, welcome to our platform!" at 0 hours and "Hi {{name}}, just checking in to see if you had any questions." at 24 hours).
2. For each step, set **Delay** (hours after the previous step; a whole number, minimum 0) and type the message (required).
3. Click **Add Next Drip Step** to add more (new steps default to 48 hours). The trash icon removes a step (only when there is more than one).
4. At least one step is required.

How timing works: the delay counts from when the **previous** step was sent. The first step goes out as soon as the platform's scheduler checks (about every 30 seconds), regardless of the delay typed on step 1. Later steps wait the number of hours you set. A step can arrive up to about half a minute late.

## Section 3: Target Audience Selection

A badge at the top shows **Targeted Audience: N Contacts**, updated live.

Only contacts that belong to the **selected channel** can be chosen. Changing the channel changes the list.

| Mode | How to use it |
|---|---|
| **Filter by Tags** | Click one or more tag chips (for example #followup, #vip, #lead). A contact is included if it has **any** of the selected tags (not all). Tags are matched ignoring case. Click **All Contacts (No Tag Filter)** to target everyone on the channel. The text shows "Matching N contacts from database". The link **Manage Contacts & Tags** opens the Contacts page. The chip list always includes followup, up, mp, vip, lead plus every tag found in your contacts. |
| **Manual Contact Selection** | A scrollable list of contacts with a checkbox, name, phone/ID and up to three tags. Click rows to select. **Select All** or **Deselect All** applies to the channel's contacts. The count shows "N contacts selected manually". |

> **Good to know:**
>
> - The page loads up to 2,000 contacts. Audiences are built from those contacts.
> - In Manual mode, switching to Tags mode keeps your manual ticks stored but uses the tag filter.
> - An audience must contain at least one contact, or you see "No contacts match the selected audience criteria. Add contacts or select different tags."
> - Each contact appears once per campaign even if selected twice.

## WhatsApp daily messaging limit panel

For WhatsApp channels, a panel "WhatsApp 24h Messaging Tier Capacity" compares your audience with the channel's limit on business-initiated conversations in 24 hours.

| Tier | Limit per rolling 24 hours |
|---|---|
| Tier 50 | 50 contacts |
| Tier 250 (assumed when the tier is unknown) | 250 contacts |
| Tier 1K | 1,000 contacts |
| Tier 10K | 10,000 contacts |
| Tier 100K | 100,000 contacts |
| Tier Unlimited | No cap |

| Panel state | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Purple / green ("well within your 24-hour messaging capacity ... Meta Health: Green") | Under 80% of the limit. |
| Amber "Approaching 24-Hour Tier Limit" | At 80% or more of the limit; shows how many contacts remain. |
| Red "Audience Exceeds WhatsApp 24-Hour Tier Capacity" | Audience larger than the limit. Messages above the limit are rejected by Meta (errors 131048 / 131056). The button changes to "Create Campaign (N Recipients - Exceeds Tier)". |

Suggested actions shown by the panel when exceeded: filter by tag to shrink the audience, use a Timed Drip to spread messages over days, or raise your tier by completing Meta Business Verification.

The page warns you but does not block creation when the limit is exceeded.

## Create the campaign

1. Check that name, channel, content and audience are correct.
2. Click **Create & Prepare Campaign (N Recipients)** (or **Create Campaign** at the top).
3. You see "Campaign ... created with N recipients!" and return to the list. The campaign is saved as a **draft** (broadcast and flow) with every recipient `pending`. Nothing is sent yet.

Validation messages:

| Message | Fix |
|---|---|
| "Please enter a campaign name" | Type a name. |
| "Please select a channel" | Choose a channel. |
| "Please select a visual Flow for this campaign" | Choose a flow (Flow type). |
| "Please select a WhatsApp template for this broadcast" | Pick an approved template. |
| "Please enter a broadcast message" | Type the text. |
| "Please add at least one drip step" | Add a step. |
| "No contacts match the selected audience criteria..." | Select different tags or contacts. |
| "channelId, name, and type are required" | Required data missing; reload and retry. |
| "flow campaign requires a valid flowId" | Choose a flow. |
| "No contacts match the specified audience criteria or tag filter" | The audience is empty on the server. |
| "channelId or one of contactIds does not refer to an existing record" | The channel or a contact no longer exists; refresh. |

## Scheduling and throttling

- **Scheduling:** there is no date/time scheduling for broadcast or flow campaigns. They are sent when you click **Send Now**. For time-spread delivery, use a **Timed Drip Sequence** (delay in hours between steps).
- **Throttling:** broadcast and flow campaigns send one recipient at a time with a short pause (about a quarter of a second) between recipients. Large audiences take time; keep the page or leave it open and watch progress on the details page. There is no rate setting for you to change.

---

title: Launch (send) a campaign
content:
# Launch (send) a campaign
## Broadcast and Flow campaigns

1. Open **Campaigns**. Find the draft campaign.
2. Click **Send Now** (on the list or on the details page).
3. Confirm "Send Broadcast".
4. Wait while the status changes to **sending**. At the end you see "Campaign sent successfully! (N sent, M failed)". The status becomes completed, partially failed or failed.

Who can send: Owners and Admins.

Before sending, the platform checks:
- The channel exists and is connected.
- For flow campaigns (or broadcasts that run a flow), the flow exists and is **published**. Otherwise: "Flow ... is missing or not published. Please publish the flow before launching the campaign."
- Only recipients with status `pending` are processed. Sending the campaign a second time only affects recipients that are still `pending`, because already-sent recipients are skipped.

During the send, each recipient receives their personalised message. If one recipient fails, the others still go out.

## Drip campaigns

- Drip campaigns have **no Send Now step in practice**: once created, the first step is due immediately and is picked up by the background scheduler within about 30 seconds, then later steps follow at their delays.
- A drip campaign's status badge is not updated by this process (it stays at the status it was created with, usually draft). Judge progress by the recipient counts, the "Current Step" column and the "Completed" counter.
- The **Send Now** button may appear on a drip campaign that is still marked draft. For drips it is not the way to start the sequence and shows an error such as "Only broadcast and flow campaigns can be triggered".

> **Good to know:**
>
> - Drip messages are text only. Template or button drips are not available; use a Flow campaign instead.
> - The drip step message is stored from the form as "message". If recipients receive empty drip messages after your first test, report it to your platform administrator before running a large drip.

## Pause, resume, cancel

There is no pause, resume or cancel command for any campaign type. The available controls are:
- **Delete** a campaign (removes the campaign and its recipient tracking; messages already sent cannot be recalled). For a drip, deleting stops further steps.

title: Campaign details and results
content:
# Campaign details and results
## How to get there

Click a campaign's name or its **Analytics** button.

## Header

- Campaign name, status badge, type badge.
- Channel name, creation date, and audience tags.
- Buttons:

| Button | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Refresh** | Reloads numbers and the recipient table ("Analytics refreshed"). |
| **Export responses (Excel)** | Only for Owners/Admins and only for campaigns that use a flow. Downloads an .xlsx file (see below). |
| **Flow Editor** | Opens the campaign's flow (flow campaigns). |
| **Send Now** | Only for drafts. |
| **Delete** | Opens a confirmation, then removes the campaign. |

The page refreshes itself every 10 seconds while the campaign is sending or while any message is still queued or waiting for a delivery report. It pauses when the browser tab is hidden.

## Number cards (KPIs)

| Card | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Audience** | Total targeted contacts. |
| **Delivery Rate** | Percent of the audience whose delivery the provider confirmed (delivered plus read). Under it: percent accepted by the provider. |
| **Delivered** | Count confirmed delivered or read; also shows how many were read, how many are sent and awaiting a receipt, and how many completed (drip). |
| **In Queue** | Waiting or scheduled recipients, with percent. |
| **Not delivered** | Failed recipients with percent of the audience. |

## Delivery Execution Funnel

A stacked colour bar and legend: **Read** (dark green), **Delivered** (green), **Completed** (teal), **Sent (no receipt)** (blue), **In Queue** (amber), **Not delivered** (grey). It also says "N of M accepted by provider".

## "Why messages were not delivered"

Appears when there are failures. It groups failures by provider error code and reason, with a short explanation and a count ("12 messages"). Up to the ten most common reasons are shown.

## Drip Sequence Step Progression (drips only)

For each step: the delay, the message, and how many recipients are at that step (with percent).

## Campaign Configuration (right panel)

Name, type, dispatch channel, the attached flow with an **Open** link (flow campaigns), a WhatsApp template preview card (template broadcasts) or a message preview (text broadcasts), and the audience tags.

## Recipient Delivery Logs

A table of every recipient.

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| **Contact** | Name and phone/ID. |
| **Delivery Status** | pending, sent, delivered, read, completed, or "Not delivered". |
| **Current Step** | Drips only. |
| **Execution / Scheduled At** | Next send time, or last update time. |
| **Diagnostics / Error** | For failures, the error code and a plain-language reason. |
| **Actions** | **Open Chat** (opens the conversation in the Team Inbox) or "No chat". |

Controls above the table:
- Search box ("Search contact name / phone...").
- Status buttons: all, pending, sent, delivered, read, completed, not delivered.
- Pagination of 20 per page with **Previous** and **Next**; text "Showing 1 to 20 of N recipients".

Failed recipients are listed first, then pending, then the rest (most recently updated first).

## Retry failed recipients

There is no "Retry failed" button. What you can do:

- **Flow and Broadcast campaigns:** sending again only targets recipients still marked `pending`. Failed recipients stay failed. To reach them again, create a new campaign for those contacts (choose them in **Manual Contact Selection**; use the status filter "not delivered" on the details page to see who they are), after fixing the cause (for example an expired template, an invalid number, or exceeding the tier limit).
- **WhatsApp automatic retry inside flows:** the Send Message and WhatsApp Template nodes have **Max Retry Attempts** to retry a failed message automatically.

## Export responses (Excel)

Owners and Admins can download the answers customers gave during a flow campaign.

1. Open the campaign details of a flow campaign.
2. Click **Export responses (Excel)**.
3. A file named like `campaign-<name>-responses.xlsx` downloads, and the action is recorded in the audit log.

The sheet "Responses" has one row per recipient with these columns:

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| Name, Phone, Email | Contact details. |
| Status | Recipient delivery status. |
| Delivered at (UTC), Read at (UTC), Failed at (UTC) | Times from delivery receipts. |
| Failure reason | Error text or code. |
| One column per question | For each Input node (the prompt is the heading) and each Template node that saves a button tap or has buttons ("Template: <template name>"), the customer's latest answer. |
| Last answered at (UTC) | Time of the latest answer. |

Limits: exports are refused above 50,000 recipients ("too many to export at once"). Every value is saved as text, so a reply such as "=1+1" is not calculated in Excel.

## Delete a campaign

Click **Delete** and confirm **Delete Campaign**. All recipient tracking and statistics for the campaign are permanently removed. Only Owners and Admins can delete.

---

title: Campaigns: common errors and fixes
content:
# Campaigns: common errors and fixes
| What you see | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "Failed to load campaigns" | Network or server problem. | Refresh. |
| "Failed to load initial data for campaign creation" | Channels, flows or contacts failed to load. | Reload the page. |
| "Flow ... is missing or not published. Please publish the flow before launching the campaign." | The chosen flow is a draft or was deleted. | Open the flow, click Publish, then send again. |
| "Channel not found" | The channel was removed. | Create a campaign on an existing channel. |
| "Campaign not found" | The campaign was deleted. | Go back to the list. |
| "Only broadcast and flow campaigns can be triggered..." | You clicked Send Now on a drip. | Drips start automatically; do not use Send Now. |
| Recipient "Not sent: conversation is handed off to a human agent" | The contact's conversation was handed to a person. | Reply to them in the Team Inbox. |
| Recipient "Not sent: flow is missing or not published" | The flow was unpublished or deleted during the send. | Publish and create a new campaign for the failed contacts. |
| Recipient "Not sent: another flow pass was already running for this conversation" | The contact's chat was busy at that moment. | Create a new campaign for the failed contacts. |
| Recipient "Not sent: the flow produced no message to send" | The flow's first steps send nothing (for example a flow that begins with a Wait). | Start the flow with a Template or Message node. |
| Many "Not delivered" with codes 131048 or 131056 | WhatsApp daily limit or spam-rate limit exceeded. | Use smaller audiences, spread over days, or raise your tier. |
| "Not delivered" with a template error | The template is not approved, was renamed, the language is wrong, or a variable is empty. | Check the template in Meta Business Suite and the parameter mappings. |
| Status shows "failed" although the send finished | Every recipient failed (including later WhatsApp reports). | Open the details page, read "Why messages were not delivered". |
| 403 / permission error when creating or sending | Your role is not Owner or Admin. | Ask an Owner or Admin. |
| Export button missing | You are not an Owner/Admin, or the campaign has no flow. | Use an Owner/Admin account; export is only for flow campaigns. |

## Best practices (supported by the screens)

- Use **WhatsApp HSM Template** broadcasts for business-initiated messages; plain text only reaches contacts within WhatsApp's customer-service window.
- Watch the **24h tier capacity** panel before creating a campaign; keep the audience below the limit or use a drip.
- Filter by **tags** to keep campaigns targeted.
- Publish and test your flow before using it in a campaign.
- Check the "Why messages were not delivered" panel and fix the main cause before the next campaign.

This part of the manual covers the "business data" screens and the administration screens of the Omni Platform tenant app:

| Screen | Sidebar entry | Address in the browser | Who normally uses it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contacts | Contacts | `/contacts` | Agents, admins, owners |
| Deals (CRM Pipeline) | Deals & CRM | `/deals` | Sales agents, admins, owners |

| System Logs | (no sidebar entry, see notes) | `/system-logs` (not wired in this build) | Owners and admins only |
| Settings | Settings & Scale | `/settings` | Everyone (some tabs are limited by role) |

Before you start, three general points apply to all of these screens.

- **Your workspace is private.** Everything you see (contacts, deals, products, orders, analytics) belongs to your own workspace (your "tenant"). Other customers of the platform cannot see it and you cannot see theirs.
- **Toast messages.** After almost every action a small coloured message appears in a corner of the screen: green for success, red for an error, blue for information. The error text usually tells you exactly what was wrong.
- **Roles.** Your workspace has four roles: Owner, Admin, Agent and Viewer. Section 7 (Settings, Team & RBAC) explains them in detail. In the screens described in sections 1 to 4, the server does not block any signed-in role from changing data, so the safest practice is to give Viewer accounts only to people who truly should only look (see the "Notes" lines in each section).
