title: Contacts
content:
# Contacts
## 1.1 What the Contacts screen is for

The Contacts screen (title on the page: **Contacts & Audience Management**) is your customer address book. Every person who messages you on any connected channel (WhatsApp, web chat, and so on) becomes a contact automatically. You can also add contacts by hand or import them in bulk from a spreadsheet. Each contact can carry:

- a **name** (optional),
- a **phone number or channel ID** (called "External ID / Phone"; this is the identity used to reach the person),
- an **email address** (optional),
- one or more **tags** (labels such as `followup`, `vip`, `lead`),
- any number of **custom attributes** (extra columns such as Company, Product, Price, Order ID) which you can insert into WhatsApp templates and Flow Builder messages,
- the **channel** the contact belongs to, and a created date.

Contacts are the starting point for broadcasts (campaigns), deals and orders.

## 1.2 How to open it

1. Sign in to the app.
2. In the left sidebar click **Contacts**.

The page loads the 1,000 most recently created contacts, the list of channels in your workspace, and the list of tags already in use. If something fails to load you will see the red message "Failed to load contacts data"; refresh the browser page and try again.

> **Good to know:** Because only the latest 1,000 contacts are loaded, search and filters work on those 1,000 contacts only. If you have more than 1,000 contacts, older ones will not appear on this screen until newer ones are deleted.

## 1.3 Page layout at a glance

From top to bottom the screen has:

1. **Header** with two buttons on the right: **Import CSV / Excel** and **Add Contact**.
2. **Filter card** containing:
   - a search box ("Search by name, phone, email, or tag..."),
   - **Channel** filter buttons (All, plus one button per connected channel),
   - **Filter by Tag** pills (All Tags, plus tags),
   - the **Select All** checkbox and, when applicable, the **Delete Filtered** button and the selection toolbar.
3. **Contacts table** with the columns Contact, External ID / Phone, Tags, Email, Created and Actions.
4. Three pop-up windows (modals) that open on demand: the Import window, the Add Contact window and the Contact Details window.

## 1.4 The contacts table, column by column

| Column | What it shows |
|---|---|
| (checkbox) | Tick to select the contact for bulk actions. The checkbox in the table heading selects or clears all contacts that match the current filters. |
| Contact | A round badge with the first two letters of the name, and the name. If there is no name it says "Unnamed Contact". |
| External ID / Phone | The number or channel ID, in a fixed-width font. Phone numbers are stored as digits only, with the country code and without a plus sign (for example `919876543210`). |
| Tags | Coloured pills such as `#followup`. "No tags" is shown if the contact has none. |
| Email | The email address, or a dash. |
| Created | Date and time the contact was created. |
| Actions | **Details** (opens the Contact Details window) and a trash-can icon (deletes that one contact). |

Tag colours are only a visual aid: `followup` is amber, `up` is blue, `mp` is purple, `vip` and `hot` are rose, `lead` is green and every other tag is grey.

If the table is empty you will see "No contacts found". If filters are active it suggests adjusting them; if there are no filters it offers **Import Excel / CSV** and **Add Contact** buttons.

## 1.5 Searching and filtering

You can combine all three filters; a contact must match all of them to be shown.

| Filter | How it works |
|---|---|
| Search box | Type any part of a name, phone number / external ID, email address or tag. Matching ignores upper and lower case. The table updates as you type. |
| Channel buttons | Click **All** or one channel name. Only contacts that belong to that channel are shown. |
| Filter by Tag pills | Click **All Tags** or a tag. The list of pills always contains the preset tags `followup`, `up`, `mp`, `vip` plus every tag that exists on your contacts. Click a pill to show only contacts with that tag; click **All Tags** to clear. |

When at least one filter is active, an extra red button appears: **Delete Filtered (N)** (see 1.10).

## 1.6 Tags: how they behave

- Tags are always stored in lower case, with no leading or trailing spaces. Typing `VIP` and `vip` gives the same tag.
- Duplicate tags on the same contact are merged into one.
- In a spreadsheet's tags column you can separate several tags with a comma, a semicolon or a space (for example `followup, hot` or `followup hot`). A tag therefore cannot contain spaces; use an underscore or hyphen instead (for example `new_customer`).
- The preset suggestion chips are: `followup`, `up`, `mp`, `vip`, `lead`, `customer`, `hot`, `new`. You can also invent any tag of your own.
- Tags are how you group contacts into an "audience". In the Campaigns screen you choose an audience by tag, and the Contacts screen "Send Broadcast / Flow" button takes you there.

## 1.7 Add a single contact (step by step)

1. Open **Contacts** and click **Add Contact** (top right).
2. In the "Add New Contact" window fill in:
   - **Contact Name**: optional, for example "John Doe".
   - **Phone Number / WhatsApp ID** (required, marked with a red star): choose the **country code** from the drop-down on the left, then type the number on the right. You may type a national number (such as `9876543210`) or the full number. Below the box a live preview shows the number as it will be saved (for example `919876543210`).
   - **Email Address (Optional)**: must look like an email address because the browser checks the format.
   - **Channel**: choose which of your connected channels this contact belongs to. The first channel is pre-selected.
   - **Tags**: type a tag and press **Enter** or the comma key to add it. A new contact starts with the tag `lead`; click the small x on a tag to remove it. Click a "+preset" chip to add a common tag quickly.
3. Click **Add Contact**.
4. The green message "Contact created successfully!" appears and the contact is placed at the top of the list.

Rules and behaviour:

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Phone / ID is required | If it is empty you see "Phone number or External ID is required". |
| Automatic formatting | If you typed a plus sign, the digits you typed are trusted as the full international number. Otherwise a leading zero is removed and, for 10-digit numbers, the chosen country code is added in front. For 9-digit and 8-digit numbers the country code is added too, unless the selected country is India (+91) or the US/Canada (+1). |
| IDs that contain letters | Channel IDs such as web chat visitor IDs or Telegram handles (anything with letters and no plus sign) are kept exactly as typed. |
| Duplicates | A contact is unique per channel and number. If you add a number that already exists on the same channel, the existing contact is updated (new name kept if given, new tags and attributes merged) instead of creating a second contact. |
| No channel connected | If your workspace has no channel at all, you get the error "No channels found for this tenant. Please connect a channel first." Connect a channel first (Channels screen). |
| Default country | The default country code in the window is +91 (India). Change it for contacts from other countries. Supported countries in the drop-down: India, United States / Canada, United Kingdom, United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Malaysia, Australia, New Zealand, Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Brazil, Mexico, South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Indonesia, Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Egypt, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait and Bahrain. |

## 1.8 Import contacts from CSV or Excel (step by step)

The import wizard lets you upload a spreadsheet, tell the system which column is which, turn extra columns into custom attributes, and tag everyone in one go.

**Preparing your file**

- Accepted formats: `.csv`, `.xlsx`, `.xls`.
- Maximum file size: **10 MB**.
- Only the **first sheet** of an Excel workbook is read.
- The first row must be the header row (column names).
- You need at least one column holding the phone number or ID. Everything else is optional.
- Click **Download CSV Sample** in the import window to get an example file named `contacts_with_custom_fields_sample.csv`. Its columns are `Name, Phone, Email, Company, Product, Price, Tags`.

**Steps**

1. Click **Import CSV / Excel**.
2. Click the dashed upload area and choose your file (it is not a drag-and-drop-only area; clicking opens the file chooser). While the file is inspected you see "Inspecting spreadsheet columns and headers...". Afterwards the area shows the file name, its size in KB and how many rows were detected. Click the area again to replace the file.
3. **Step 1: Map Main System Columns.** For each of the four system fields choose the matching spreadsheet column from the drop-down (each entry shows an example value from the first row):
   - **Contact Number / Phone** (required, marked with a red star; the drop-down shows a red outline until you choose),
   - **Contact Name** (optional),
   - **Email Address** (optional),
   - **Tags Column in Spreadsheet** (optional).
   The system pre-selects columns whose headings it recognises:

   | System field | Headings recognised automatically (case, spaces, dashes and underscores ignored) |
   |---|---|
   | Name | name, full name, contact name, customer name, client name, user |
   | Phone | phone, phone number, mobile, mobile number, contact, contact number, whatsapp, whatsapp number, external id, number, tel, id |
   | Email | email, email address, mail, email id |
   | Tags | tag, tags, category, categories, label, labels, group, groups, segment |

4. **Step 2: Custom Variable Fields (Attributes).** Every column that you did not map in Step 1 is listed here with a checkbox. Ticked columns are saved on each contact as custom attributes.
   - Use **Select All / Deselect All** to flip all of them at once.
   - For each ticked column you can edit the **Save as key** name. Keys are forced to lower case letters, digits and underscores (any other character becomes an underscore). For example the column "Order ID" becomes `order_id`.
   - Next to each key you see how to use it in templates and flows: `{{contact.attributes.<key>}}`, for example `{{contact.attributes.company}}`.
   - If every column is already mapped you see "All detected spreadsheet columns are currently mapped to main system fields."
5. **Step 3: Preview Spreadsheet Rows** (optional): click **Show Preview** to see the first 5 rows so you can double-check the columns. Click **Hide Preview** to collapse it.
6. **Step 4: Target Channel, Country Code and tags.**
   - **Target Channel**: the channel all imported contacts will belong to (required).
   - **Default Country Code**: added in front of 10-digit numbers that have no country code (so that WhatsApp replies match the imported contact and do not create a duplicate). Default is +91.
   - **Assign Default Audience Tags**: tags given to every imported contact, in addition to any tags that come from the spreadsheet's tags column. The import window starts with the tag `followup` already added. Type a tag and press Enter or comma, click x to remove, or click the **+preset** chips.
7. Click **Start Import with Mappings**. The button stays disabled until a file is chosen and a phone column is selected.
8. When finished you see a green banner "Import Finished!" saying how many rows were processed, how many new contacts were created and how many existing contacts were updated. A red box lists any rows that failed. The contact list reloads behind the window. Click **Cancel** (or the close button) to close the window.

**What happens to each row**

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Phone cell empty | The row is skipped silently when the file is read (it is not counted as an error). |
| New number for the target channel | A new contact is created (counted under "new"). |
| Number already exists on that channel | The existing contact is updated (counted under "updated"): the name is replaced only if the row has a name; tags are merged (old plus new, no duplicates); email and custom attributes from the row overwrite the old values; the stored number is upgraded to the full international format if it was saved in short form earlier. |
| A row fails (for example a database problem) | It appears in the error list as "Row N (number): message" and the rest of the import continues. |

**Import errors and fixes**

| Message | Meaning and fix |
|---|---|
| Please select a CSV or Excel file | You clicked Start without choosing a file. |
| Please select a column for Contact Number / Phone (Required) | Choose the phone column in Step 1. |
| Failed to inspect spreadsheet headers / Failed to parse spreadsheet | The file is damaged, password protected, larger than 10 MB or not a real CSV/Excel file. Re-save it from Excel as `.xlsx` or CSV (UTF-8) and retry. |
| No contact rows found. Ensure the mapped column contains valid contact numbers / IDs. | The phone column you mapped is empty for all rows, or you mapped the wrong column. |
| No channels found. Connect a channel before importing contacts. | Connect a channel first. |
| Row N: Missing external ID / phone number | That row has no usable number. |

## 1.9 Contact Details window

Click **Details** at the end of a row. The window title is the contact's name and its subtitle shows "Phone / ID". It contains:

- **Email** and **Created** date.
- **Audience Tags**: all tags with an x to remove each. Below it, an input "Add tag" (press Enter or click **Add Tag**) and the preset chips (+followup, +up and so on). Adding or removing a tag is saved immediately and a message such as `Tag "vip" added` appears. Adding a tag that the contact already has does nothing.
- **Custom Attributes (Flow Builder and Template Variables)**: shown only if the contact has attributes besides email and tags. Each attribute card shows its key, the exact placeholder to use, for example `{{contact.attributes.company}}`, and its value. Attributes are read-only here; to change them re-import the contact with new values.
- **Associated Deals (N)**: the deals linked to this contact with their stage and value. **View All Deals** opens the Deals screen. The value is displayed in dollars with the sign `$` (see 2.4 for the cents rule).
- **View Inbox** (opens the Team Inbox) and **Start Campaign** (opens the new-campaign screen).

## 1.10 Delete contacts (single, selected and filtered)

Deleting a contact is **permanent**. It also removes that contact's conversation history, deals and campaign recipient records.

**Delete one contact**

1. Click the trash-can icon at the end of the row.
2. Confirm "Delete Contact" in the red confirmation box.

**Delete selected contacts**

1. Tick the checkboxes of the contacts you want, or tick **Select All (N matching contacts)** to select everything that matches the current filters.
2. A toolbar shows a badge "N selected", the red **Delete Selected (N)** button and the blue **Send Broadcast / Flow** button.
3. Click **Delete Selected (N)** and confirm.

**Delete everything that matches the current filters**

1. Apply a tag, channel or search filter.
2. Click the red **Delete Filtered (N)** button. The confirmation lists the filters in force (for example "Tag: #followup, Channel: WhatsApp Sales").
3. Confirm. All N contacts currently shown are deleted.

Safety notes: the confirmation window shows the exact number of contacts that will be deleted; read it. The "Select All" checkbox selects only the contacts shown after filtering. There is no undo and no recycle bin.

## 1.11 Bulk actions available on Contacts

| Action | Where | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Delete selected | Selection toolbar | Removes the ticked contacts. |
| Delete filtered | Filter bar (only when a filter is active) | Removes all contacts matching the filter. |
| Send Broadcast / Flow | Selection toolbar | Opens the New Campaign screen (the contact selection itself is not carried over; you choose the audience there by channel/tag). |
| Bulk tagging | Import window only | Default tags are applied to every imported contact. There is no bulk "add tag to selected contacts" button. |

## 1.12 Features that are not on this screen

To avoid confusion, the following are **not** available on the Contacts screen in this version: saved segments, opt-in / opt-out (consent) flags, block lists, merging duplicate contacts, export of the contact list to CSV, and editing the name, email or custom attributes of an existing contact by hand. Use tags as your segments, import to update attributes, and use Settings > Audit Trail & Compliance for a single-person data export (section 7.7).

## 1.13 Common problems with contacts

| Problem | Likely cause and fix |
|---|---|
| A contact I added is missing after refresh | It may be older than the latest 1,000 contacts, or you have a filter active. Clear filters; check the date. |
| Imported numbers look wrong (for example 10 digits only) | The Default Country Code was not set correctly, or the number has fewer/more digits than expected. Include the country code in the sheet, with a plus sign, for example `+14155552671`. |
| Phone numbers in Excel turn into `9.88E+11` | Format the phone column as Text before saving, or save as CSV from a text editor. |
| A customer replied and now there are two contacts | The first contact was saved in a different format than the incoming number. Re-import with the correct country code; numbers that match after formatting are merged into the existing contact. |
| Tag filter shows no tags I expect | The tag list contains tags that currently exist on at least one contact, plus the four presets. |
| "Failed to create contact" | The message from the server follows; most often no channel exists or the phone is missing. |

title: Deals (CRM Pipeline)
content:
# Deals (CRM Pipeline)
## 2.1 What the Deals screen is for

The Deals screen (title: **CRM Pipeline**) is a Kanban board for sales opportunities. Each "deal" is a card that belongs to one contact, has a title and a money value, and sits in one **stage** of your sales process. You move the card from stage to stage as the opportunity progresses, and the board totals show how much value is in each stage.

Open it from the sidebar entry **Deals & CRM**.

## 2.2 The summary cards

Four cards run across the top:

| Card | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Total Pipeline Value | The sum of the value of all deals in every stage (including Won and Lost), shown in dollars. |
| Total Deals | The number of deals in the workspace. |
| Won Deals | The number of deals currently in the **Won** stage. |
| Won Value | The total value of deals in the **Won** stage. |

Values are stored in cents and shown divided by 100 with a `$` sign (see 2.4).

## 2.3 The six pipeline stages

The board has six fixed columns, from left to right. The stage names are fixed; you cannot add, rename or reorder stages.

| Stage | Typical meaning |
|---|---|
| Lead | A new, unqualified opportunity. Default stage for a new deal. |
| Qualified | You have confirmed the contact is a real prospect with a need. |
| Proposal | A quote or proposal has been sent. |
| Negotiation | Terms and price are being discussed. |
| Won | The customer accepted; the deal is closed successfully. |
| Lost | The opportunity was lost or abandoned. |

Each column header shows the stage name, the number of cards in it and the total value of that stage. Columns scroll sideways on small screens and each column scrolls up and down when it holds many cards. An empty column shows "No deals in <stage>".

## 2.4 About deal values (important)

The deal value box is labelled **Deal Value (in Cents)**. You type the amount in cents, not in dollars. Example: type `10000` for $100.00; type `250050` for $2,500.50. The cards, the summary cards and the Contacts detail window all show the value divided by 100 with a `$` sign. The value field is a plain number: it must be a number, and if left invalid it is saved as 0. The currency symbol on this screen is always `$`.

## 2.5 Searching deals

The search box ("Search deals by title or contact...") filters the board as you type. It matches the deal title or the name of the linked contact (not case sensitive). The summary cards are not affected by the search.

## 2.6 What a deal card shows

- **Title** (bold) and, when you hover over the card, two icons: a pencil (**Edit Deal**) and a trash can (**Delete Deal**).
- **Value** in green.
- **Contact** (small badge with the first two letters and the contact's name) when the contact is known.
- A **"Move to ..." drop-down** that changes the stage.
- The creation date and time.

## 2.7 Create a deal (step by step)

1. Click **Add Deal** (top right).
2. Fill in the "Create New Deal" window:
   - **Deal Title** (required), for example "Enterprise License - Acme Corp".
   - **Deal Value (in Cents)** (required), default 10000 ($100.00).
   - **Associated Contact** (required): choose from the list of contacts (the list shows each contact's name or, if there is no name, its phone number; only the 1,000 newest contacts are offered).
   - **Initial Stage**: defaults to Lead.
3. Click **Create Deal**. The message "Deal created successfully!" appears and the board and totals refresh.

If you leave the title empty or do not select a contact, nothing is saved (the form requires both). If the contact has been deleted in the meantime you get "contactId does not refer to an existing contact".

## 2.8 Move a deal between stages

1. Find the card.
2. Use the drop-down at the bottom of the card ("Move to Lead", "Move to Qualified", and so on) and pick the new stage.
3. The message "Deal moved to <stage>" appears, the card jumps to the new column and the totals recalculate.

There is no drag-and-drop; use the drop-down. Any stage can be chosen from any stage (for example straight from Lead to Won, or from Lost back to Lead).

## 2.9 Edit a deal

1. Hover over the card and click the pencil icon.
2. Change **Deal Title**, **Deal Value (in Cents)** or **Stage** in the "Edit Deal" window.
3. Click **Save Changes**.

## 2.10 Delete a deal

1. Hover over the card and click the trash-can icon.
2. Confirm "Delete Deal" in the red confirmation box. The card is removed from the pipeline.

## 2.11 Deals and other screens

- Deals appear in a contact's detail window (1.9).
- Deleting a contact also deletes that contact's deals.
- In Analytics, the **Conversion Funnel** counts "Deals Created" and "Deals Won" (see 5.5). Note the caveat there about the "Won" count.
- Settings > Usage & Plans does not limit deals.

## 2.12 Common problems with deals

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| Cannot choose a contact when creating a deal | The contact list is empty. Add contacts first (section 1). |
| Value looks 100 times too small | You typed dollars instead of cents. Edit the value (multiply by 100). |
| A deal I created is not in the column I expect | Check the **Initial Stage** you picked; use the stage drop-down on the card to move it. |
| Deal card shows no contact | The contact was deleted or is outside the 1,000 newest contacts. |

title: Products
content:
# Products
## 3.1 What the Products screen is for

The Products screen (title: **Products & Catalogs**) is where you keep the list of things you sell. The product list is used for WhatsApp interactive commerce: when a customer sends a WhatsApp cart order, the system matches each ordered item to a product by its **SKU** and creates an order in the Orders screen with the product's name and price. Open it from the sidebar entry **Products**.

## 3.2 Layout

- **Header** with **Refresh** (reloads the list) and **Add Product**.
- **Filter card**: search box, **Category** drop-down and the **In Stock / Available Only** checkbox.
- **Product cards** in a grid (three per row on large screens).

## 3.3 Filters

| Filter | How it works |
|---|---|
| Search ("Search products by title, SKU, description...") | Matches part of the product name, SKU or description, ignoring upper and lower case. The list refreshes about 0.2 seconds after you stop typing. |
| Category drop-down | "All Categories (n)" or one of the categories that exist on your products (n is the number of different categories). |
| In Stock / Available Only | Tick to hide products that are marked out of stock. |

The list shows up to 50 products at a time on this screen. If you have more than 50 products, use search or the category filter to reach the others.

## 3.4 What a product card shows

- A picture (the first image URL) or "No image uploaded". Click the picture to open it larger in a lightbox; click anywhere outside or the X to close it.
- On the picture: a green **In Stock** or grey **Out of Stock** label, the **category** (purple label) and the **SKU**.
- Name, price with currency (for example `INR 499`), and the description (two lines, or "No description provided.").
- **Qty** (inventory quantity) and "Updated <date and time>".
- Footer buttons: **Mark Out of Stock / Mark Available** (toggles availability immediately), a pencil (**Edit Product**) and a trash can (**Delete Product**).

## 3.5 Product fields

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| Product Title | Yes | Any text. Spaces at the ends are removed. |
| SKU (Retailer Product ID) | Yes | Saved in capital letters. Must be unique inside your workspace: two products cannot have the same SKU. The system suggests a random one like `SKU-4821` for new products. Use the same SKU that you use in your WhatsApp / Meta catalog (the "retailer ID"), because incoming WhatsApp orders are matched to products by this value. |
| Price | Yes | A number, 0 or higher, decimals allowed (two decimal places are stored). Negative or empty prices show "Please enter a valid price". |
| Currency | No | Choose INR (default), USD, EUR, GBP or AED. |
| Inventory Quantity | No | Whole number; blank counts as 0. |
| Category | No | Free text. Existing categories are suggested as you type; typing a new one creates it. New products start with the first existing category or "General". |
| Product is available for purchase | No | Checkbox, ticked by default. Unticked = shown as Out of Stock. |
| Product Description | No | Free text shown in the WhatsApp catalog message. |
| Image URLs (one URL per line) | No | One web address per line (commas also work as separators). Images are **not uploaded** here; paste links to images already hosted somewhere (https links work best). The first link is used as the card picture. |

## 3.6 Create a product (step by step)

1. Click **Add Product**.
2. In the "Add New Product" window enter **Product Title** and check the suggested **SKU** (change it to your catalog's retailer ID if needed).
3. Enter **Price**, choose **Currency**, and type the **Inventory Quantity**.
4. Choose or type a **Category**, tick or untick **Product is available for purchase**.
5. Add a **Product Description** and the **Image URLs**.
6. Click **Create Product**. The message "Product created successfully" appears and the grid reloads.

If the title or SKU is empty you see "Product name and SKU are required". If another product already uses the same SKU you will see an error message from the server and the product is not saved; use a different SKU.

## 3.7 Edit a product

1. Click the pencil icon on the card.
2. Change any field and click **Save Changes**. The SKU can be changed, but if you change it, orders arriving from WhatsApp for the old SKU will no longer match this product.

## 3.8 Mark a product out of stock or available again

Click **Mark Out of Stock** (or **Mark Available**) on the card. The change is immediate and a blue message says "Product is now unavailable/available". It does not change the quantity number.

## 3.9 Delete a product

1. Click the trash-can icon.
2. In the "Delete Product" window read the warning ("will remove it from future WhatsApp catalog queries") and click **Delete Product**.

Past orders keep the product name, SKU and price that were recorded when they were placed.

## 3.10 Catalog sync, variants and bulk import

In this version the Products screen manages products **one at a time**. There is no product CSV import, no variant (size/colour) support and no "sync catalog with Meta" button on this screen. Products are matched to WhatsApp catalog orders purely by SKU, so keep SKUs identical in both places.

## 3.11 Common problems with products

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| "Please enter a valid price" | Price is empty, negative or not a number. |
| SKU error when saving | Another product already uses that SKU. |
| No picture appears | The image link is wrong, private or not a direct link to an image file. Open the link in a new browser tab to test it. |
| Customer's WhatsApp order shows "Product (SKU)" with price 0 | No product with that SKU exists in your Products list. Create it with the same SKU. |
| Product not found in search | Search matches only title, SKU and description, not category; use the Category filter. |

title: Orders
content:
# Orders
## 4.1 What the Orders screen is for

The Orders screen (title: **Orders & Invoices**) lists every order in your workspace and lets you follow it through its life: payment, processing, shipping and completion. Open it from the sidebar entry **Orders**.

**How orders are created.** There is no "New order" button on this screen. Orders are created automatically when a customer sends a **cart order from your WhatsApp catalog**. The system reads each item's SKU, looks up the product in your Products list, uses the price sent by WhatsApp (or your product price if WhatsApp did not send one), and creates an order with:

- an order number like `ORD-20260115-AB12` (the letters "ORD", the date and a random code),
- the contact and conversation it came from,
- the list of items (name, SKU, quantity, unit price, line total),
- the total (sum of the line totals),
- status **Pending** and payment **Pending**,
- the currency from the WhatsApp message (default INR) and the note "whatsapp_catalog" as the payment method.

## 4.2 The four summary cards

| Card | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Total Orders | All orders in your workspace. |
| Total Revenue | The total of orders that are paid: those whose payment is "captured" **or** whose status is Paid, Processing, Shipped or Completed. Shown with the ₹ sign whatever the order currency. |
| Pending Orders | Orders whose status is Pending. |
| Paid / Fulfilled | Number of orders that are paid (status Paid or payment captured) **plus** the number of orders with status Completed. (An order that is both paid and completed can be counted twice in this card.) |

## 4.3 Filters

| Filter | Options |
|---|---|
| Search | Type part of an **order number**, the **contact name** or the contact's **phone**. |
| Status | All Statuses, Pending, Paid, Processing, Shipped, Completed, Cancelled, Refunded. |
| Payment | All Payments, Pending, Captured / Success, Failed, Refunded. |

The list shows up to 50 newest orders. Use the filters to find older ones. **Refresh** reloads the screen.

## 4.4 The orders table

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Order Number | The order number and the date/time it was created. |
| Customer | Contact name and phone / external ID. |
| Items | The total quantity ("3 items") and the item names with quantities. |
| Total Amount | Currency and total. |
| Order Status | A coloured label (see 4.5). |
| Payment | A coloured payment label and, in brackets, the payment method if known. |
| Actions | **Details** opens the order window. |

## 4.5 Order statuses and what they mean

| Status | Meaning | Colour |
|---|---|---|
| Pending | New order, not yet paid or handled. | Amber |
| Paid | Payment received. | Green |
| Processing | You are preparing the order. | Blue |
| Shipped | The order has been sent to the customer. | Green |
| Completed | Delivered and finished. | Green |
| Cancelled | The order was cancelled. | Red |
| Refunded | The money was returned to the customer. | Red |

## 4.6 Payment statuses and what they mean

| Payment status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Pending | No payment received yet. |
| Authorized | The payment was approved by the bank/gateway but not yet collected. |
| Captured | The money has been collected (shown as "Captured / Success" in the filter). |
| Failed | The payment attempt failed. |
| Refunded | The payment was returned. |

Payment methods you may see next to the payment label: `razorpay`, `stripe`, `whatsapp_pay`, `cod`, `manual` or `whatsapp_catalog`.

## 4.7 The order window

Click **Details** to open "Order <number>" (with the date it was placed). It contains:

1. **Lifecycle Status**: the current status label and a drop-down with the choices **Mark Pending, Mark Paid, Mark Processing, Mark Shipped, Mark Completed, Mark Cancelled, Mark Refunded**. Choosing one saves immediately ("Order status updated to <status>") and the summary cards refresh. On the right is the **Total Payable** amount.
2. **Customer**: name and phone / external ID.
3. **Order Items**: each line with name, SKU, quantity times unit price and the line total.
4. **Payment Gateway Link** section with the payment label (see 4.8).
5. **Manual payment** box (shown while the order is not Paid or Completed): see 4.9.
6. **Close** button.

Changing the order status does not change the payment label by itself; the drop-down changes the order status only.

## 4.8 Create and send a payment link (step by step)

Use this to let a customer pay online.

1. Open the order (**Details**).
2. In the **Payment Gateway Link** box choose the gateway: **Razorpay Standard Link** or **Stripe Checkout Session**.
3. Click **Generate & Send Link**.
4. The message "Payment link generated via RAZORPAY/STRIPE" appears and the link is shown in a read-only box with two buttons: **Copy Link** (copies it) and **Open Payment Page** (opens it in a new tab).
5. Send the link to the customer (for example paste it in the conversation in the Team Inbox).

Once a link exists, the gateway chooser is replaced by the link box: an order keeps one link. When the customer pays, the payment gateway informs the platform automatically and the order becomes **Paid** with payment **Captured**; you do not need to do anything.

## 4.9 Record a manual payment (cash, bank transfer, UPI)

Use this when the customer paid you outside the gateways (cash on delivery, bank transfer, UPI to your own number).

1. Open the order (**Details**). The manual payment box is shown only when the status is not Paid or Completed.
2. Type the **Manual payment ref / UPI transaction ID** (optional but recommended).
3. Click **Record Manual Payment**.
4. The system records a "manual" payment transaction for the full order amount and shows "Payment recorded manually & order marked as paid".

## 4.10 Refunds

There is no "Refund" button that sends money back through Razorpay or Stripe. To refund a customer you return the money yourself (in the payment provider's dashboard or by bank transfer) and then set the order status to **Refunded** from the **Lifecycle Status** drop-down. Use **Cancelled** for orders that were never paid.

## 4.11 Typical order flow

1. Customer sends a cart from your WhatsApp catalog. Order appears as **Pending / Pending**.
2. You open the order, generate a Razorpay or Stripe link and send it to the customer.
3. Customer pays. The order turns **Paid / Captured** automatically. (For cash or bank transfer, record a manual payment and mark it Paid.)
4. Set **Processing** while preparing, **Shipped** when dispatched, **Completed** when delivered.
5. If it goes wrong, use **Cancelled** or **Refunded**.

## 4.12 Common problems with orders

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| "No orders found" | Orders appear only after customers send WhatsApp catalog carts. Check your catalog is connected on the WhatsApp channel and filters are cleared. |
| Items show "Product (SKU)" with no real name | The SKU is not in your Products list. Create the product with the same SKU. |
| "Failed to generate payment link" | The order has no gateway account behind it, or the gateway returned an error. The message from the gateway is shown. Try again or choose the other gateway. |
| The customer paid but the order is still Pending | Payment notifications from the gateway may not have reached the platform. Verify in the gateway dashboard and set the status to Paid manually. |
| Revenue number looks different from the Analytics screen | They are calculated differently (see the notes in 5.2). |

---

title: Analytics & Infra
content:
# Analytics & Infra
## 5.1 What the Analytics screen is for

The Analytics screen (title: **Analytics & Distributed Infrastructure**) gives managers a view of message volume, conversations, response speed, busiest hours, the sales funnel and outbound webhooks. Open it from the sidebar entry **Analytics & Infra**.

The header has **Refresh Telemetry** (reloads every tab). When the Outbound Webhooks tab is active, an **Add Webhook** button also appears. All data is for your whole workspace and for **all time**: there is no date-range picker in this version.

The screen has five tabs: **Executive Overview**, **SLA & Agent Scorecard**, **7x24 Traffic Heatmap**, **Conversion Funnel** and **Outbound Webhooks**.

## 5.2 Tab: Executive Overview

Four KPI cards and two panels.

| Card | What it shows and how it is counted |
|---|---|
| **Total Volume** | The total number of messages stored for your workspace (all time). Underneath: how many were **in** (sent by customers, "inbound") and how many were **out** (sent by you, flows or campaigns, "outbound"). |
| **Conversations** | Total conversations ever opened. Underneath: **active** (open) and **resolved** (closed) conversations. |
| **Audience** | Total number of contacts in the workspace ("Verified omnichannel contacts"). |
| **Commerce Revenue** | Total value of paid orders, with "N paid orders / M total". |

**Channel Traffic Distribution** shows one bar per channel type (for example whatsapp, webchat) with the number of **conversations** on that channel, and the percentage. WhatsApp is green, everything else is blue. If there is nothing yet you see "No channel message activity yet." Note: the bar shows the conversation count for each channel type divided by the total number of messages, so treat the percentages as a rough guide only.

**Distributed Infrastructure Status** lists three fixed information cards: the real-time WebSocket gateway ("Active"), the background workers for flow delays, campaigns and webhooks ("Running") and credential encryption ("Secured"). These are descriptive labels; they are not live health checks.

> **Good to know:** The revenue and paid-order counts here count orders whose payment status is exactly "paid". Order payments in this platform are normally recorded as "captured", so this card may show 0 or a lower number than the Orders screen's Total Revenue even though orders were paid. Also, the money value on this card is divided by 100 and shown with a `$` sign by the screen, while order totals are stored in whole units; for a reliable revenue figure use the Orders screen cards.

## 5.3 Tab: SLA & Agent Scorecard

SLA means "service level agreement": here, how quickly your team answers. The threshold used is **5 minutes (300 seconds)** for the first reply.

| Card | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Avg First Response Time** | Average time from the customer's first message to the first reply by an agent or flow, across all conversations that have a recorded first reply. |
| **Avg Resolution Duration** | Average time from the start of a conversation until it was resolved. |
| **SLA Compliance Rate** | Percentage of answered conversations whose first reply took 5 minutes or less. Shows 100% when no replies are recorded yet. |
| **SLA Breaches** | Number of conversations whose first reply took longer than 5 minutes. |

Times are shown as seconds ("45s"), or minutes and seconds ("3m 20s").

**Agent Productivity Scorecard** table:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Agent | Name and email of every user in your workspace (including admins and owners, even those with no conversations). |
| Role | owner, admin, agent or viewer. |
| Assigned | Number of conversations assigned to that person. |
| Resolved | Number of those conversations that are closed. |
| Avg First Response | That person's average first reply time. |
| Avg Resolution | That person's average resolution time. |
| Performance | **Fast** (average first reply 3 minutes or less), **Normal** (up to 10 minutes) or **Delayed** (over 10 minutes). People with no recorded replies show as Fast (their average is 0). |

Agents are sorted with the busiest first. "No agent conversation activity recorded yet." appears when there is no data.

## 5.4 Tab: 7x24 Traffic Heatmap

A grid with the seven days of the week (Sun to Sat) as rows and the 24 hours (0 to 23) as columns. Each cell holds the **number of messages** (both inbound and outbound, all time) sent in that day-and-hour slot. The darker the colour, the busier the hour.

- Legend: **Low** (grey/very light) to **Peak** (dark).
- Colour steps: empty = grey, up to 25 percent of the busiest slot = lightest, up to 60 percent = medium, above that = darkest with white bold numbers.
- Hover over a cell to see "Sun 14:00 - 37 messages".
- Use it to plan staffing: put more agents on the dark hours.

> **Good to know:** Times are based on the message timestamps in universal time (UTC), not your local time zone. If you are, for example, in India (UTC+5:30), shift the hours by 5 hours 30 minutes in your head.

## 5.5 Tab: Conversion Funnel

A five-step funnel from first contact to payment. For each step you see a number, a bar (length relative to the first step), a "conversion" percentage (how many from the previous step reached this one) and under it the "dropoff" percentage to the next step.

| Step | How it is counted |
|---|---|
| 1. Inbound Contacts | Number of contacts (or the number of conversations if that is larger). |
| 2. Conversations Started | Number of conversations. |
| 3. Deals Created | Number of deals in the CRM pipeline (any stage). |
| 4. Deals Won | Number of deals marked as won. |
| 5. Paid Orders | Number of orders with payment status "paid". |

Conversion rates are capped at 100 percent. The last step is shown with a green label.

> **Good to know:** The funnel counts "won" deals by the stage value `closed_won` and paid orders by payment status `paid`. The Deals screen uses the stage name **Won** and orders are normally marked **captured**, so steps 4 and 5 can show 0 even when you have won deals and paid orders. Use the Deals and Orders screens for authoritative numbers.

## 5.6 Tab: Outbound Webhooks

An outbound webhook sends a message from the platform to **your own system** (a CRM, a spreadsheet script, Zapier and so on) every time something happens. Each delivery is a web request (HTTP POST) signed with a secret so your system can check it is genuine (HMAC-SHA256 signature).

**The list** shows, for each subscription: its **name**, a green **Active** or grey **Disabled** label, a red "N failures" label if deliveries have failed, the destination **URL** (with a copy button), the subscribed **events**, the time it was **last triggered** and the last HTTP status code.

**Buttons on each row**

| Button | What it does |
|---|---|
| Test Ping | Sends a sample event named `ping` to your URL right now. A green message "Test ping succeeded (Status: 200)" or a red "Test ping failed: ..." tells you the result. |
| Delivery Logs | Opens a window listing the latest 50 deliveries: result (SUCCESS/FAILED with HTTP code), the event name, date/time, duration in milliseconds, attempt number and the response text from your server. |
| Trash can | Deletes the subscription after confirmation. Events will no longer be sent to that URL. |

**Register a webhook (step by step)**

1. Open the **Outbound Webhooks** tab and click **Add Webhook** (top) or **Register Endpoint** (in the card).
2. Fill in:
   - **Webhook Name** (required), for example "Production CRM Sync".
   - **Target Endpoint URL (HTTPS)** (required): must start with `http` (use `https://` for security).
   - **HMAC Signature Secret** (optional): leave blank and the platform generates a strong secret for you.
   - **Subscribed Events**: tick **All Events (*)** or choose individual events (see the table below). If you untick everything it goes back to All Events.
3. Click **Register Webhook**. The message "Webhook endpoint subscribed successfully" appears.
4. Click **Test Ping** to check that your server answers.

| Event | Fires when |
|---|---|
| `*` (All Events) | Any event below. |
| `message:new` | An inbound or outbound message is stored. |
| `conversation:new` | A new customer conversation thread starts. |
| `order:new` | A new commerce order is created. |
| `deal:won` | A deal reaches the won state. |

Errors: "Name and URL are required" (fill both), "A valid HTTP(S) url is required" (the address must start with http).

## 5.7 Reading the analytics: quick reference

| Question | Where to look |
|---|---|
| How many messages have we handled? | Executive Overview, Total Volume. |
| Are we answering fast enough? | SLA tab, SLA Compliance Rate and SLA Breaches. |
| Which agent needs help? | SLA tab, scorecard, Performance column. |
| When are customers writing? | Traffic Heatmap. |
| Where do prospects drop off? | Conversion Funnel, "dropoff" lines. |
| Is my CRM receiving events? | Outbound Webhooks, Delivery Logs. |

## 5.8 Common problems with analytics

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| All numbers are 0 | Analytics reflect real activity; connect a channel and receive or send messages. Click **Refresh Telemetry**. |
| Heatmap or message totals are 0 although you chat | The message storage service may be temporarily unreachable; the screen then shows zeros instead of an error. Try again later. |
| Spinner never ends | Reload the page; if it persists check your internet connection. |
| A webhook shows "N failures" | Your server is rejecting the call. Open **Delivery Logs** and read the response; fix your endpoint, then press **Test Ping**. |

title: Settings & Scale
content:
# Settings & Scale
## 7.1 What the Settings screen is for

**Workspace Settings & Scale** is where you manage your own account, your team, developer keys, your plan and quotas, and security/compliance tools. Open it from the sidebar entry **Settings & Scale**, or from the profile menu in the top bar (click your avatar/name, then "Profile & Account Details", "Workspace Settings & RBAC" or "Developer API Keys", which jump straight to the right tab).

There are **five tabs**. The tab you open is remembered in the web address (`/settings?tab=profile`, `?tab=team`, `?tab=api-keys`, `?tab=billing`, `?tab=compliance`), so you can bookmark it.

| Tab (label on screen) | Short name | Who can fully use it |
|---|---|---|
| My Profile & Account | `profile` | Everyone for their own account |
| Team & RBAC | `team` | Everyone can see the list; owners and admins change it |
| Developer API Keys | `api-keys` | Owners and admins |
| Usage & Plans | `billing` | Everyone can see usage; owners and admins buy plans and see invoices |
| Audit Trail & Compliance | `compliance` | Owners and admins (data export), owners only (permanent erasure) |

> **Good to know:** This version has no separate screens for "Organization profile", "AI settings", "Notifications" or "Security (two-factor)". Your organization name is shown on the Profile tab but cannot be edited by tenant users here. If you do not see a setting in this section, it is not part of this version. (AI quotas are shown under Usage & Plans; knowledge bases are managed on the AI Knowledge Base screen.)

## 7.2 Roles and permissions at a glance

| Role | Intended purpose (as written on the Team tab) |
|---|---|
| Owner | Full authority: billing upgrades, API keys, member management, permanent data erasure. |
| Admin | Manages team invites, channels, integrations, knowledge bases and flows. The Team tab says admins "cannot modify billing tiers", but in practice the server lets admins start checkouts and change plans too. |
| Agent | Day-to-day work in the Team Inbox, CRM contacts, deals and orders. |
| Viewer | Intended as read-only: dashboards, search and analytics. Cannot be added to teams. |

What the server enforces in Settings:

| Action | Roles allowed |
|---|---|
| Change your own name or password | Any signed-in user |
| See the team list and the support teams list | Any signed-in user |
| Invite a member, change role or status, remove a member | Owner, Admin |
| Make someone an **Owner** | Owner only |
| Create, rename, delete a support team, set its members | Owner, Admin |
| List, create or revoke API keys | Owner, Admin |
| See usage and available plans | Any signed-in user |
| Start a checkout, verify payment, change plan, list invoices | Owner, Admin |
| Read the audit trail | Owner, Admin |
| Export a contact's data (Article 15) | Owner, Admin |
| Permanently erase a contact's data (Article 17) | **Owner only** |
| System Logs | Owner, Admin |

If a user without permission clicks a protected action they get a red error message such as "Forbidden" and nothing changes.

## 7.3 Tab: My Profile & Account

**Identity banner.** Shows your initials, your name, a coloured role label (Owner purple, Admin blue, Agent/Viewer green), an "Active Session" tag, your email, "Last Active" (time of your last login) and, on the right, your **Workspace Organization** name and your current **Plan** name.

**Personal Information**

1. **Account Email Address**: read-only. The note says your login email is managed by your workspace administrator.
2. **Full Display Name**: type your new name. This is the name shown in conversations, flow activity and team logs.
3. Click **Save Profile Name**. The button is disabled until the name has changed. The message "Profile name updated successfully" appears.

**Password & Security (change your password)**

1. Type your **Current Password**.
2. Type a **New Password** (at least 6 characters) and **Confirm New Password**.
3. Click **Update Password**.

Validation messages:

| Message | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Please enter your current password | The first box is empty. |
| New password must be at least 6 characters long | Too short. |
| New password and confirmation do not match | The two new-password boxes differ. |
| Current password is incorrect | Your current password was typed wrongly. |

After a successful change the three boxes are cleared. If you forgot your password, use "Forgot password" on the sign-in page instead.

**Workspace Identifiers.** Two cards with copy buttons:

- **Workspace Tenant ID**: the unique ID of your workspace. Support and developers ask for it.
- **Active User Member ID**: your own user ID.

Click **Copy** to copy the value to your clipboard.

## 7.4 Tab: Team & RBAC

**Workspace Members.** Top-right button **Invite Member**. Under the heading four coloured cards explain the roles (Owner, Admin, Agent, Viewer).

**Members table**

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Member | Name (or "Unnamed Member"), a "You" tag on your own row and a short ID. |
| Email | Login email. |
| Role | Drop-down: Owner, Admin, Agent, Viewer. Changing it saves immediately. If you are an owner you cannot change your own role. |
| Status | **active** (green) or **deactivated** (grey). |
| Last Login | Date of last sign-in, or "Never". |
| Actions | **Deactivate / Activate** and **Remove** (not shown for your own row). |

**Invite a team member (step by step)**

1. Open Settings > **Team & RBAC** and click **Invite Member**.
2. Fill in "Invite Team Member":
   - **Full Name** (optional).
   - **Email Address** (required).
   - **Workspace Role** (required): Administrator, Support / Sales Agent (default) or Viewer. You cannot invite someone directly as Owner; invite them and then promote them (owners only).
   - **Temporary Password** (optional): if you leave it blank a standard temporary password is assigned by the system. Whatever it is, tell the person to change it right after the first sign-in (Profile tab).
3. Click **Send Invitation**. The message "Invited <email> as <role>" appears and the person is added with status **active**.

Rules and errors:

| Message | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Valid email address is required | The email is empty or has no "@". |
| Role must be one of: admin, agent, viewer | An invalid role was sent. |
| A user with this email address already exists. | That email is already registered on the platform, in your workspace **or any other**. Use a different email. |
| Forbidden | You are not an owner or admin. |

**Change a role.** Pick the new role in the member's Role drop-down. Safety rules: you cannot demote the last remaining Owner ("Cannot demote the last remaining workspace owner") and only an Owner can promote somebody to Owner ("Only workspace owners can promote members to owner").

**Deactivate / reactivate.** Click **Deactivate** to block someone's access without deleting them; their history stays. Click **Activate** to restore. Rules: you cannot deactivate yourself, and you cannot deactivate the only active owner.

**Remove a member.** Click **Remove**, then confirm "Remove Team Member". The person loses access to chats, contacts and workspace tools. Rules: you cannot remove yourself and you cannot remove the only owner.

All of these actions are written to the Audit Trail (7.7).

**Support Teams (below the members table).** Teams are groups of agents such as "Support" or "Sales". In the Team Inbox you can route a conversation to a team.

*Create a team*

1. In the "New team name" box type a name (up to 60 characters).
2. Click **Add**. "Team '<name>' created" appears.

Rules: the name is required, 60 characters at most, and must be unique in your workspace ("A team with this name already exists"). Only owners and admins see the box and buttons; other roles see the list only.

*Set the members of a team*

1. Click **Members** on the team row.
2. Tick the people to include. Only **active** Owners, Admins and Agents are listed; Viewers and deactivated people cannot join a team.
3. Click **Save members**. "Team members updated" appears. A team can hold up to 500 members. Saving replaces the whole member list with what is ticked.

*Delete a team*: click **Delete** and confirm. Conversations that were routed to it simply end up with no team; nothing else is deleted.

If the list fails to load, you see "Could not load teams. Try again".

## 7.5 Tab: Developer API Keys

API keys let your own software call the platform (for example to read contacts or to send messages) without a user login. Keys act with **administrator-level** power for your workspace, so treat them like passwords. Only owners and admins can see or manage them; other roles will see an error message when opening the tab.

Top of the tab: heading, button **Generate API Key**, and a dark box showing how to use a key: send it in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer omni_live_...`, with an example `curl` request to `https://omni-platform.ad96.in/api/contacts`.

**Keys table**

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Name | The label you gave the key. |
| Token Prefix | The first characters of the key (so you can tell keys apart). The rest is never shown again. |
| Scopes | What the key may do. Keys created from this screen have "*" (everything). |
| Created | Creation date. |
| Last Used | Date it was last used, or "Never". |
| Action | **Revoke**. |

**Create an API key (step by step)**

1. Click **Generate API Key**.
2. Enter an **API Key Name** (required), for example "Production Webhook Server" or "Zapier Sync".
3. Choose **Token Expiration**: 30 Days, 60 Days, 90 Days (default), 1 Year or Never Expire.
4. Read the yellow warning: the secret is shown only once.
5. Click **Generate Key**.
6. In the "Save Your Secret API Key" window click **Copy** and store the key in a password manager. Keys start with `omni_live_`.
7. Click **I Have Saved My Secret Key**. You cannot view the secret again; if you lose it, revoke the key and create a new one.

Error: "API Key name is required".

**Revoke a key (step by step)**

1. Click **Revoke** on the key's row.
2. Confirm "Revoke Key". Integrations using this key stop working immediately. The key is removed from the list and cannot be restored.

## 7.6 Tab: Usage & Plans

**Usage cards.** Four progress bars show how much of your plan you are using:

| Card | What is counted | Limit comes from |
|---|---|---|
| Connected Channels | Channels with status active | Your plan |
| Verified Contacts | All contacts in the workspace | Your plan |
| Monthly Messages | Messages sent and received since the first day of the current month | Your plan; the text under the bar says "Resets on <date>" |
| AI Copilot and RAG Queries | AI assistant / knowledge-base answers since the first day of the current month | Your plan |

The bar turns **red above 85 percent**. The percentage is capped at 100.

**Plans.** Under "Subscription Plans and Quota Tiers" there is a **Monthly Billing / Annual Billing** switch (annual saves about 17 percent; the yearly price is the monthly price times 10 unless the plan defines its own yearly price: "2 months free") and one card per plan. Your current plan card is outlined and labelled **Active**, with a disabled "Current Plan" button.

Built-in plan tiers (the platform may replace these with its own list; prices are in USD):

| Plan | Monthly | Yearly | Channels | Contacts | Messages / month | AI queries / month |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free Sandbox | $0 | $0 | 1 | 500 | 2,000 | 100 |
| Starter Growth | $29 | $290 | 3 | 3,000 | 15,000 | 500 |
| Pro Scale | $99 | $990 | 10 | 25,000 | 100,000 | 5,000 |
| Enterprise Custom | $299 | $2,990 | 50 | 500,000 | 1,000,000 | 50,000 |

Each plan card also lists feature lines (for example "AI Smart Copilot", "Full RAG Knowledge Bases", "Team RBAC and Developer API Keys", "Audit Trail and GDPR Compliance Suite") and a badge such as Popular or Recommended.

**Change plan (step by step)**

1. Open Settings > **Usage & Plans**.
2. Choose **Monthly Billing** or **Annual Billing** with the switch.
3. On the plan you want click **Upgrade to <plan>** (or **Activate <plan>** for a free plan).
4. In the checkout window you can still change the billing cycle (Monthly or Annual) and see the plan's quotas.
5. For a paid plan choose the **Payment Gateway**: **Stripe** (cards, global), **Razorpay** (UPI, netbanking) or **Sandbox** (instant simulation, no real payment).
6. Click **Proceed to Pay $<amount>** (for a free plan the button says **Activate Free Tier** and the plan is activated at once).
7. What happens next depends on the gateway:
   - **Sandbox**: the payment is simulated and the plan changes immediately; the invoice is shown.
   - **Stripe or Razorpay**: a checkout page opens in a new browser tab (click **Open Checkout** if your browser blocked it). Pay there. Come back to the Omni window and click **Verify Payment and Activate**. On success the quotas change immediately.
8. A confirmation shows "Upgrade Successful!" with an **Official Invoice Receipt**: invoice number, amount, billing cycle, payment method and plan expiration ("Ongoing (Auto-renew)" if none). Click **Done and Return to Workspace**.

While the window is working (creating the session or verifying) it cannot be closed. Use **Back** from the payment step to return to the plan choice.

**Invoices and Payment History.** A table of every receipt:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Invoice # | Sequential invoice number. |
| Plan Tier | Plan purchased. |
| Amount | Amount and currency. |
| Cycle | Monthly or yearly. |
| Gateway | stripe, razorpay, sandbox or free_tier. |
| Status | **paid** (green) or another status (grey). |
| Date Issued | Date of the invoice. |
| Receipt | **View Receipt** opens the invoice: number, status, plan, amount, billing cycle, gateway, transaction reference, date and coverage period. |

"No Invoices Recorded Yet" means you have never upgraded. Invoices are visible only to owners and admins.

## 7.7 Tab: Audit Trail & Compliance

This tab has two tools: the personal-data tools (GDPR) and the audit log.

**GDPR / data-subject requests**

Privacy laws (GDPR, CCPA) let a person ask for a copy of the data you hold about them (Article 15) or ask you to erase it (Article 17). This tool works on **one contact** at a time using the contact's unique ID.

*How to find the Contact ID*: the contact's ID is a long code (a UUID such as `3f6d...`). Ask your administrator or support to look it up; the Contacts screen does not display it.

*Export a contact's data (Article 15)*

1. Paste the **Contact ID** in the box "Enter Contact ID (e.g. UUID)".
2. Click **Art. 15 Export Data (JSON)**.
3. A file named `gdpr-export-<id>-<date>.json` downloads. It contains: export information (date, who requested), the contact record, all their conversations, all their messages in time order, their deals and their orders.
4. The action is written to the audit log (`compliance.export`).

Errors: "Please enter a valid Contact ID for GDPR export"; "Contact not found in this workspace" (wrong ID or the contact belongs to another workspace). Owners and admins can export.

*Permanently erase a contact's data (Article 17)*

1. Paste the **Contact ID**.
2. Click **Art. 17 Permanent Erasure**.
3. Read the red warning: this permanently deletes the contact profile, their deals, orders, conversations and all message history. It cannot be undone.
4. Click **Permanently Delete All Personal Data**. A green message reports the result and the audit log gets a `compliance.delete` entry.

Only the **Owner** can do this; admins receive "Forbidden". Export the data first if you need a copy for your records.

**Immutable Security Audit Trail**

A tamper-evident list of important actions in your workspace: who did what, when and from which IP address. It loads the latest 50 entries.

| Control | Details |
|---|---|
| Action filter | All Actions, user.invite, user.role_change, user.status_change, user.remove, apikey.create, apikey.revoke, plan.upgrade, compliance.export, compliance.delete. |
| Refresh | Reloads the list. |

Table columns: **Timestamp**, **Action** (green for create/upgrade, red for delete/revoke/remove, blue for others), **Resource** (type and ID), **Actor** (email or ID, or "System / API"), **IP Address** and **Inspect**. Click **Inspect** to see the full record: actor, timestamp, resource, IP address and a "Payload Details" box with extra information (for example the invited email and role, the API key name, or the plan).

"No security audit records logged yet." appears when nothing has been recorded. Only owners and admins can read it. Other (non-listed) action names may also appear in the list but cannot be selected in the filter; the filter box only offers the ones above.

## 7.8 Common problems in Settings

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| "Forbidden" or an error toast when opening Developer API Keys, Invoices or Audit Trail | Your role is not owner or admin. Ask an owner to do it or to change your role. |
| Cannot change my own role | Owners cannot change their own role; ask another owner. |
| "Cannot demote the last remaining workspace owner" | Promote another person to owner first. |
| Invited person cannot sign in | Check you gave them the correct email and temporary password; check their status is **active**; remind them to change the password on first sign-in. |
| "A user with this email address already exists." | The email is already registered somewhere on the platform. Use another email. |
| Lost an API key secret | Revoke the key and generate a new one. |
| Upgrade completed but plan still shows old name | Reload the page; if it persists check Invoices to see whether the payment was recorded, and contact support with the invoice number. |
| Stripe / Razorpay page did not open | Click **Open Checkout** in the payment step, or allow pop-ups for the site. Then click **Verify Payment and Activate**. |
| Erasure button is disabled | Enter a Contact ID first. |

title: Glossary for this part
content:
# Glossary
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Tenant / workspace | Your organization's private space on the platform. |
| Channel | A connected messaging line, such as a WhatsApp number or web chat. |
| External ID | The identifier of a contact on a channel: a phone number for WhatsApp, a visitor ID for web chat. |
| Tag | A short lower-case label on a contact, used to group audiences. |
| Attribute | An extra named value on a contact (company, price, order ID) that can be inserted in messages as `{{contact.attributes.name}}`. |
| Stage | A column of the deal pipeline. |
| SKU | Your unique code for a product; also used to match WhatsApp catalog orders. |
| SLA | The target time within which you promise to reply (5 minutes here). |
| First Response Time | Time from a customer's first message to the first reply. |
| Webhook | An automatic message sent from the platform to your own web address when an event happens. |
| HMAC signature | A secret-based stamp that lets your system verify a webhook really came from the platform. |
| API key | A secret code that lets your software use the platform without a person logging in. |
| RBAC | Role-based access control: what each role may do. |
| Audit trail | A permanent record of important actions (who, what, when, from where). |
| GDPR Article 15 / 17 | The right of a person to receive a copy of their data / to have it erased. |
